comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 A reward-floor check on the NuminaMath-LEAN training tasks from #11095, before the first Lean RL run. I rebuilt the 4,035 tasks with the recipe's own `row_contract` on main `2bf3f721c`, drew 1,000 at random and compiled fixed replies against each statement in the grader's proof-term form, with the grader image's Lean v4.34.1 and Mathlib `d13f23b`. 795 of the 1,000 were graded in the time I had (the first 300 in order, then a random part of the other 700); the shares weight the two parts by their size.

| Fixed reply | Tasks proved (95% interval) |
|---|---|
| `grind` | 19% (16.5-22%) |
| `first \| (rfl; done) \| (decide; done) \| ... \| (exact?; done)` over 15 tactics | 25% (22-28%) |
| any one of `simp`, `norm_num`, `decide`, `omega`, `linarith`, `exact?`, `aesop`, `trivial`, `rfl` | 17% (14-19%) |

So about 1,000 of the 4,035 tasks give reward 1 to one constant reply. On ProofNet-Verified, `simp`, `simp_all`, `aesop`, `grind`, `tauto`, `ring` and `exact?` proved 49 of 366 rows through the grader (13%, in my #10879 review); those seven prove 24% here. Every task has a compiling human proof, so none is false, but in a random 200, `grind` derives `False` from the hypotheses of 4.

I read 20 of the proved tasks. 16 are faithful but easy: final computations such as `algebra_15505` (`gcd 2835 8960 = 35`), and answers that follow from the stated equations. 4 state less than their problem:

- `algebra_13062` (`fbf349fa`): `h : ∀ x, x ≠ 3 ∧ x ≠ -5 ∧ ...` is false at `x = 3`.
- `algebra_160868` (`ec81e530`): `∀ n, F n = F (n - 1) + F (n - 2)` over ℕ forces `F 0 = 0`, but `F 0 = 1`.
- `algebra_235251` (`f7637b05`): the equation that solves the frog problem is a hypothesis.
- `Number_Theory_640629` (`ed0dad30`): the egg problem became a statement whose inner condition cannot hold, so it is true for every `m`.

Two more have contradictory hypotheses: `algebra_174839` (`c1528388`) and `combinatorics_609372` (`3962696e`, `r = 50`, `b = 50`, `r - b = 5`).

A group in which every sample succeeds has no advantage, so most of these tasks only cost rollouts, and the vacuous ones reward a reply that ignores the problem. Grading the `first | ...` reply once per task at curation takes about 4 s a task in a batch. Would a filter, or a difficulty tag for the curriculum, be useful? I can add either to the recipe.

comments.author: Robertboy18
comments.body:
Thanks Xiaoyuan, this is really useful! Yes please, I think both would help:
- Drop the tasks whose hypotheses already prove `False` (your `grind` check), since any reply gets reward there.
- Tag the rest by whether the fixed `first | ...` reply proves them, so the selection recipe can drop or downweight the easy ones. Small models may still learn from them, so a tag seems better than a hard filter.

The ones that state less than the problem, like `algebra_235251` and `Number_Theory_640629`, won't show up in either check. On #11526 we ran the human problem text through a judge against the Lean for every row, and it caught a lot of these, so I'm happy to run the same thing over the 4,035 and send you the list :)

Your judge list would be great, since neither check sees the statements that say less than their problem; I'm happy to fold it in once you have it.

comments.author: BirgerMoell
comments.body:
Related to steps 2 and 3: we've built an open set of Lean tasks with a verifier built to resist reward exploits. It may be a useful input, especially for the verifier audit and the RL curation.

Lean Arena (Renaissance Labs): https://huggingface.co/datasets/RenaissanceLabsEU/math, with a map of the 63 MSC areas and their Mathlib coverage at https://math.renaissancelabs.eu/

Tasks: 972 tasks in 9 environments (inequalities, group theory, linear algebra, real analysis, finite sums, and more). Each environment has 84 train and 24 eval tasks at three difficulty levels. A model fills in Solution.lean, or writes a definition. The tasks are in Harbor format.
Generated, not scraped: every task comes from a seeded generator, so each row has a seed, a family and a difficulty, and the dataset can't overlap with miniF2F, PutnamBench or Proof-Pile. Fresh seeds give unlimited new tasks.
Verifier: Verify.lean loads the hidden reference and the submission and compares kernel terms. It requires that the task's own definitions are unchanged, that the statement matches exactly, and that the proof uses only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. We also re-check with leanchecker. sorry, native_decide, a user axiom, a changed definition and a weakened statement are all rejected, and tools/verifier_cheats.py tests each of these.
Container check: we ran it with no network on one held-out task per environment. The reference solution scored 1.0 and the untouched start file scored 0.0. Grading takes about 2.5 minutes per task, mostly importing Mathlib several times.

Caveats:

It's on Lean 4.29.1 with Mathlib 5e932f97, not v4.34.1. The generators don't depend on the version, but moving would mean regenerating and re-running the self-tests.
We have no model baseline yet. One automation tactic closes 15 of 192 sampled proving tasks, which is a floor for how much needs no real proof, not a model score.
The eval split is in distribution (same templates, different seeds). It's good for RL practice, but it's not a general theorem-proving benchmark and shouldn't replace miniF2F or PutnamBench.

We can discuss this more in the math channel.

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
Marin cannot serve or evaluate `reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B` because the locked `transformers` 5.12.1 cannot load its tokenizer. Marin loads the tokenizer in its own environment in two places: `read_tool_chat_template` (`lib/marin/src/marin/inference/model_preparation.py`), called when vLLM starts, and the evaluation task worker (`lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/task_worker.py:210`). `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` reads the model config first. `transformers` 5.12.1 does not register model type `beam`, and its fallback config fails RoPE validation on Beam's `rope_parameters`, which sets `full_attention` to `null`:

```
File ".../transformers/models/auto/tokenization_auto.py", line 720, in from_pretrained
File ".../transformers/configuration_utils.py", line 844, in from_dict
File ".../transformers/modeling_rope_utils.py", line 795, in validate_rope
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'
```

vLLM itself serves Beam: upstream vLLM 0.34.0 registers `BeamForCausalLM` and its own `BeamConfig`. This blocks Beam 1.0 as a Tier 3 comparison model for the Nov 30 eval policy.

Reproduce:
1. `uv run python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B', revision='877a5d6973c6ae6a55335483002c06717662d23c')"` in a Marin checkout fails as above.
2. The same call succeeds with `transformers` 5.16.1 and 5.22.0.

Expected: Marin loads Beam's tokenizer, so Beam can be served and evaluated.

Upgrading the lock is blocked: `transformers` 5.16.1 requires `safetensors>=0.8.0`, while `lib/levanter/pyproject.toml` pins `safetensors[numpy]>=0.4.2,<0.7.0`. Beam's `tokenizer_config.json` names its tokenizer class (`TokenizersBackend`), so a tokenizer load that does not read the model config would also avoid the error.

Part of #12156. cc @yonromai @dlwh @rjpower

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Research**

`transformers` 5.12.1 reads `config.json` before `tokenizer_config.json` in `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained`. Beam's unregistered `beam` model type reaches fallback RoPE validation and fails before its declared `TokenizersBackend` can load. Both serving and evaluation use Levanter's shared tokenizer loader.

**Relevant code**
- [`hf_checkpoints.py#L1518`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/hf_checkpoints.py#L1518) — shared AutoTokenizer call
- [`model_preparation.py#L88`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/model_preparation.py#L88) — serving template probe
- [`task_worker.py#L207`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/task_worker.py#L207) — evaluation tokenizer load

**Proposed Fix**

When `tokenizer_config.json` explicitly declares `TokenizersBackend`, load that class through the shared loader before asking `AutoTokenizer` to parse the model config. Keep `AutoTokenizer` for other tokenizer classes. Add a local regression fixture with Beam's unsupported config shape and verify tokenization and special tokens.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body: 🤖 [PR #12224](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12224) applies the shared tokenizer-loader fix. A Beam-shaped offline reproduction fails before the change; the tokenizer and export cases pass afterward (4 passed). Formatting and Pyrefly pass. The broad local selection reached its 600-second limit after 485 passes and one synthetic-Hub fixture failure, which the follow-up commit fixed and reran successfully.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
**A higher-priority multi-host job cannot get capacity when a reservation is fully held by smaller, lower-priority slices.** Preemption only replaces one existing slice of the same size or larger. The autoscaler never scales down busy lower-priority slices to make room. So the job waits indefinitely, whatever its priority.

## Example (2026-11-17, reserved v4 pool, us-central2-b)

- **Demand:** a production-band (band 1) coscheduled job needing a v4-1024 slice (512 chips, 128 hosts), submitted 17:13Z.
  - Its scale group created a queued resource at 17:16:21Z. That resource was still `WAITING_FOR_RESOURCES` in GCP at 18:45Z.
  - All 128 tasks were pending with "No workers match constraints".
- **Supply:** the reservation's 1,024 chips were all in READY slices, every one running tasks. No slice was idle.

| Slice size | Ready slices | Chips | Bands of running tasks |
|---|---|---|---|
| v4-8 | 96 | 384 | batch (95), interactive (1) |
| v4-32 | 4 | 64 | batch, interactive |
| v4-64 | 4 | 128 | batch, interactive |
| v4-128 | 1 | 64 | batch |
| v4-256 | 1 | 128 | batch, interactive |
| v4-512 | 1 | 256 | batch |

- Every running task was in a lower band than the waiting job, yet nothing could be evicted for it.
- Removing about 512 chips of the smaller slices (for example most v4-8 slices plus the v4-128 and v4-256) would have let GCP create the v4-1024 slice.

## Why, in the code (main at f5d3c85f9e)

- **[`_preempt_coscheduled`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f5d3c85f9e4914a48994d9a29f8c3e9104de84e0/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/scheduling/policy.py#L456-L502)** evicts **one** victim slice. That slice must have the same `device_variant` as the preemptor, strictly lower band on every member, and at least `n_required` members. Smaller slices of another variant never qualify, and several slices are never combined.
- **[`run_preemption_pass`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f5d3c85f9e4914a48994d9a29f8c3e9104de84e0/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/scheduling/policy.py#L614-L637)** documents the same rule: a coscheduled preemptor evicts an entire slice "of the same device-variant and at least the preemptor's task count".
- **[`_preempt_coscheduled_partial_hosts`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f5d3c85f9e4914a48994d9a29f8c3e9104de84e0/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/scheduling/policy.py#L550-L565)** frees hosts by evicting solo co-tenants, but only on hosts of the gang's own variant, so it needs those workers to exist first.
- **Autoscaler scale-down is idle-based only** ([`scaling_group.py` idle threshold](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f5d3c85f9e4914a48994d9a29f8c3e9104de84e0/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/autoscaler/scaling_group.py#L125-L135)).
  - Routing orders groups by the group's config priority ([`route_demand`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f5d3c85f9e4914a48994d9a29f8c3e9104de84e0/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/autoscaler/routing.py#L715-L725)), not by the priority band of the demand.
  - Nothing releases busy lower-band slices to free reservation quota for higher-band demand that a group cannot satisfy.

The rule is deliberate: "same-variant + slice-shaped" avoids large/small thrashing. But inside a fixed reservation, it means priority cannot reclaim capacity that has been fragmented into smaller slices.

## Proposed direction

When a higher-band demand stays unmet because its group cannot get capacity in a reservation, the autoscaler should drain lower-band slices in the **same reservation** until enough chips are free for the requested slice:
- Preempt their tasks through the normal preemption path, then delete the slices.
- Prefer the lowest band, then the youngest tasks.
- Gate it on the demand having been unmet for a minimum time, and stop as soon as the chips are free, to limit thrashing.
- Record each drain (preemptor, victims, chips freed) so it can be audited.

---

```markdown
  - Routing orders groups by the group's config priority ([`route_demand`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f5d3c85f9e4914a48994d9a29f8c3e9104de84e0/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/autoscaler/routing.py#L715-L725)), not by the priority band of the demand.
  - Nothing releases busy lower-band slices to free reservation quota for higher-band demand that a group cannot satisfy.

The rule is deliberate: "same-variant + slice-shaped" avoids large/small thrashing. But inside a fixed reservation, it means priority cannot reclaim capacity that has been fragmented into smaller slices.

## Proposed direction

When a higher-band demand stays unmet because its group cannot get capacity in a reservation, the autoscaler should drain lower-band slices in the **same reservation** until enough chips are free for the requested slice:
- Preempt their tasks through the normal preemption path, then delete the slices.
- Prefer the lowest band, then the youngest tasks.
- Gate it on the demand having been unmet for a minimum time, and stop as soon as the chips are free, to limit thrashing.
- Record each drain (preemptor, victims, chips freed) so it can be audited.

```

</details>

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The current preemption pass binds a coscheduled preemptor to workers freed by one same-variant slice, so it cannot combine smaller v4 slices into a new v4-1024 allocation. The autoscaler routes by scale-group priority, does not carry the pending job's band in `DemandEntry`, and scales down only idle slices; `quota_pool` groups quota failures but has no shared chip ledger. [#6818](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6818) and [#6819](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6819) developed the ledger, drain lifecycle, and cross-variant pass, then closed unmerged after inactivity. I found no open PR for this issue or mechanism.

**Relevant code**
- [`policy.py#L460-L503`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/scheduling/policy.py#L460-L503) — one same-variant victim slice
- [`models.py#L29-L39`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/autoscaler/models.py#L29-L39) — demand lacks priority band
- [`routing.py#L710-L756`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/autoscaler/routing.py#L710-L756) — group-priority routing
- [`scaling_group.py#L647-L671`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/autoscaler/scaling_group.py#L647-L671) — detach before cloud deletion
- [`controller.py#L1021-L1072`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/controller.py#L1021-L1072) — schedule and autoscale tick ordering

# Proposed design

A production v4-1024 demand should reclaim enough chips from lower-band slices in its own reserved pool, then wait for a new v4-1024 slice to become ready. This crosses scheduling, autoscaling, slice persistence, and cloud deletion, so I would split it into reviewable stages:

1. **Pool accounting and safe drain lifecycle.** Add an explicit physical chip budget to each reserved `quota_pool` (1,024 chips for the reported `v4-reserved/us-central2-b` pool), validate that all member groups agree, and derive a per-tick ledger of live, capacity-backed creating, and draining chips. Track `WAITING_FOR_RESOURCES` requests separately because they have not acquired chips. Keep a slice tracked as `DRAINING` until cloud deletion is confirmed; make drain idempotent and retry a stuck deletion. The autoscaler must count draining chips as unavailable for new allocations and cap launches across *all* sizes in the pool. Adapt the useful parts of #6818 to the current controller.
2. **Band-aware demand and cross-size drain.** Carry the requested priority band into `DemandEntry` and admit pool launches in band order. On an autoscale tick, when a reserved-pool demand has waited at least a configurable grace period and no ready or capacity-backed creating slice of the requested shape can satisfy it, calculate the chip deficit. A queued GCP resource still `WAITING_FOR_RESOURCES` must remain eligible for a drain; reuse that request after capacity is freed. Select physical victim slices in the same pool whose *every* occupant is strictly lower band, preferring the lowest band and then youngest tasks. Skip victims with a coscheduled job spanning several slices unless its whole gang can be handled. Evict nothing unless eligible victims cover the full deficit; stop selecting as soon as they do. Commit task preemption and slice drain together on the same tick, then launch or unblock the requested shape only after GCP releases the chips. Adapt #6819's physical-slice grouping and schedule-only-tick guard; include an audit record with preemptor, victims, pool, and chips freed.
3. **Regression and rollout gates.** Use a 1,024-chip mixed-size fixture matching this issue to prove that one production v4-1024 demand reclaims exactly enough lower-band chips and eventually receives its slice. Cover equal/higher-band occupants, another pool or zone, insufficient eligible chips, a queued replacement blocked on capacity, a replacement already backed by capacity, repeated ticks, failed deletion, and a schedule-only tick. Run the Iris unit suite and repository lint/review gates, then verify on a dev controller before enabling the policy on the reserved v4 pool. No live drain or controller restart is part of this triage.

The main risk is evicting work while GCP still cannot create the replacement slice. The ledger and deletion confirmation prevent double-spending chips; the grace period and in-flight check limit repeated churn. Before enabling this for the production pool, confirm that the configured `quota_pool` maps to one fungible GCP reservation and that its physical budget is 1,024 chips.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 **Design for a fix (for review before code).**

## Prior work checked

- **Issue 6217** ("Higher Queues Should Preempt Across Node Types for Reserved Compute", closed as stale on 2026-08-29) asked for the same thing. Its research comment proposed relaxing the scheduler's same-variant gate on reserved capacity and left three questions open:
  1. What is a "reserved pool"?
  2. How do we stay thrash-safe?
  3. Which bands may cross?

  This design answers all three.
- Echo searches on reservation, priority and drain found no other decision. `lib/iris` docs have nothing on this.
- The config already has the pool key: every size of a `tpu_pools` entry gets `quota_pool = "<pool>/<zone>"` (`config.py:1509`), for example `v4-reserved/us-central2-b`. Groups with `capacity_type: reserved` and the same `quota_pool` draw on one reservation.

## Which component acts: the autoscaler, with the controller doing the preemption

Relaxing the scheduler gate alone does not work:
- The preemptor cannot land this tick. A v4-1024 needs a new slice, not freed v4-8 workers.
- The preempted batch tasks go back to PENDING and are re-placed on the freed workers of their own slices on the next tick, because those slices are still READY and their groups still have demand. Nothing is returned to the reservation.

The capacity owner must remove the slices. The autoscaler is the only component that knows all four facts that matter:
- the pool,
- that the preemptor's group has a slice waiting on the cloud and for how long,
- each slice's chip count,
- which slices are READY.

**Change:**
1. **`DemandEntry` gains `priority_band`.** The residual-demand builder in `scheduling/policy.py` already reads the job row.
2. **`WorkerStatus` gains `max_running_band`,** the highest band of the tasks running on that worker (none when idle). The controller already builds `WorkerStatusMap` from running tasks.
3. **New pure function `plan_reservation_reclaim(groups, demand, worker_status, now)`** in a new `autoscaler/reclaim.py`. It returns `ReclaimDecision(preemptor_job, pool, victim_slices, chips_needed, chips_freed)`.
4. **`AutoscaleResult` gains `reclaim: list[ReclaimDecision]`.** The controller folds each decision in one transaction:
   - Mark every task on the victim workers PREEMPTED, with the reason `reservation reclaim for <job> in <pool>`, through the existing preemption transition. This counts against the victim's preemption-retry budget, the same as ordinary preemption.
   - Fence those workers, then call the existing `remove_capacity`. The slices are deleted, so their chips go back to the reservation, and the cloud then fulfils the preemptor's waiting queued resource.

## Trigger (all must hold)

- **Reserved demand:** a coscheduled demand entry of band B is routed to a group with `capacity_type: reserved`.
- **Waiting on the cloud:** that group has a slice that is not READY because it is waiting on the cloud (BOOTING or REQUESTING for the queued resource).
- **Unmet long enough:** that slice has existed for at least `reclaim_min_wait`, default 10 min. A short wait usually means normal provisioning, not a full reservation.
- **No recent reclaim:** no reclaim for this pool within the last `reclaim_cooldown`, default 30 min, unless the earlier reclaimed slice has since become READY. If the cloud still cannot place after a drain (for example, the reservation is also used outside Iris), Iris does not keep killing jobs.

## Victim choice

- **Candidates:** READY slices in other groups (any size) with the same `quota_pool` and `capacity_type: reserved`.
  - Every worker of a candidate is idle or runs only bands strictly lower than B. **Equal or higher bands are never touched.**
  - A slice with even one equal-or-higher task is skipped whole.
- **Order:**
  1. Idle slices first. They cost nothing; scale-down would have taken them after the idle threshold anyway.
  2. Then the lowest band first (batch before interactive).
  3. Then fewest chips first.
  4. Then the youngest slice, so the least work is lost.
- **Stop** as soon as the freed chips reach `chips_needed`, the chip count of the waiting slice.
- **All or nothing:** if the candidates cannot reach `chips_needed`, drain nothing and record `reclaim_blocked` with the shortfall.
- **One preemptor per pool per tick:** the highest band first, then the oldest.

**Limit:** Iris does not know how many chips are free in the reservation; GCP only reports the queued resource as waiting. So `chips_needed` assumes none are free. That may drain somewhat more than strictly needed, never less. A follow-up could add an optional per-pool `reserved_chips` budget to the config and subtract live usage.

## Recording

- Every reclaim is written to the autoscaler action log (`_log_action("reservation_reclaim", ...)`), as scale-ups and scale-downs are today. The entry carries:
  - the preemptor job and its band,
  - the pool,
  - each victim slice with its chips and its jobs' bands,
  - `chips_needed` and `chips_freed`.
- `reclaim_blocked` is recorded the same way.
- Victim tasks get the preemption reason above, so `iris job` views show why they stopped.

## Tests (existing fakes; no cluster)

All pure-function tests of `plan_reservation_reclaim`, plus one controller fold test:
1. Today's case: a reserved pool full of batch v4-8, v4-32, v4-64, v4-128, v4-256 and v4-512 slices, and a production v4-1024 waiting past `reclaim_min_wait`.
   - Expect idle slices, then the smallest batch slices, until 512 chips are freed.
   - Expect no interactive slice to be drained while batch slices suffice.
2. Equal-band victims are never chosen, and a slice with one equal-band task is skipped whole.
3. Below `reclaim_min_wait`, or inside the cooldown: no reclaim.
4. Not enough lower-band chips: no drain, and `reclaim_blocked` is recorded.
5. A preemptible or on-demand pool, or a different `quota_pool`: never reclaimed from.
6. Controller fold:
   - victim tasks go to PREEMPTED with the reason, and their workers are fenced and passed to `remove_capacity`;
   - the victim jobs' preemption-retry counts go up by one;
   - the preemptor is not placed in the same tick.

## Not in scope

- Solo (non-coscheduled) preemptors.
- Preemptible pools, where freeing chips gives no guarantee.
- Any change to deployment or a live cluster.

The settings live in the autoscaler config: `reservation_reclaim.enabled` (proposed default: on), `min_wait` (10 min) and `cooldown` (30 min). Operators can tune reclaim, or turn it off, per cluster.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Draft fix: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11617. It follows the design above, with two changes:
- **Off by default:** reclaim runs only for pools listed in `defaults.autoscaler.reservation_reclaim.quota_pools`.
- **Tasks fail through the worker-failure path:** a victim's tasks become `WORKER_FAILED` on their preemption budget, through the existing `_remove_worker_capacity` path, not `PREEMPTED`.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 **GB200 instance on cw-us-east-08a (2026-11-25): the blocked production gang is unplaceable per-pod — and Kueue preemption there is not same-shape-gated**

Context: four PRODUCTION micro210 eval rows (16-task coscheduled gangs each) sat `SchedulingGated` for hours on 08a while other users' single-host batch jobs held most of the fleet — the same symptom as this issue. I probed whether exact-shape requests force preemption on GB200.

**What the rows request** (Kueue workload `iris-pg-7e723fbd5c35df5d-0`, identical across the four): one podset of 16 pods × `nvidia.com/gpu: 8` + `rdma/ib: 8`, 32 CPU / 512Gi each, topologyRequest `preferred: backend.coreweave.cloud/leafgroup`, workload priority 1000 (production). The Iris job requests GPU variant H100: `res_device_json = {"gpu": {"variant": "H100", "count": 8}}`.

**Fleet at observation:** 204 ready nodes × 4 GB200 GPUs = 816 allocatable; ClusterQueue `iris-cq` (cw-tas flavor) usage 816/864 → 48 free GPU/RDMA quota, 0 free physical GPUs.

**Two successive pending reasons on the same workload:**

1. While quota was scarce: `couldn't assign flavors to pod set 36189f9a: ... insufficient unused quota for nvidia.com/gpu in flavor cw-tas, 80 more needed, ... rdma/ib ... 80 more needed` (128 requested − 48 free).
2. After later preemptions freed quota to 212 GPUs: `topology "multinode-nvlink-ib" doesn't allow to fit any of 16 pod(s). Total nodes: 205; excluded: resource "cpu": 65, resource "memory": 48, resource "nvidia.com/gpu": 92` — no node on 08a has more than 4 GPUs, so an 8-GPU pod fits nowhere. The H100-variant, 8-GPU-per-task shape is unplaceable on this fleet regardless of preemption.

**Probe matrix** (all PRODUCTION priority, 2-minute sleep jobs, `/benfeuer/gb200-preempt-probe-*`, UTC 2026-11-25; each cancelled or finished within ~2 min):

| probe | shape | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a1 | 1 task × 4 GB200, no coscheduling (the batch shape) | Placed via preemption: a batch 4-GPU pod was evicted at 10:23:30Z (`WorkloadEvictedDueToPreempted`, preemptor = the a1 pod), pod initializing 10:23:44Z, running ~10:23:47Z — ~30 s submit→running; victim requeued. |
| b1 | exact row shape: 16 × 8 GPU (H100), coscheduled leafgroup-preferred | Never placed in 7 min: reason 1, then after quota freed, reason 2. Reproduces the rows exactly. |
| c1 | 16 × 4 GB200, coscheduled hard `nvlink.domain` (one rack) | Placed via preemption: an interactive 32-pod gang (128 GB200) was atomically evicted at 10:31:16Z to free a 16-node rack; all 16 pods RUNNING in one nvlink.domain by 10:32:45Z (~2 min); victim gang requeued. |
| c3 | 32 × 4 GB200, coscheduled `nvlink.domain.sliced` (2 × 16-node slices) | Placed ~100 s with no further preemption: 16+16 pods on nvlink.domains DH1-124 and DH1-128. |

Only lower-band (batch/interactive) workloads were preempted, all with retry budgets intact.

**Code:** the same-shape rule this issue documents — `_preempt_coscheduled` evicts one victim slice of the same device variant with ≥ n_required members, every member strictly lower band (`lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/scheduling/policy.py:456-502`, gates at lines 473-495; documented in `run_preemption_pass`, lines 630-634) — governs Iris worker-fleet backends. On CoreWeave it never runs: `K8sTaskProvider.schedule` is a no-op ("Kueue owns placement, so Iris makes no scheduling decisions", `lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py:2678-2680`), and Kueue v0.18.3 admits/preempts with ClusterQueue `preemption: {withinClusterQueue: LowerPriority}` (`lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/kueue_manifests.py:409`) plus topology-aware scheduling.

**What the GB200 instance shows:**

- Production preemption on GB200/Kueue is not same-shape-gated the way the TPU instance is: production preempted single-host batch for a solo request, and evicted an entire 128-GPU interactive gang to assemble a 16-node rack for a 64-GPU request.
- Victim eviction is gang-atomic, so fragmentation surfaces as over-eviction (64 requested → 128 evicted) rather than as refusal.
- The four rows are blocked only by their per-pod shape. A relaunch at 4 GPUs/task, variant GB200 places: 16 × 4 = 64 GPUs hard-bound to one rack (`nvlink.domain`), or 32 × 4 = 128 GPUs split 2 × 16 across two racks (`nvlink.domain.sliced`) — same total compute as the current rows.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 **Separate finding: victim selection when production preempts for a whole rack (GB200, cw-us-east-08a)**

This is distinct from this issue's shape-awareness gap, which concerns which request shapes can preempt. This one concerns **which band gets evicted** once a placement needs a whole rack.

**Verified**
- At 10:31:16Z on 2026-11-25, probe `/benfeuer/gb200-preempt-probe-c1` ran at production as 16 × 4 GB200, coscheduled with a hard `nvlink.domain` constraint (one rack). Kueue evicted an **interactive** 32-pod gang (128 GB200) to admit it (`WorkloadEvictedDueToPreempted`, preemptor and preemptee path `/iris-cq`). All 16 probe pods were running in one NVLink domain by 10:32:45Z.
- The evicted job ended `worker_failed` with `preemptions=1`, `cosched_failed=31` and `preempted=1`. Its owner later resubmitted it as a resume.
- At the same time, roughly 230 single-node **batch** jobs (4 GB200 each) were running on 08a.
- Our ClusterQueue uses `preemption: {withinClusterQueue: LowerPriority}` (`lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/kueue_manifests.py:409`). Batch and interactive are therefore equally eligible victims for a production preemptor. No setting prefers the lowest band.
- Eviction is gang-atomic: a 64-GPU request cost 128 GPUs of eviction.

**Inferred, not yet verified**
- The batch pods were spread one per node across many racks, interleaved with other non-evictable work, so no single rack could be freed by evicting batch alone. The interactive gang occupied whole racks, so evicting it was the only one-step way to free a full rack.
- A per-rack occupancy snapshot at 10:31Z would confirm or refute this. I didn't capture one.

**Consequence**

Any rack-shaped production job on 08a can evict another user's interactive gang even while batch capacity is available elsewhere. That covers multi-node RL, rack-bound eval serving, and placement probes. The probe here was ours, and our probes now run at batch or interactive only. That doesn't protect against legitimate rack-shaped production jobs.

**Possible directions (policy call for Iris/Kueue owners)**
- A Kueue preemption or fair-sharing policy that exhausts lower-band candidates before higher ones, with rack-aware candidate selection.
- Requiring production rack requests to fail over to `nvlink.domain.sliced` before evicting interactive gangs.
- Surfacing the expected victim set before admission, so the submitter can choose.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Atlas ingest must resolve permission before conversion, census, oracle execution or QA. Missing, restricted and unrecognized terms block new ingestion and admission unless a human or coordinator records an explicit, revision-scoped exception. This issue records blocked sources and their evidence; absence of a grant is not permission.

The canonical policy reuses Marin Data Belay's Blue Oak Council v16 permissive SPDX list, CC BY/CC BY-SA and ODC-By additions, and OpenMDW pattern ([existing policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/data_belay/intake.py)). NC and ND terms are rejected; custom and unknown terms require review. The deterministic stage-0 checker evaluates only the pinned dataset’s own card, LICENSE files and README license statements: PASS permits ingestion, FAIL stops it, and ESCALATE goes to the user. Underlying OSS repository licenses and generated outputs alone are not ban grounds. Resolver hints do not override a permissive dataset grant; unidentified separate terms are escalated, without tracing teachers or upstream lineage.

| Source and scope | Verdict | Decision date | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym apps and task data at `dc279a3735f0d59f9b9b9806f1fc8cd99c28e6f9` | MISSING: no license grant found | 2026-11-15 | Blocked pending explicit permission | [Repository at pin](https://github.com/Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym/tree/dc279a3735f0d59f9b9b9806f1fc8cd99c28e6f9); [GitHub API](https://api.github.com/repos/Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym) reports `"license": null`; [prior investigation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10231#issuecomment-6231071121) |
| OpenGCUA trajectories (separate from harness code) | MISSING: no trajectory-specific grant established | 2026-11-15 | Blocked pending trajectory permission | [Trajectory publisher](https://tongyi-mai.github.io/OpenGCUA/trajectories.html); [code at pin](https://github.com/Tongyi-MAI/OpenGCUA/tree/55c33aea792b48b9c1330a514bfcc8f6d3ecc704); [prior license investigation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10231) |

Evidence excerpts: the MAI-Gym investigation records “its repository has no license”. OpenGCUA's trajectory publisher describes “eight frontier models”; its Apache-2.0 link points to the code repository. The prior investigation reports unlicensed trajectories, mostly closed-model outputs. That output-provenance claim is not a model-by-model permission audit. The code's Apache-2.0 grant does not establish permission for separately hosted trajectories. No text exists to quote as a missing license grant.

Registry procedure:
- Record each reviewed source's exact revision and data scope, verdict, primary evidence URLs, short quoted clauses, decision date and status.
- A ban or exception must name the decision-maker, timestamp, exact source and revision, permitted use, evidence and rationale, and link back to this issue. Permission for one revision or code artifact does not silently extend to another dataset.
- Review backfill findings before adding them as bans or changing existing admissions. An unresolved audit row is not a retroactive admission decision. The script never applies an admission or ban diff: the user approves it. Active source bans remain binding until a recorded user lift.

Done when:
- [ ] Every current Atlas source has a primary-evidence license receipt or an explicit unresolved audit row.
- [ ] New ingestion and admission fail before other ingest stages without permission or an explicit exception.
- [ ] Reviewed blocked sources and subsequent permission changes remain recorded here with evidence.

comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Atlas currently carries license labels in source tags, but `SourceDeclaration` has no permission receipt. The driver selects a source and constructs conversion steps before the catalog's admission check, so that check cannot enforce permission before ingest. Draft PR #11277 owns this Atlas code; no open PR references #11497.

**Relevant code**
- [`intake.py#L25-L76`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7cc62606154b50b95fb24b2bbede1e23dc8219b9/experiments/data_belay/intake.py#L25-L76) — existing license classifier.
- [`source.py#L116-L145`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9fecbbf0b4c976bb48c66ae0a2ff28792af8304d/experiments/post_training/task_curation/source.py#L116-L145) — source metadata and tags.
- [`sources.py#L74-L149`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9fecbbf0b4c976bb48c66ae0a2ff28792af8304d/experiments/post_training/task_curation/sources.py#L74-L149) — source inventory and receipt binding.
- [`driver.py#L105-L174`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9fecbbf0b4c976bb48c66ae0a2ff28792af8304d/experiments/post_training/task_curation/driver.py#L105-L174) — selection and conversion construction.
- [`admission.py#L41-L55`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9fecbbf0b4c976bb48c66ae0a2ff28792af8304d/infra/marina/apps/rl_data_catalog/server/admission.py#L41-L55) — current catalog admission check.

# Proposed Fix

1. Add a typed, reviewed permission receipt keyed to upstream source identity, exact revision, data scope, and intended use. Record verdict, decision date, reviewer, primary evidence URLs and short clauses. Reuse Data Belay's Blue Oak v16, CC BY/CC BY-SA, ODC-By, and OpenMDW classification; reject NC/ND and send custom or unknown terms to review. Keep human policy records in Git, as Atlas does for other reviewed decisions.
2. Inventory every current `all_sources()` entry at its pinned revision. Add either a primary-evidence receipt or an explicit unresolved audit row before enabling the gate for existing sources. Preserve the MAI-Gym apps/tasks and OpenGCUA trajectories in this issue as separate blocked scopes; the OpenGCUA code license does not cover trajectories. Record bundled third-party content and model-generated output decisions separately. An exception must bind approver, timestamp, exact source/revision/scope, permitted use, evidence, rationale, and this issue.
3. Check the receipt after source selection and before any conversion step, download, census, oracle run, or QA. Apply the same check to other ingest entry points and to catalog publication/loading, so a direct call cannot bypass it. Missing, rejected, stale, or mismatched receipts fail with the source and scope; a license tag alone grants nothing.
4. Test allowed, missing, NC/ND, unknown, changed-revision, third-party/output, and exact-exception cases, including that a blocked source starts no ingest work. Run the package tests and repository lint review. Implement against #11277 or its merged successor, then open the change PR with `Fixes #11497` after the full inventory is reviewed.

The automated checker escalated the custom June 9 Researcher Reciprocity License v1.0 as **E1**. The user decided: “Ban kernelbot for now I don't want us to have to write a custom license just for them.”

issues.author: hammer
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Iris cannot put users in groups or grant priority bands by group membership. Band access is set one user at a time in each cluster's YAML, and on the GCP hubs every IAP user is an admin who can submit PRODUCTION. This issue proposes three things: named groups in Iris, a band policy keyed on groups, and moving the hubs off `unprovisioned_role: admin`. It builds on the group design in #10131.

## Background

- **Tiers are unnamed user lists.** At controller start, `reconcile_user_budget_tiers` ([budget.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/0849c20336f2399464f4dc7edbaec9a7e5400851/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/budget.py#L121-L160)) turns each `user_budgets` tier into one row per user, each with a `budget_limit` and a `max_band`. The tier itself is not kept, and `UserBudgetTier` has no name field. "Admins" and "researchers" exist only as comments in [marin.yaml](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/263527428c8352ce5abeba806e410cad484ba07d/lib/iris/config/marin.yaml#L328-L361).
- **`max_band` governs only INTERACTIVE and BATCH.** SYSTEM and PRODUCTION need `MANAGE_BUDGETS`, which only admins hold ([jobs.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/0849c20336f2399464f4dc7edbaec9a7e5400851/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/jobs.py#L601-L640)). A tier with `max_band: PRODUCTION` therefore grants nothing to a non-admin.
- **Roles match exact identities.** `RolePolicy` checks `user_roles`, then `admin_users`, then the provider default ([auth.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/0849c20336f2399464f4dc7edbaec9a7e5400851/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/auth.py#L451-L490)). There is no group lookup.
- **The PRODUCTION gate is open on the hubs.** [marin.yaml](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/263527428c8352ce5abeba806e410cad484ba07d/lib/iris/config/marin.yaml#L129) and [marin-dev.yaml](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/263527428c8352ce5abeba806e410cad484ba07d/lib/iris/config/marin-dev.yaml#L61) both set `unprovisioned_role: admin`, so every IAP-admitted user is an admin (#10182). Anyone not demoted through `user_roles` can submit PRODUCTION, and the admin tier in marin.yaml restricts nothing. #7194 and #7195 tried to close this gap; both lapsed.
- **Access changes are made per person.** #6010, #9846, #11192 and #11602 each needed a config PR and a controller restart.
- **Group-like rules exist only outside the band check.** `allowed_submitters` accepts `*@domain` for federation admission, and the IAP grants in Pulumi include whole domains. Neither one decides which band a user gets.
- **Prior proposals.**
  - On #9846, Russell suggested making group membership an Iris primitive ([comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9846#issuecomment-6177872543)).
  - #10131 designs named groups: `iris_access_groups.yaml`, `auth.group_directory`, and `group:<name>` references in roles, budget tiers and admission ([design](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10131#issuecomment-6179434813)). It is aimed at privacy and less repetition, and it does not address PRODUCTION.
  - #10950, the OpenFGA pilot, tested nested groups for Iris RPC and sandbox access. It does not cover bands.

## Proposed work

1. **Named groups.** Implement the #10131 design, with `group:<name>` accepted in `user_roles`, `admin_users`, `user_budgets` tiers and `allowed_submitters`, and resolved at controller start. Keep the design compatible with #10950, so OpenFGA can later serve as the source of membership.
2. **A band policy keyed on groups.**
   - Add a per-cluster policy mapping each group to the bands it may submit to, e.g. `band_access: [{group: group:prod-runners, max_band: PRODUCTION}]`.
   - Make PRODUCTION reachable through this policy without the admin role, so "may run PRODUCTION" no longer means "may manage the cluster".
   - Deny by default. A user in no group gets the cluster's default band. A user in several groups gets the highest band among them.
   - Keep a clear PERMISSION_DENIED message that names the group needed.
3. **Close the hub gap.** Once item 2 can express today's access, change `unprovisioned_role` on marin and marin-dev from `admin` to `user`. Move the current admins into an admin group and the current PRODUCTION users into a PRODUCTION group.
4. **Visibility.**
   - Add `iris group list/show` and show each user's effective band and source group in `iris user budget get` and on the dashboard.
   - Extend the #10131 audit command to report bands.
5. **Docs.** Update `lib/iris/docs/priority-bands.md` to say how to add a person to a group and how band access is decided.

## Done when

- [ ] `group:<name>` references resolve in roles, budget tiers and admission, with tests for unknown groups, empty groups and conflicting rules.
- [ ] A cluster config can grant PRODUCTION to a non-admin group and deny it to everyone else, with a test for each case.
- [ ] marin and marin-dev no longer set `unprovisioned_role: admin`, and the access each current user had before the switch is verified after it.
- [ ] `iris` CLI and dashboard show each user's effective band and the group it comes from.
- [ ] Adding a person to a group takes one membership change, not one edit per cluster file.

Related: #10131, #9846, #10950, #10182, #7194, #7195, #6592, #6338, #11602, #4096.

On current `main`, roles match individual identities, budget tiers become persistent per-user rows, and the job gate requires `MANAGE_BUDGETS` for PRODUCTION. This makes a non-admin `max_band: PRODUCTION` ineffective and leaves old budget assignments after a person is removed from a tier. [#10131](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10131#issuecomment-6179434813) has the group design but no implementation PR; the open [#10950](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10950) pilot does not implement this band policy.

**Relevant code**
- [`auth.py#L458-L500`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/263527428c8352ce5abeba806e410cad484ba07d/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/auth.py#L458-L500) — role lookup.
- [`budget.py#L130-L166`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/263527428c8352ce5abeba806e410cad484ba07d/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/budget.py#L130-L166) — tier reconciliation.
- [`jobs.py#L605-L627`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/263527428c8352ce5abeba806e410cad484ba07d/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/jobs.py#L605-L627) — band gate.

# Proposed Fix

1. Implement #10131's group resolution across roles, budget tiers, and admission. Validate unknown, empty, and conflicting groups before a controller starts.
2. Add the issue's per-cluster group band policy. Compute the highest permitted band across memberships, use the cluster default for no match, authorize PRODUCTION using the authenticated root submitter, and leave SYSTEM admin-only. Carry the root decision through child jobs and federation.
3. Separate band policy from persisted budget spending. Reconciliation must revoke stale group-derived tier assignments while preserving explicit budget overrides. Expose the effective band and source group through the RPC, CLI, dashboard, and audit command.
4. Apply the hub config change described above only after a before-and-after access comparison. Update the priority-band docs.

Test non-admin PRODUCTION admission, ungrouped and SYSTEM denial, overlapping groups, membership removal, child inheritance, and federation. Use `Part of #12273` for foundation PRs and `Fixes #12273` when the final migration satisfies the issue's done criteria.

## Open question

Should group membership be visible to every authenticated user? I propose operator-only group listings and self-service effective-band lookup.

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
Graders that execute a model's program run it in the grader's own sandbox, as the grader's user, with the verifier's files readable. On the local eval backend the grader is root without capabilities, so it cannot switch the candidate to another user either. A candidate can therefore read hidden answers, replace the checker, or tamper with the grading process, and score without solving the task.

Each grader is hardening itself separately:

- #11990 / #11992: the RL LiveCodeBench scorer ran the program in the process that computed the reward; the fix compares outputs in the parent.
- #12207: the Lean grader deletes `/tests` files, kills the candidate's processes and checks toolchain files when it is not root. Review keeps finding escapes from the same user, most recently writing the grader's memory through `/proc/<pid>/mem` and hiding a process behind a non-UTF-8 name.
- The curated LiveCodeBench grader (`experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/livecodebench_grade.py`) runs Python submissions with `/tests/tests.json.zlib` readable, and the LiveCodeBench Pro grader runs compiled C++ with the test archive and checker in reach (the candidate can overwrite the checker binary). No graded program in the LiveCodeBench Pro full runs (1,356 replies) touched files, so their scores are unaffected.

A program running as the grader's user in the grader's sandbox can always reach the grader, so per-grader hardening does not converge. The runtime could instead offer graders a way to run a candidate program in its own sandbox that holds only the candidate's inputs, with CPU, wall-time and memory limits, and return its exit status, output and resource use; verifier-role files never enter it. #11998 (nested bubblewrap in Kubernetes tasks) may provide the mechanism on Iris.

Done when: candidate code run by a grader cannot read verifier-role files or affect the grading process on every backend, and the graders above drop their own hardening.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The fresh grading machine already separates a rollout from verifier files, but it installs `/tests` and then runs the grader and submitted code in that same machine. `Command.user` cannot supply the missing boundary: Iris cannot change users for an exec, and the local backend explicitly does not promise isolation from hostile code. The nested Bubblewrap path in #11998 is still open, conflicts with main, and failed its live user-namespace checks; it cannot be a prerequisite assumed to work.

**Relevant code**
- [`runtime/grading.py#L678-L798`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/263527428c8352ce5abeba806e410cad484ba07d/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py#L678-L798) — stages and executes verifier inputs together.
- [`shellbox/machine.py#L144-L186`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/263527428c8352ce5abeba806e410cad484ba07d/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/machine.py#L144-L186) — limits and result omit candidate CPU use.
- [`livecodebench_grade.py#L38-L52`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/263527428c8352ce5abeba806e410cad484ba07d/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/livecodebench_grade.py#L38-L52) — scorer runs code beside hidden cases.
- [`lean_grade.py#L318-L355`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/263527428c8352ce5abeba806e410cad484ba07d/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/lean/lean_grade.py#L318-L355) — candidate subprocess shares grader sandbox.
- [`livecodebench_pro_grade.py#L112-L139`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/93293f92ac51097d3a2a40eb553d63cc817e1079/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/livecodebench_pro_grade.py#L112-L139) — pending #12276 compiles and runs beside checker and answers.

# Proposed Fix

Keep the grader in its verifier machine. Give it a narrow candidate-execution interface backed by the trusted worker, which creates a separate machine from a clean runtime image that has never received verifier files. A request supplies an executable or source, explicit input bytes/files, allowed output paths, and CPU, wall-time, memory and output limits. The response contains exit reason/code, bounded stdout/stderr, measured resource use and bounded requested artifacts. It never accepts host paths or mounts, and the candidate machine receives no `/tests`, checker, verifier process access, judge credentials or broker endpoint.

1. Add the interface and preflight to Shellbox and TaskCompendium. The worker owns candidate machine creation, file transfer and cleanup; a grader can request execution but cannot grant the candidate access to its machine. Enforce every limit and confirm descendant cleanup before accepting outputs. If a backend cannot enforce the contract, return an infrastructure error before running candidate code. Local grading needs an isolation backend suitable for hostile code; a second `LocalMachine` alone does not meet the Shellbox README's stated boundary.
2. Migrate one Python LiveCodeBench path first. Send only the current test input to the candidate and compare its result with hidden expected output in the verifier. Then migrate LiveCodeBench Pro (#12276): compile and run candidate C++ in the candidate machine, return only program output, and run the checker in the verifier. Migrate Lean (#12207): candidate compile/export in the candidate machine, bounded proof artifact transfer, reference compilation and replay in the verifier. Include the RL LiveCodeBench scorer from #11992 in the audit. Remove each grader's same-user hardening only after its replacement passes the isolation tests.
3. Cover every backend used for grading, including local, Docker, gVisor, Daytona and Iris; assess QEMU against the same boundary and reject Linux candidate execution on ShellSim. Test programs that try to read `/tests`, inspect the verifier through `/proc`, overwrite the checker, forge a reward, leave a background process, and exceed each limit. Confirm unchanged verdicts for honest Python, C++ and Lean samples; verify unsupported paths fail closed. Run an Iris live check before enabling that path. #11998's node policy failure must be resolved if nested Bubblewrap is selected; a separate Iris candidate task is the alternative to evaluate.

The worker-to-grader protocol and backend admission should land first as a `Part of #12274` change. Close this issue only after the three grader families and the backend matrix are covered. The main cost is one more sandbox and data transfer per grade; benchmark startup and per-test overhead before choosing whether a candidate machine can be safely reused across cases.

Open questions for that first change: which supported local runtime provides the required hostile-code boundary, and whether Iris should create a sibling task or wait for #11998's namespace policy to be fixed. Neither choice changes the grader-facing contract.

issues.title: [shellbox] Run graded candidate code apart from the verifier's files

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
A model reply with malformed tool-call arguments stops the whole evaluation run at grading time, not just its own attempt. In an 8-task SWE-bench-Science run with mini-swe-agent on Daytona, Nemotron 3.5 Super returned a `bash` tool call whose `arguments` JSON was cut off mid-string. When that attempt was graded, the worker raised and ended the run after 2 minutes: 5 attempts had been recorded and the other 3, still running, were lost.

```
rolloutengine/grading.py:83  GradingAttempt(chat_conversation(list(messages)), ...)
taskcompendium/chat.py:72    ChatAssistantMessage.model_validate(message)
ValidationError: tool_calls.0.function.arguments
  Value error, Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 12 (char 11)
```

`_grade_rollout` builds a `GradingAttempt` from the transcript for every grader, including script graders that grade the task machine and never read the conversation. `assistant_message` deliberately rejects invalid JSON arguments at this boundary, so one malformed reply raises a `ValidationError`. `_score_rollout` (`lib/marin/src/marin/rollouts/evaluation.py`) treats any error outside `RETRYABLE_ERRORS` as permanent and re-raises it after saving the attempt, and the worker's task group then cancels every other attempt. The trigger is model output, which a weaker or truncated model produces often, so full runs on smaller models will hit it.

Two possible directions. The narrow one: record an attempt whose transcript cannot be validated as a failed submission scored 0, the same outcome as other malformed model output, and keep grading the rest of the run. The broader one: have the worker record any unexpected exception raised while grading as that attempt's infrastructure failure instead of ending the run; #12268 fixed one instance of the same pattern, a Daytona grader machine that vanished while starting.

🤖

# Research

`_grade_rollout` validates the whole transcript before selecting the grader. Malformed JSON in a model tool call raises `ValidationError` there; `_score_rollout` treats it as a permanent grading error and the worker task group cancels other attempts.

**Relevant code**
- [`grading.py#L83`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/grading.py#L83) — transcript validation before grader dispatch

# Proposed Fix

Convert a transcript validation failure at the grading boundary into a failed submission scored 0. Add a regression in which malformed model arguments leave the remaining evaluation attempts to finish.

issues.author: XiaoyuanWang111
issues.body:
Since #11989 (e3de9706b), three shapes of math reference no longer grade as they did before it. Each is either rejected at conversion, which drops its row, or parsed with part of its text as a symbol, so the right value scores 0. A census of every row of the `MarinSkyRL` math sources and the five TaskTrove math sets (the method of [my review on #11989](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11989#issuecomment-7113679024)) finds 27 such rows: `numina_math` 24, `deepscaler` 3. Before #11989 (0c236d36c), each of these references gave 1 to its value and 0 to the value raised by one.

| Shape | Rows | Examples | On e3de9706b |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Compound unit | 12 | `\frac{4}{3} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}`, `215 \, \text{kJ}/\text{mol}`, `30 \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}` | 10 rejected; in 2 (`30 \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}`, `1.8^{\circ} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{h}`) the value scores 0 |
| Ordinal | 14 | `11^{\text{th}}`, `25^{\text{th}}`, `4^{\text{th}} \text{ minute}` | the number scores 0 |
| Unit power with a sign or spaces | 1 | `9.9 \, \text{s}^{-1}` (also `15\mbox{ cm}^{ 2 }`) | rejected |

Causes, all in `_parse_reference` of `lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py`:

- Compound units: the tail check ([L129](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e3de9706b774c02117ec80d8a4693936543cc866/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py#L129)) accepts only a power after a text group, so `/ \mathrm{s}` is not a unit tail. The group must then read as a symbol, which L130-L136 allow only for a one-token group that starts a term, touches the previous token or is one upright letter. So `\frac{4}{3} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}` and `215 \, \text{kJ}/\text{mol}` are rejected, and `30 \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}` parses as `30 m/s`.
- Ordinals: the group in `11^{\text{th}}` follows `{`, so the start-of-term rule ([L134](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e3de9706b774c02117ec80d8a4693936543cc866/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py#L134)) reads `th` as a symbol and the reference parses as `11^th`.
- Powers: `TERMINAL_UNIT_POWER` ([L68](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e3de9706b774c02117ec80d8a4693936543cc866/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py#L68)) allows neither a sign nor spaces inside the braces.

Reproduce with `uv run --package marin-verifyit --extra math python repro.py`:

```python
from verifyit.modes.grade_math import grade_math_candidate
from verifyit.spec import MathSpec

for reference, value in [(r"30 \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}", "30"), (r"11^{\text{th}}", "11"), (r"9.9 \, \text{s}^{-1}", "9.9")]:
    try:
        print(reference, grade_math_candidate(MathSpec(expected=reference), value).reward)
    except Exception as error:
        print(reference, type(error).__name__)
```

On e3de9706b it prints `0.0`, `0.0` and `InvalidTask`; on 0c236d36c it prints `1.0` three times.

Expected: each reference gives 1 to its value and 0 to a wrong value, as before #11989.

I have a tested patch that restores 26 of the 27 rows (all but `1000 \, \text{kg} \cdot \text{m}^2/\text{s}`) and changes no other row of the census, with regression tests; I can open it as a PR.

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
We are targeting an update to our post-training eval policy on November 30th, 2026\. The new policy will focus on improving coverage over key capabilities, especially factuality and math/science reasoning. The purpose of this issue is to invite the community to provide feedback on the listed evals and suggest changes to our implementations.

## Changes to In-Distribution Benchmarks

The tables below list the major changes to our the in-distribution benchmark composition.

* Benchmarks slated for **removal** will be taken out of the policy with high probability,
* Benchmarks flagged for **changes** need some repair to make them work on more recent versions of main,  
* Benchmarks marked as **potential additions** have draft implementations and may be included in the next round.

We will select our in-distribution benchmarks to collectively cover the capabilities necessary for Mochi to do well on our out-of-distribution benchmarks (listed below). Beginning in 2027, we hope to make this process more data-driven, but for the Nov 30 policy, we will select ID benchmarks based on:

1. Our assessment of each benchmark’s quality and appropriateness for hillclimbing,  
2. Whether an eval can be run reliably in our eval infrastructure,  
3. The resource cost of running the eval,  
4. The wall clock time of running the eval,  
5. Coverage over our out-of-distribution benchmarks,  
6. Whether we find eval contamination in our training data.

In the policy announcement on Nov 30, we will explain why particular evaluations were included or excluded. Our full set of in-distribution evals must run in no more than 24 hours for Mochi, and our eval lite subset used for model development must run in no more than 3 hours.

The proposed changes favor more recent evaluations (which have a smaller chance of contamination and reflect modern capability priorities) while increasing implicit weight on scientific tasks. This includes the addition of a number of benchmarks specifically targeting scientific knowledge and reasoning. New core capability benchmarks target factuality (SimpleQA Verified, FACTS Parametric/Grounding), instruction following (MultiChallenge) and realistic long context tasks (LongBench v2). We have not significantly changed the set of agentic evaluations in this round and will instead focus on reliable, performant implementations of our existing evals, with a few exceptions.

| [MBPP+](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/50d4f6f/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/code.py#L119) | Non-Agentic Code | Remove | Close to saturation on Snowball and Mochi comparisons. |
| [PIQA](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/50d4f6f/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/multiple_choice.py#L152) | Reasoning | Remove | Close to saturation on Snowball and Mochi comparisons. |
| [BoolQ](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/50d4f6f/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/multiple_choice.py#L135) | Reading Comprehension | Remove | Close to saturation on Snowball and Mochi comparisons. |
| [AIME24](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/50d4f6f/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/math.py#L196) | Math | Remove | Close to saturation on Snowball and Mochi comparisons. |

### Changes

## Changes to Out-of-Distribution Benchmarks

Our previous eval policy listed AAII v4.3, Terminal Bench Science v0.1 and DeepSWE v1.1 as out-of-distribution benchmarks. We largely retain this set of evals, with some changes, notably the inclusion of LAB-Bench v2.

Below, we list the full set of evals we consider out of distribution. As a reminder, we do not run these evaluations until the completion of a Marin post-training round and do not look at any individual tasks. The single exception to this rule is the evals team that implements the public subsets of these evaluations for us to report. The evals team does not share any data from the implementation testing with the training team and will protect any data from testing runs from Marin’s training engineers and their agents.

### Public Out of Distribution Benchmarks

Mochi belongs to a different weight class from Snowball and its competitor set needs to update accordingly. We are tentatively scoping a four-tier comparison set:

**Tier 0**: Existing Marin models (currently, Snowball)  
**Tier 1**: Strong models in a smaller weight class where Mochi should be competitive.  
**Tier 2**: A collection of peer models from other open providers.  
**Tier 3**: Strong models in Mochi’s weight class that roughly represent the open frontier.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 Implementation notes on the listed evals and comparison models, checked against `main` at `6081e9b` and the open PRs' current heads. Items 1-4 can change a model comparison.

1. **Thinking-off does not reach 8 of the 12 external comparison models.** Protocols express thinking only as `enable_thinking`. In the linked repositories' chat templates, `enable_thinking=false` renders the same prompt as no kwargs for Muse Glimmer, K2 Horizon, Command A+, Solar Open 2, Mistral Large 4, Beam 1.0, Inkling 2 Small and GLM 5.3 Flash. A catalog entry can map thinking-off to another kwarg ([evaluation.py#L157-L160](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/marin/src/marin/rollouts/evaluation.py#L157-L160)), but only Glimmer has an entry. Glimmer, K2 Horizon, Mistral Large 4, Beam and GLM 5.3 Flash have no setting that turns reasoning off. MRCR, IFBench and CRUXEval grade `reasoning + "\n\n" + content` ([response.py#L31-L32](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/evaluation/response.py#L31-L32)), so MRCR scores 0 for any reply with reasoning (it must start with the nonce, [long_context.py#L36-L40](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/long_context.py#L36-L40)), and one reasoning line can turn an IFBench strict pass into 0 (key 296, `format:no_whitespace`). The 2,048-token caps of CRUXEval and SimpleQA Verified non-thinking and the 4,096 cap of LongBench v2 non-thinking can cut these models off mid-reasoning. Smallest fix: `thinking_off_template_kwargs: {reasoning_effort: none}` for Command A+, Solar Open 2 and Inkling; grade the final answer on thinking-off selections for the rest (#10828, third item); report which rows ran with reasoning. The new catalog entries also need reasoning parsers for these models' markers, because the scorers' inline fallback strips only `</think>` and `<|end_think|>`.

2. **Gemma 4 31B.** The link is the pretrained `google/gemma-4-31B`, which has no chat template. The instruction-tuned `google/gemma-4-31B-it` defaults to thinking off. SuperGPQA, GenomeQA, EconEvals, MultiChallenge and ARC-AGI-2 (#12149) send empty `chat_template_kwargs` (for example [supergpqa.py#L49](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/supergpqa.py#L49)), so Gemma would answer them without reasoning while every other listed model reasons by default. Fix: serve the -it model and set `enable_thinking: true` on those five.

3. **WinoGrande and TruthfulQA MC2 contexts reach the model without BOS.** `encode_pair` encodes non-empty contexts with `add_special_tokens=False` and sends token ids ([likelihood.py#L68-L80](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/likelihood.py#L68-L80)). When I rescored gemma-4-26B-A4B-it's October campaign requests with `<bos>` added, WinoGrande accuracy rose 4.97 points [1.26, 8.68] and MC2 6.26 [3.24, 9.36]. Gemma 4's tokenizer adds no special tokens on encode, so `add_special_tokens=True` would not help. Prefixing `bos_token_id` when the chat template writes `bos_token` covers Gemma 4, Snowball, Glimmer, K2 Horizon, Command A+ and Mistral Large 4. This is #10828's BOS item.

4. **MMLU-Pro** sends the five worked examples in one user message, and the scorer reads the first `answer is (X)` ([choices.py#L23-L28](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/choices.py#L23-L28)), which can be the model's answer to the first example. On the two Grug checkpoints of #11981 (a merged checkpoint and a Snowball RL step) this gives 41.3% and 28.8%, against 74.5% and 75.5% with the examples as turns. Other models are not measured.

5. **GLM-5.3-Flash judges PHYSICS-Verified** ([evalchemy.yaml#L81-L92](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/experiments/evaluation/configs/evalchemy.yaml#L81-L92)) **and IMO-ProofBench (#11967)**, and it is a Tier 3 comparison model, so it would grade its own answers. The gpt-oss-120b judge used elsewhere avoids that.

6. **OlympiadBench** grades the first `\boxed` in reasoning plus answer, and an empty extraction skips the judge ([olympiad.py#L43-L65](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/olympiad.py#L43-L65), [main.py#L52-L53](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/main.py#L52-L53)). The trial policy's smoke run recorded 62 empty extractions in 200 Qwen3.6 attempts (72cd9f8). This is #10828's third item.

7. **ChemBench (#11831):** the prompt's example allows a "comma- or space-separated list" (the next sentence asks for commas), but the answer regex accepts only commas ([chembench.py#L26-L29](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2abdd2c89614aa91b55da1363d415007e3930282/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/chembench.py#L26-L29)). Written with spaces, the correct letters score 0 on all 394 rows that have more than one correct letter; with commas they pass all 2,542 multiple-choice rows.

8. **DS-1000:** see the note on #12147.

<details><summary>Reproduce 1 and 7</summary>

Item 1 (`huggingface_hub`, `transformers`; Qwen 3.8 is a control that honors the flag):

```python
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from transformers.utils.chat_template_utils import render_jinja_template

messages = [[{"role": "user", "content": "What is 2 + 3?"}]]
for repo in ("meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B", "IFM/K2-Horizon-375B-A23B", "CohereLabs/command-a-plus-05-2026-bf16",
             "upstage/Solar-Open2-250B", "mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B", "reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B",
             "thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small", "zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash", "Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B"):
    template = open(hf_hub_download(repo, "chat_template.jinja")).read()
    default, off = (render_jinja_template(messages, chat_template=template, add_generation_prompt=True,
                                          bos_token="", eos_token="", **kwargs)[0][0]
                    for kwargs in ({}, {"enable_thinking": False}))
    print(repo, default == off)  # True: enable_thinking=false changes nothing
```

Item 7, from a checkout of #11831 with `PYTHONPATH=lib/taskcompendium/src:lib/verifyit/src`:

```python
from taskcompendium.importers.evalchemy.scorers.chembench import grade_chembench

config = {"kind": "multiple_choice", "letters": ["A", "B", "C", "D"], "correct": ["A", "C"]}
for reply in ("[ANSWER]A, C[/ANSWER]", "[ANSWER]A C[/ANSWER]"):
    print(grade_chembench(config, reply).reward)  # 1.0, then 0.0
```
</details>

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Measure exact repetitive tails in Mochi SFT step 400407, then test whether online FTPO can halve per-domain incidence while retaining native task correctness. Baseline measurement precedes training.

## Description

Adapt the [Dr. Doom campaign](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9691) to Mochi. Preserve the exact tail-loop detector and FTPO objective. Use TP1/BF16 serving and Mochi's MuonH/R3 training path. The fixed, hashed evaluation panel covers math, instruction following, coding, reasoning_gym, structured outputs, and STEM MCQ. All graders are programmatic and fail closed.

## Hypothesis or Goal

For each target domain, obtain a post-training loop upper bound no greater than half its confirmed baseline count on identical prompts. Extend low-incidence 32K cohorts from 128 to 256; fewer than 10 confirmed loops after extension makes a domain non-target. Non-target upper bounds may increase by at most three. Per-domain correctness may lose at most max(3, 5% of N) passes; pooled correctness may lose at most 2% of the panel.

## Status

Native-rendered cohort v2 is published and verified (manifest SHA-256 `1c2f2b83a3b895b518e7745d3a1fe05af857f56273449c6a3aad9087f9354af3`). Corrected S0 was submitted November 24 at 19:45:04 EST, runtime `2026.11.24.4`, source `1661a15e9f`, for 128 GB200 on cw-us-east-08a at production priority. Coordinator and GPU child are running. No valid incidence count is available yet; training remains pending.

The first S0 attempt was cancelled at 19:25 EST because preparation omitted the native answer-format instruction when hashing prompts. Its outputs and v1 hash table are excluded. V2 exactly matches the saved native prompt; all 512 original math tasks remain eligible.

Seal the full baseline and sparse-domain reserves before S1. The executor clock remains November 24 17:46 EST through November 26 17:46 EST; start no training after November 26 13:46 EST.

## Links

- Prior campaign: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9691
- Source branch: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/benfeuer/mochi-doom-ftpo
- Logbook: https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/codex/77-mochi-doom-ftpo/logbooks/77-mochi-doom-ftpo/notebook.md

## Decision Log

- Freeze baseline prompts and detector before choosing target domains.
- Keep circular but nonperiodic reasoning out of the exact-loop objective; report length stops and open reasoning spans separately.

## Conclusion

Pending measurement.

# Research

The issue defines a bounded FTPO experiment, but no baseline counts, frozen panel, logbook, or training result is published yet. The linked source branch currently returns 404. The prior [Dr. Doom campaign](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9691) found that a short-tail detector missed longer exact cycles and that a smoke can exit successfully without an optimizer update. [#11120](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11120) contains related Mochi serving and long-loop work, while [#12221](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12221) changes chat-task answer selection; neither is a substitute for this experiment's frozen baseline.

# Plan

1. Publish or correct the source-branch link and start the issue-linked logbook. Pin the step-400407 checkpoint, runtime and grader revisions, TP1/BF16 serving configuration, sampling parameters, and prompt IDs and hashes before choosing target domains. Pin the final full-response exact-suffix detector semantics from #9691 and test their period cap, eight-repeat rule, generation masks, length stops, and unassessed-response accounting on saved examples.
2. Run the baseline on the fixed math, instruction, coding, reasoning_gym, structured-output, and STEM MCQ cohorts. Record each domain's confirmed loops, conservative upper bound, programmatic-grader passes and unavailable grades at the specified output budgets. Count unavailable grades as non-passes for acceptance. Extend each low-incidence 32K cohort from 128 to 256 prompts; classify a domain with fewer than 10 confirmed loops after extension as non-target. Publish the hashes, counts, detector revision, and grader results before training.
3. Make the #9691 FTPO source revision available and adapt its objective to Mochi's MuonH/R3 path without duplicating the overlapping long-loop work in #11120. Preflight TP1/BF16 weight loading and a short update smoke; require a detected training signal, committed optimizer update, finite gradients, retained checkpoint, and verified export before spending the full budget. Keep the run within 128 GB200 on cw-us-east-08a at production priority, leave V5 SFT running, and stop within 48 hours of executor start with no new training after hour 44.
4. Evaluate each candidate on the identical prompts, budgets, detector, and graders. Accept a target domain only if its post-training loop upper bound is at most half its confirmed baseline count. Limit non-target upper-bound increases to three and correctness loss to max(3, 5% of domain N) passes per domain and 2% of the pooled panel. Report unassessed generations and length stops separately, preserve the best export and exact launch/evaluation artifacts, and record negative results before deciding whether another update is justified.

This is a multi-stage GPU experiment, so there is no isolated small fix to submit as a PR at triage.
