issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
[LiveCodeBench Pro](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.11928) measures competitive programming on Codeforces problems from July 2024 to June 2025: a model writes a C++ program from the statement, and the program passes only if it is accepted on every hidden test by the problem's testlib checker. Statements come from [`QAQAQAQAQ/LiveCodeBench-Pro`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/QAQAQAQAQ/LiveCodeBench-Pro) at `adebffce04` (the two half-year releases with public tests) and tests from [`QAQAQAQAQ/LiveCodeBench-Pro-Testcase`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/QAQAQAQAQ/LiveCodeBench-Pro-Testcase) at `5257736c0a`, one archive per problem with `config.yaml`, `checker.cpp` and numbered input and answer files (15.5 GB). Of 720 problems, 678 are evaluated: 26 interactive problems are excluded because their archives replace the interactor with an offline checker that rejects correct solutions, 10 have no tests, and 6 (1988D, 1988E, 1998D, 2004F, 2023E, 2044H) have tests that give one input two different answers. The prompt and code extraction follow the official harness ([GavinZhengOI/LiveCodeBench-Pro](https://github.com/GavinZhengOI/LiveCodeBench-Pro) at `d614eef4f9`), and the judge follows its local judge's compile flags (`g++ -O2 -pipe -std=gnu++17`) and the limits it reads from each archive's `config.yaml`: CPU time, twice that in wall time, and memory as address space. Every archive inspected (74) sets 2 s and 512 MB, while the statements list 1 to 13 s and 256 or 512 MB; the official harness also never passes the statement's limits to the judge. Generation is single-shot with thinking enabled and no token cap beyond the context window; the grader sees the final answer only. The benchmark is not in a suite.

Deliberate differences from upstream: the judge is reimplemented rather than vendored, since [LightCPVerifier](https://github.com/YanagiOrigami/LightCPVerifier) is AGPL-3.0, and judging stops at 480 seconds per reply so a slow program scores 0 inside the curated run's 600-second grading limit. Attempts keep a corpus reference instead of a copy of the task (#11885), because a task carries its whole test archive, up to 203 MiB.

| Model | Scored | Accuracy ± SE | Easy | Medium | Hard | Stopped at the token limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Muse Glimmer 30B (H100x2) | 678/678 | 67.9 ± 1.8 | 91.1 | 46.6 | 3.3 | 6.2% (context window, 73k) |
| qwen3-8b (H100x1) | 678/678 | 27.4 ± 1.7 | 45.4 | 5.1 | 0.0 | 5.5% (about 40k) |

No published score uses matching settings for either model, so there is no reference comparison; qwen3-8b is a low anchor. Hard problems are near 0% for the strongest models in the paper as well. Truncation is above 2% for both models and falls mostly on medium and hard problems, where reasoning reaches the context window; a truncated reply scores 0. Neither run had a grader infrastructure error. The catalog's qwen3-8b is served without a reasoning parser, so its replies reached the grader with their reasoning; extracting code from the final answer alone gives the same program for every reply whose reasoning closed, so its score is unaffected.

Validation: a local rejudge of 30 replies stratified by model, verdict and difficulty, in a Linux container with the same grade script, reproduced all 30 cluster verdicts, and each problem's checker rejected an empty output. The same check reproduced all 20 verdicts of a 20-problem smoke run. Unit tests cover code extraction, conversion, selection of interactive and contradictory problems, and judging of correct, wrong, slow and crashing programs. After the full runs the grade script gained an exact check of fractional CPU limits, which `RLIMIT_CPU` rounds up; rejudging all 32 passes on problems whose statements list fractional limits with the updated script reproduced every verdict, since their archives set 2 s.

Known gap: the submitted program runs in the grader's sandbox as the grader's user, so it could read the test answers or replace the checker. None of the 1,356 graded programs touches files, the checker or the test data. Plain LiveCodeBench has the same exposure; #12274 tracks isolating candidate code in the runtime rather than in each grader.

Grading needs `run.concurrency: 16`: at the default 64, the 12 GiB grader job ran out of memory staging test archives. At 16 it peaked at 7.2 GiB (Glimmer) and 5.8 GiB (qwen3-8b). #12217 tracks bounding grading separately so the override can go.

| Run | Hardware | Start to finish | GPU-hours | $ (CoreWeave list, $6.155/GPU-hour) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Glimmer | H100x2 | 6.1 h, 5 inference preemptions | at most 11.5 | at most $71 |
| qwen3-8b | H100x1 | 7.6 h, 5 inference preemptions | at most 6.0 | at most $37 |

Costs are upper bounds from job durations; preemptions inflated both. Grading runs on CPU and has no judge cost.

License: statements are Apache-2.0 (gated on Hugging Face; accept its terms); the tests and the official harness state no license, and the harness is followed rather than copied, apart from its one-sentence prompt; `testlib.h` 0.9.41 is MIT, fetched at a pinned commit.

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
TruthfulQA's authors released a binary-choice version in January 2025 ([sylinrl/TruthfulQA](https://github.com/sylinrl/TruthfulQA), [announcement](https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/Bunfwz6JsNd44kgLT/new-improved-multiple-choice-truthfulqa)). It pairs each question's Best Answer with a new Best Incorrect Answer column and recommends this setting over the original MC1/MC2. The curated catalog's `truthfulqa` is still the v1 MC2 protocol on `truthfulqa/truthful_qa` (817 rows). The new benchmark `truthfulqa-binary` sits alongside it and reads `TruthfulQA.csv` at commit `d71c110897f5d31c5d7f309e7bc316c152f6f031` (sha256-pinned). That gives 790 questions: 30 v1 questions were removed and 3 added.

Upstream asks for the two options to be shown in random order but ships no runner, prompt or per-model scores, so the prompts are Marin's own. Option order is the low bit of `sha256(question)`, which places the true answer at A for 395 questions and at B for 395. The order is shared by two protocols:

| Protocol | `--evals` key | Prompt | Scoring |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `likelihood` (default) | `truthfulqa-binary` | `Q: …\nA. …\nB. …\nAnswer:`, zero-shot | log-probability of ` A` vs ` B` (`acc,none`) |
| `chat` | `truthfulqa-binary-chat` | instruction asking for a final `Answer: A` or `Answer: B` line | verifyit `McqSpec` on the last answer line in a grader machine, final answer only |

Validation used full-population runs on two models of the standard panel:

| Model | Hardware | Likelihood | Chat |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Muse Glimmer 30B | H100x2 | 0.765 ± 0.015 | 0.925 ± 0.009 |
| Marin Snowball v0.1 | likelihood on TPU v5p-8, chat on H100x4 | 0.637 ± 0.017 | 0.828 ± 0.013 |

All 790 items scored in every run. Every chat answer produced an extractable letter and stopped normally, so nothing was truncated. For Glimmer, the extracted letter matched the last `Answer:` line in all 790 responses. The 59 misses are typical TruthfulQA traps, plus a few debatable gold answers (for example, the karma question). Snowball was served with the `grug` reasoning parser. In 49 of 790 responses it opened a second think block after the first had closed, so reasoning text reached the graded content. The grader still read the final answer line, and accuracy on those 49 (0.80) is close to the run's 0.83. An earlier prompt that asked for `Answer: $LETTER` led Glimmer to write `Answer: $B` in 495 of 790 responses, which the extractor rejects. The prompt now spells out both literal lines.

No reference implementation or published per-model score exists for this protocol, so there is no reference comparison. A Qwen3-0.6B smoke scored 0.65 on both protocols over 20 items. A grader audit of those 20 found each extracted letter matching the response's final answer line.

Snowball v0.1 has no catalog entry. The runs used a local `--model-config` pointing at `open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1@adc0078a19a4383bc998fcdb43867b3360baf5f3`. The likelihood run used the v5p-8 TP4 layout from `experiments/weight_merging/rsi/snowball-v01-v5p8.yaml`. The chat run used H100x4 with DP4, expert parallel, and `reasoning_parser: grug`, because the TPU vLLM build has no `grug` parser.

| Run | Accelerator | Wall time | Records |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Glimmer likelihood | H100x2 | 23 min | `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/20261124-142416-muse-glimmer-30b-4edd1f10a33f440f963366d6e2bc0a71-truthfulqa-binary-f5b31deeda865b91821b03ceb2362fef` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fevals%2F20261124-142416-muse-glimmer-30b-4edd1f10a33f440f963366d6e2bc0a71-truthfulqa-binary-f5b31deeda865b91821b03ceb2362fef)) |
| Glimmer chat | H100x2 | 21 min | `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/20261124-151507-muse-glimmer-30b-60e03984aaab4d8d9f134fa357488d2e-truthfulqa-binary-chat-2b00c17ba5d85c8dbebfb362566635b8` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fevals%2F20261124-151507-muse-glimmer-30b-60e03984aaab4d8d9f134fa357488d2e-truthfulqa-binary-chat-2b00c17ba5d85c8dbebfb362566635b8)) |

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
### What

PR #10984 adds the original [GenomeQA benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05774) to TaskCompendium. Models answer 5,200 binary-choice and multiple-choice questions across six biological subtasks, using the [pinned Hugging Face dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa/tree/e655e415fa30681dddbaf4acc182bcbd8ac41943) and the authors’ fixed prompt, without tools or retrieval.

### Why

A model can describe a splice site in words. Can it also recognize one when given a DNA sequence? GenomeQA lets us test that distinction with sequence-based questions about regulatory elements, splice sites, species, histone marks, transcription-factor binding sites, and motifs. The six subtask scores show where a model can select the correct biological label from the sequence and where it struggles. That gives us a way to compare checkpoints and track which sequence tasks improve as training changes.

Hugging Face’s biology team used a modified multiple-choice version of GenomeQA to evaluate [Carbon-X](https://huggingface.co/HuggingFaceBio/Carbon-X). Its taxonomy task differs from the original, which limits direct score comparisons.

### Validation

All 5,200 Hugging Face rows match the authors’ release on the evaluation fields. The runs used the fixed prompt and sampling settings from the released runner (temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95).

All six native runs are complete: **5,200/5,200 graded per run**. They use the same questions, prompt, sampling, and total output cap. GPT-OSS reasons at both settings: low/medium is not off/on. These are single-seed comparisons, not claims of statistical superiority. [Validation launch scripts and per-model configurations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/928e45d65c81fb7bd88040d40309a3685fdd2eca/experiments/evaluation/genomeqa_validation).

| Measure | Gemma off | Gemma on | Qwen off | Qwen on | GPT-OSS low | GPT-OSS medium |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Enhancer/promoter | 38.60% | 36.30% | 47.20% | 50.40% | 48.90% | 50.00% |
| Splice sites | 37.30% | 23.40% | 29.70% | 32.00% | 37.70% | 35.00% |
| Species classification | 47.10% | 34.90% | 50.00% | 50.20% | 49.90% | 49.40% |
| Histone marks | 40.70% | 31.70% | 40.40% | 38.80% | 39.70% | 40.20% |
| TF binding sites | 41.80% | 39.40% | 41.80% | 42.60% | 46.30% | 45.70% |
| Motifs | 59.00% | 69.00% | 57.00% | 59.50% | 60.00% | 60.00% |
| BCQ, mean across six subtasks | 54.43% | 49.47% | 51.87% | 54.03% | 53.77% | 54.73% |
| MCQ, mean across six subtasks | 33.73% | 28.77% | 36.83% | 37.13% | 40.40% | 38.70% |
| **Overall macro** | **44.08%** | **39.12%** | **44.35%** | **45.58%** | **47.08%** | **46.72%** |
| Truncations / 5,200 | 12 | 1341 | 318 | 393 | 34 | 42 |

Gemma thinking falls **4.97 points**, with 25.79% truncation; Qwen thinking rises **1.23 points**; GPT-OSS medium falls **0.37 points**. All non-length-stopped responses in these runs parsed successfully. All 2,140 length-stopped responses remain in the denominator. Of those, 353 had nonempty final text and none contained a parseable answer. Grading available final content at the cap changes none of the six scores. Truncations materially limit interpretation of Gemma’s thinking-on result.

- **Paper comparison.** Rescoring Maverick’s 5,200 saved responses with the shared parser gives 50.58% macro (2,467 correct, seven unanswered). The prior Marin grader scored 50.60%. Running the authors’ extractor on the same final responses gives 50.62%, versus 49.07% derived from their published tables.
- **Replay.** We verified the prompts, generation settings, and weights for 31,200 saved responses. Replaying them through the corrected grader at `b706dbdc87` reproduced every native extracted answer and metric. All 26 grader/importer tests passed.
- **Shared parser replay.** Selecting the last `### Answer` section before applying the shared MCQ parser recovers 1,324 choices across the six native runs, including 1,050 on Qwen thinking-off. This reproduces all 31,200 choices of the prior Marin grader. The authors’ permissive fallback selected a letter on 306 additional native responses, all length-stopped, of which 99 matched the reference.
- **Blinded spot check.** A single Codex reviewer labeled 24 saved responses before seeing the references or grades. All 24 agreed on extraction and score: seven correct, eleven wrong, and six truncated. The sample included one truncation per run.

### Cost

**The six native runs consumed 30.03 H100-hours** including serving and recovery. Worker time sums the durations of started worker attempts. Elapsed time spans the first worker start to the last worker stop, including recovery gaps and excluding the initial queue wait.

| Scope | H100s per worker | Worker time (min) | Elapsed (min) | H100-hours |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Gemma off and on, including recovery | 2 | 399 | 5,310 | 13.29 |
| Qwen off | 4 | 91 | 91 | 6.04 |
| Qwen on | 4 | 118 | 118 | 7.86 |
| GPT-OSS low | 1 | 95 | 226 | 1.58 |
| GPT-OSS medium | 1 | 76 | 76 | 1.26 |

<details>
<summary>Model pins, usage, replay evidence, and recovery details</summary>

Current-main validation (2026-11-17, `5e07ba7498`): **23 focused tests and lint pass; all applicable CI checks are green**. The PR reuses main’s `final_only` implementation; its custom shared-code addition is removed. All six advisory lanes completed; fixes reuse the existing Parquet reader and centralize repeated constants. The compact grader and source-row dictionaries were retained because splitting this linear grading operation or wrapping boundary rows would add little value.

At `5e07ba7498`, the November 17 audit established: **all 31,200 saved answers across six runs match**, with zero source-row, prompt, generation-setting, extracted-answer, metric, or weight differences. All expected cell populations and latest graded attempts were verified. The upstream `final_only` change alters none of these results; no saved message combines a refusal field with nonempty content. Follow-up constant cleanup is semantically identical, and the shared Parquet reader preserves all 5,200 source hashes. The CPU-only audit succeeded within its one-hour cap, with **zero new model calls**.

Private EvalDash ingestion reproduces all six macros, all six subtask and twelve cell metrics, and full 5,200-item coverage. The macro remains continuous, with weighted uncertainty and no fabricated integer correct count. **A shared reporting gap remains:** `coverage.n_unanswered` is not populated by the native reader, although the saved `unanswered` metric is correct. No public records were ingested; this verifies backend reduction and measurement projection, not browser rendering.

Historical paper comparison: Maverick’s complete 5,200-question run scored **50.60%**, versus **49.07%** derived from the paper’s BCQ/MCQ table. Replaying it through TaskCompendium reproduced every per-item metric and all 120 grouped metrics with identical prompts. A separate two-question live native smoke also passed.

Review fixes in `b706dbdc87` reject `B1` and `B or (C)`, identify renamed pinned input files by digest, and independently test wrong answers and cell populations. All 26 grader/importer tests and changed-file lint passed. CI passed. A CPU-only replay of all 31,200 native final answers on the corrected grader found zero changes to extracted answers or metrics. Rechecking all 5,200 historical Maverick responses changed one histone MCQ from unparseable to a valid wrong answer (B, gold A). Its parse failures fall from six to five and the macro stays 50.60%.

**Blinded spot check at `b706dbdc87`.** A single Codex reviewer inspected 24 saved responses, four per run and 12 per format, and recorded the final choices before seeing the answer key or grader verdicts. All 24 extracted answers and grades agreed: seven correct, eleven wrong, and six length-truncated. Four truncations had empty final content and two had partial text; all six scored zero. Sampling deliberately included one truncation per run. This checks grading against the pinned answers, without estimating a population error rate or assessing the biological validity of the answer key.

Unlike the [merged SimpleQA Verified example (#11393)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11393)’s 2,048/16,384 off/on allowances, these comparisons keep the output cap equal to avoid changing both thinking and budget.

The declaration now follows the [add-eval guide](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8eca4ffc4b5bc9b63de1db08c3c77c8763e0b4f6/docs/tutorials/add-evaluation.md). Its curation source ID is `Eval:genomeqa`, its recipe name is `eval-genomeqa`, and its protocol benchmark key is `genomeqa`. The recipe pairs converter version `2026.11.18` with the grader hash. The publication and output-budget test passed using this declaration. The six archived model runs below used the earlier declaration.

All native inference used runtime `fe813e34c2a0d047f10a1604a12da35f162031cd`. Gemma: `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` at `4d7ae4984b7db7de8f8457170b3f1a419ee76d52`, two H100s. Qwen: `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` at `995ad96eacd98c81ed38be0c5b274b04031597b0`, four H100s (TP2 × DP2). GPT-OSS: `openai/gpt-oss-20b` at `6cee5e81ee83917806bbde320786a8fb61efebee`, one H100. Compilation and CUDA graphs remained enabled. Template checks and saved request options verify the selected thinking/effort controls. Other settings retain checkpoint/server defaults; these are fixed GenomeQA-protocol runs, not each model’s full recommended sampling recipe.

| Run | Input tokens | Output tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| gemma-off | 7,298,523 | 1,436,334 |
| gemma-on | 7,288,123 | 47,058,415 |
| qwen-off | 7,654,474 | 13,909,197 |
| qwen-on | 7,644,074 | 28,897,134 |
| gptoss-low | 7,812,272 | 8,041,128 |
| gptoss-medium | 7,812,272 | 8,005,514 |

Usage covers final graded attempts only; output includes reasoning and final answers without a separately measured split. Qwen thinking uses 2.08× output tokens; GPT-OSS medium uses 0.44% fewer than low. Failed-attempt usage is not included.

This is historical worker runtime, including serving overhead, not billing or a sum of authorization caps. Queue-only attempts have no start timestamp and contribute zero. Gemma’s paired/recovery workers span both modes, so their time is not falsely split. GPT-OSS low includes the preempted worker and successful recovery; its capacity-blocked recovery obtained no GPU. All inference workers are stopped. The subsequent audit is CPU-only and makes no model calls.

Native retries retained successful answers. Gemma’s final one-question recovery preserved all 5,199 prior responses; GPT-OSS low recovery preserved all 5,058. Qwen on recovered 28 first-pass infrastructure failures; GPT-OSS medium recovered 126 across two further native passes. Successful grades were not resampled. Earlier queue, connection, and preemption failures are operational history, not additional scored model failures.

Private audit evidence: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/genomeqa/audit-merged-main-20261117/` · [Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fexperiments%2Fgenomeqa%2Faudit-merged-main-20261117%2F). Includes per-item hashes, aggregate audits, ingestion projections, worker timestamps, and the prior detailed issue record.

Native result roots: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/genomeqa/gemma-paired-fe813e34-20261112/` · [Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fexperiments%2Fgenomeqa%2Fgemma-paired-fe813e34-20261112%2F), and `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/genomeqa/cohort-fe813e34-20261116/` · [Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fexperiments%2Fgenomeqa%2Fcohort-fe813e34-20261116%2F). Original questions/responses remain controlled.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Pinned assets, parser details, and historical parity</summary>

Data: [HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa/tree/e655e415fa30681dddbaf4acc182bcbd8ac41943), revision `e655e415fa30681dddbaf4acc182bcbd8ac41943`; only `binary/train-00000-of-00001.parquet` and `mcq/train-00000-of-00001.parquet`. The `train` split is used for evaluation. Evaluation fields match the author release; metadata equivalence was not checked.

Binary SHA-256: `0ef4c3d33541980e3fded9a5b23a952296ce3c51cb0415b42c0299a61c21938a`; MCQ: `c1cbb51449eb8a5241890337c88dc1bc0a58974b8eb4cb8bc49f310b12faeb75`.

Prompt: authors’ [run.py](https://github.com/ai4nucleome/GenomeQA/blob/7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d/run.py), revision `7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d`. Parse the literal without executing upstream code. Prompt-development-set disjointness has not been established. The paper’s CC BY Figure 8 differs from the runner; it is not substituted. Code/data availability statements do not establish reuse terms for the assembled dataset or runner prompt.

For each subtask, average its BCQ and MCQ accuracies; overall is the mean of those six values. Reversing the two equal-weight averaging steps gives the same result. `genomeqa_macro` uses weight 5 for the 100-question motif cells and 1 for each 500-question cell; ordinary accuracy remains unweighted. Format macros follow the authors’ [aggregation](https://github.com/ai4nucleome/GenomeQA/blob/7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d/collect_res.py).

The grader receives final content only. When the released prompt’s `### Answer` heading is present, it grades the text following the last heading. It accepts the last explicit option recognized by VerifyIt’s MCQ parser or a standalone option letter. A missing or out-of-range choice scores zero and counts as unanswered. The authors’ runner also scans prose for a standalone letter as a fallback. Validation reports use archived model turns to count length and content-filter stops.

Maverick (2026-11-06, historical Evalchemy path): macro 50.60%, BCQ 57.43%, MCQ 43.77%, unweighted 47.46% (2,468/5,200); paper-derived macro 49.07%. Six parse failures, no truncations or separately classified refusals. Four failures were splice-site MCQ, one histone MCQ, one TFBS MCQ. Natural-language declarations such as “The answer is X” would recover one additional correct answer: macro 50.6167%. Those counterfactual scores were not adopted. Reported API cost was $3.08, conservative accounting bound $3.93, excluding CPU hosting and connectivity pilot.

The first complete motif-MCQ cell scored 64/100 versus the paper’s 65/100; its temporary integration code was retired after the full run. The initial native replay reproduced the six historical extraction failures. The November 17 replay at `b706dbdc87` left five: one histone MCQ yielded a valid wrong answer. Both versions scored 2,468/5,200 correct. The two-question native smoke used 1,982 input and 348 output tokens ($0.0010417 API cost); it validates execution, not performance. Its provider request included seed/thinking kwargs absent from the historical run, without proving provider enforcement.

</details>

### Initial implementation

- **Protocol.** Use the authors’ fixed prompt, including its short explanation, and enable thinking wherever supported for the main comparison. Marin used a 16,384-token output cap for validation. The released runner leaves that limit to the provider. [Paper §4.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05774v1#S4.SS1) · [Released runner](https://github.com/ai4nucleome/GenomeQA/blob/7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d/run.py)
- **Scores.** Report the six biological subtasks first, averaging binary-choice (BCQ) and multiple-choice (MCQ) accuracy equally within each. Report BCQ and MCQ separately, giving each subtask equal weight within each format. The mean of the six subtask scores is a secondary summary.
- **Use.** Proceed with internal evaluation, including internal EvalDash review, and report aggregate results. We found no explicit reuse license for the original questions, their Hugging Face copy, or the released prompt. See the [upstream license request](https://github.com/ai4nucleome/GenomeQA/issues/1). If a public report will include per-example traces, ask the authors for permission first. [Original questions](https://github.com/ai4nucleome/GenomeQA/tree/7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d/benchmark) · [Hugging Face dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa) · [Chris’s comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10981#issuecomment-6991338723)

### Follow-ups

- **Thinking and explanations.** Our hypothesis is that all six subtasks primarily probe recognition of learned sequence patterns, such as motifs or patterns associated with phylogeny. If a model has learned those patterns, extended reasoning or a written explanation may add little to its accuracy. First, use the existing paired runs to see how accuracy changes by subtask when thinking is turned down or off while the authors’ prompt stays fixed. Then explore an answer-only prompt at that same lower setting. This second comparison would tell us whether asking for an explanation affects accuracy even at the lower setting.
- **Output caps.** Choose a routine cap for each model once we know which thinking setting and response format we want to use. A model generating extended reasoning and a visible explanation may need a different allowance from one returning only an option. When comparing settings, check truncation alongside accuracy. At the same 16,384-token cap, Gemma hit the limit on 1,341 of 5,200 questions with thinking on and 12 with it off.
- **Lower-cost checkpoint evaluation.** Test a fixed subset stratified by biological subtask and question format for routine checkpoint comparisons. Replay the same sampled question IDs across the saved full runs at several subset sizes. Measure error in each of the six subtask scores, how often the direction of between-model differences is preserved, and input and output tokens saved. Use those results to choose a size before freezing the question IDs. Keep the full 5,200 questions for paper comparisons.
- **EvalDash reporting.** Check the shared unanswered-count metadata gap and verify that the browser shows all six subtask scores.

The adapter has been validated. Adoption into the ID policy is a separate decision.

issues.body:
BioTasks development has moved to [Open-Athena/biotasks](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks), which is now the source of truth for the current design, code, prompt templates, and research tracking. Start new work there using the [design documentation](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/main/docs/README.md) and [research and contribution workflow](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/main/AGENTS.md).

Generate realistic computational biology tasks for **Harbor**, with **deterministic executable rewards and no LLM-as-a-judge**. Deliver public, reusable task packages that others can plug into their pipelines. The project remains in early development: the design and initial prompts are under review, and there is no runnable generator yet.

## Migration status — September 30, 2026

- [Integration baseline migration #1](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/issues/1) is complete. Maintained documentation, packaged prompts, and repository tooling live in BioTasks.
- [Discovery migration #2](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/issues/2) is complete. Follow-up questions, analyses, and plots continue in [BioTasks research issue #5](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/issues/5). The preserved study and verification records are linked there; the raw cache is archived in the public [open-athena/biotasks HF bucket](https://huggingface.co/buckets/open-athena/biotasks).
- [Authoring migration #3](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/issues/3) remains open. Prompt and authoring research on Marin's [`codex/bio-tasks-authoring`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/codex/bio-tasks-authoring) still needs preservation and reconciliation with its owner, including local work. Do not assume that all authoring evidence has moved.

Current scientific requirements, validation criteria, and publication guidance are maintained in the BioTasks design docs. Research stays on dedicated BioTasks branches; supported changes are extracted into focused PRs to BioTasks `main`. The former instruction to base new development PRs on Marin's `codex/bio-tasks` is superseded.

## Historical Marin context

This issue and its discussion preserve the earlier coordination record. The [integration snapshot](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/72008dd68247318a367a840a4f41e27fb15ff7e1) and [plan at that revision](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/72008dd68247318a367a840a4f41e27fb15ff7e1/docs/experiments/bio-task-generation/index.md) remain historical references. Migration issues link source revisions, preserved results, and outstanding work. Earlier prototypes and validation evidence do not constitute a completed dataset release.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 **This 31-trace, ten-step single-task SFT pilot is closed.** Training and the 39-shard BF16 export succeeded, but the one unchanged `bix-51-q2` post-SFT attempt was ungraded because the agent did not submit `/workspace/answer.txt`. Its trajectory shows premature completion, JSON parsing errors, and use of the synthetic siblings’ `Groups=1/2` response schema where the original task requires `Efficacy` PR/SD/PD recoding. The graded pre-SFT baseline was 0/1; this pilot did not demonstrate task improvement or measure a post-SFT pass rate. No further training or evaluation of this 31-trace checkpoint is planned. The next phase is a separate team-run SFT and matched evaluation on a larger, reviewed synthetic corpus once that data is ready; its recipe and hardware are not yet set. The current model-only and HF checkpoints are in lifecycle-managed `tmp/ttl=14d/` scratch and will be left to expire. The [detailed experiment record](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5778284554) contains prior configurations and artifacts.

<details>
<summary>Pilot artifacts, limitation, and next step — September 24, 2026</summary>

- **Pilot closed; larger-data follow-on planned (September 24):** No further runs with the 31-trace, ten-step checkpoint are planned after the single ungraded original-task attempt. All pilot and diagnostic Iris jobs are terminal; no further GPU jobs are planned for this model. The follow-on will use a larger synthetic corpus reviewed for original-label recoding, recovery from failed commands, and verified answer-file submission before the team runs SFT and a matched original-task evaluation. The new corpus, training recipe, and hardware are still pending. Leave the native and HF model artifacts under the managed `tmp/ttl=14d/` lifecycle prefix; no manual deletion is planned. This status closes the present pilot attempt while preserving its ungraded result and reproducibility links below.

- **Trajectory review (September 24):** The read-only one-CPU job `/exedev/bio-bix51-postsft-trajectory-lite-20260924-204812` succeeded and checked the archived trajectory SHA256 `b5508f2d61e99bc68703c1b5f92cfbc01a6e13631dd05d5026a061a3e64c3073`. There are ten top-level steps (one user, nine agent). The agent called `mark_task_complete` three times, first after its third turn, and received three JSON parsing-error responses. It repeatedly stated that `/workspace/answer.txt` existed, but the verifier found no such file. It initially sought `/app/response/parameters.csv`, received missing-file feedback, then reasoned with `Groups=1/2`, matching the sibling schema rather than the original `Efficacy` PR/SD/PD labels. Later text asserted AIC `297.877142`; no answer was submitted or graded, and the original reference interval is `111.8–111.82`. These observations support premature completion, format errors, and poor schema transfer in this trial. They do not isolate whether SFT, sampling, or serving caused them. The graded pre-SFT student did submit a wrong answer (73.5366) after recovering from three parse errors; this is one attempt per checkpoint. The separate 512-token first-response probe was capped and remains inconclusive. No additional GPU evaluation or training job was started.

- **Verified export; original-task attempt ungraded (September 24):** The corrected eight-H100 HF export `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-native-hf-export-20260924-192313` succeeded from the step-10 BF16 native checkpoint. Its receipt verifies all 39 shards (134,157,765,632 weight bytes) and index SHA256 `97804308c997e23e1e9c19726863122e48bf9a2a6de3a594435e69cfd0fcc3e8` at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-logistic-sft-sep21-cosine10-native-20260924/hf/`. The matched `/nothink` evaluation `/exedev/snowball-sep21-bix51-native10-20260924-194724` used the original task bytes and one attempt. Its canonical `record.json` at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/snowball-sep21-bix51-native10-20260924-194724/record.json` reports `RewardFileNotFoundError`, `had_answer: false`, `scored: 0/1`, and null reward after 169.9 agent seconds. The task verifier omits the reward file when `/workspace/answer.txt` is missing; this is no accuracy verdict. The trajectory is archived with SHA256 `b5508f2d61e99bc68703c1b5f92cfbc01a6e13631dd05d5026a061a3e64c3073`. A separate fixed-prompt response failed JSON parsing under a 512-token cap; its finish reason was not recorded, so it cannot isolate a model or harness cause. The subsequent trajectory review and closure decision are recorded above. Both Iris jobs are terminal; no further GPU run was submitted.

- **Native checkpoint succeeded; separate HF export stopped at startup (September 24, 19:18 UTC):** Iris job `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-native-20260924-190343` completed all ten updates on the same pinned student, 31 traces, and cosine recipe. All four tasks succeeded. The final BF16 model-only TensorStore checkpoint at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-logistic-sft-sep21-cosine10-native-20260924/native/` has a step-10 metadata marker that the training job read back; no optimizer or intermediate checkpoint was saved. Native save took 80.6 seconds; the job took 373 seconds after Python start. Fixed training-batch loss moved 0.752085 → 0.210412. The separate eight-H100 job `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-native-hf-export-20260924-191702` failed before its first shard when `SnowballAttention.init` encountered `PartitionSpec` outside `jax.set_mesh`; the launcher had used `with mesh`. A one-line launcher correction uses `jax.set_mesh(mesh)` and passes syntax checks, but has not been run. The native checkpoint remains available; no HF model or original-task grade exists yet.

- **Ten updates completed; final export timed out (September 24, 18:47 UTC):** Iris job `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-finitegate-20260924-173026` ran the approved 31 accepted traces, 10 cosine steps, batch 8, length 4,096, native Snowball loss with the CPU-tested layout fix, and 32 H100s. The full-student first-batch check returned finite loss 0.753044 and gradients (norm 9.905, max absolute 0.512); standalone forward loss was 0.753316 (relative difference -0.036%). All ten optimizer updates logged finite losses. Fixed training-batch loss was 0.753316 before training, spiked to 3.830647 after update 1, and reached 0.206134 after update 10. The standard Levanter 39-shard BF16 HF export began, but slowed substantially: the last verified rank-zero progress was 114/134 GB and entering shard 34/39 at 18:45 UTC. Iris then reported `Execution timeout exceeded`; all four tasks are terminal. The run has **no verified final index or `training-complete.json` marker**, so the partial export at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-logistic-sft-sep21-cosine10-finitegate-20260924/` must not be served. The matched unchanged `bix-51-q2` evaluation was not submitted. Read-only thread snapshots during the slowdown placed ranks in the exporter’s JAX `process_allgather` and `sync_global_devices`; they identify the slow stage, not its root cause. The prior four-step export completed in 16.4 minutes on the same 32-GPU shape, whereas this export remained incomplete after more than an hour. Diagnose or redesign final export before another training allocation; no automatic retry or new GPU run was started.

- **Model-only checkpoint recovery plan (prepared, not run):** The [HF exporter](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ca9511b8db88f120549f1c3c67eece49f5c52045/lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/hf_checkpoints.py) gathers each tensor across hosts, then writes and uploads the 39 shards in order. Thread snapshots placed ranks in that gather/barrier path, but do not establish why this run took longer than the earlier export. Levanter already supports [model-only TensorStore saves](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ca9511b8db88f120549f1c3c67eece49f5c52045/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py) and [later HF conversion](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ca9511b8db88f120549f1c3c67eece49f5c52045/lib/levanter/src/levanter/main/export_lm_to_hf.py). A draft launcher saves BF16 model weights after step 10 (about 134 GB), then exports on one eight-H100 node; it retains no optimizer or intermediate checkpoint. The large-model save and restore are untested. A complete HF index and the unchanged `bix-51-q2` grade remain required. No further GPU job was submitted.

- **Finite-gradient-gate run configuration (September 24, 17:30 UTC):** Compared with the preceding failed retry, the only training-code change recorded the relative difference between separately compiled forward and gradient-pass losses instead of requiring `1e-5` equality. Finite loss and full-student gradients still gated update 1. It used the same original student, corpus, optimizer, ten-step schedule, and final-export-only policy, with zero automatic retries and a 75-minute execution cap.

- **Corrected ten-step retry stopped before update 1 (September 24, 17:01 UTC):** Iris job `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-gradfix-20260924-165321` passed the 80-presentation corpus audit, same-node I/O check, full checkpoint load, and first-batch gradient computation. The standalone forward loss was 0.7523802519. The separately compiled value-and-gradient pass returned loss 0.7541760802, finite gradients, norm 10.127945, and maximum absolute gradient 0.51953125. An additional `np.testing.assert_allclose(..., rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6)` check failed on the 0.24% loss difference. The first failing task is rank 1; other tasks became `cosched_failed`, and the later gRPC errors followed rank 1 exiting. **Zero optimizer updates, no trained checkpoint or HF export, all four tasks terminal.** The source of the forward/gradient loss difference is unresolved. A follow-up payload is prepared at a fresh output prefix with only that cross-compile equality assertion removed; it retains both finite checks, records the relative difference, and leaves the 31 traces, 10 cosine steps, batch 8, length 4,096, optimizer, 32-H100 mesh, and original-task evaluation unchanged. No new GPU job has been submitted.

- **Corrected retry preparation (September 24, 16:53 UTC):** A small CPU JAX gradient-summary check passed in `/exedev/bio-first-batch-gradcheck-cpu-fixed-20260924-165028`, without establishing full-model GPU correctness. The preceding attempt `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-realbatch-20260924-163247` stopped on the one-line `.scalar()` diagnostic error before any optimizer update. Both retries had zero automatic restarts and a 75-minute cap. The latest attempt targeted `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-logistic-sft-sep21-cosine10-gradfix-20260924/`; its code path did not reach training updates or HF export.

- **Ten-step real-batch attempt failed in diagnostic code (September 24):** Iris job `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-realbatch-20260924-163247` on `cw-us-east-02a`, pinned Marin `ca9511b8db88f120549f1c3c67eece49f5c52045` and original September 21 student. It keeps 31 accepted traces, 10 cosine steps, batch 8, sequence 4,096, 32 H100s, native loss with the CPU-tested layout correction, and final BF16 HF export only. The randomly initialized tiny gradient comparison is replaced with a finite-gradient check on the loaded student and first real batch before its first update. The corpus audit still verifies 80 presentations and zero answer leakage. No automatic retries; a 75-minute job cap. The full student loaded and fixed first-batch loss was finite at 0.752465, but a `LinearizeTracer has no attribute scalar` error at the new gradient-check helper stopped rank 0 before any optimizer update; all four tasks are terminal. The later gRPC connection failures were consequences of rank 0 exiting. A one-line correction removes the extra `.scalar()` call; the subsequent small CPU check passed, and the single user-approved GPU retry is recorded above.

- **Guidance refresh (September 24, 15:10 UTC):** Further GPU runs remain on hold. Echo now includes [Harshit’s exact reported setup](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1552425627976474645/1552425818746126408), confirming the screenshot, but the retrieved discussion still supplies no code revision or hardware. A [new reply from Marianna](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1552425627976474645/1552600743628775495) reports that SFT improved formatting and fewer than 15 RL steps changed premature stopping in her experiments. This is supporting experience, not a validated recipe for the biology pilot; measure recovery and completion behavior alongside parsing.

  [#9331](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9331) was simplified to a task-generation → SFT → evaluation pipeline overnight. At `0f02d4a1f41a49e14449f18bd547851a30250e05` it remains open and explicitly says the revised packed path has not run end to end. #9328 is merged into that feature branch. [#9368](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9368) merged a fused cross-entropy compile-coordination fix, but its eight-node rerun is unvalidated and it does not establish a fix for our preflight NaNs. No newly verified H100 training/export recipe was found. Resume criteria remain unchanged. Useful data follow-up while paused: siblings that exercise the original PR/SD/PD recoding failure, plus verified recovery examples; no corpus or configuration was changed by this review.

- **Hold further GPU runs; closer precedent identified (September 23):** The user supplied the text of [Harshit Varma’s report](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1374989195109466122/1552425627976474645). It continues the same `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21` checkpoint on filtered AgentTrove plus GLM-5.3 RST successes: 63,504 rows, two epochs/722 steps, batch 64, sequence 32,768, `5e-5` AdamH with cosine and 3% warmup. Reported held-out NLL improves 1.094 → 0.909 and parse-fail turns fall 67% → 25%, while premature completion, recovery, and long-context behavior regress. This supports a functioning SFT/serving path for our student, not a claim of improved overall TB2 performance. The screenshot does not give hardware, code revision, or the exact optimizer class.

  The completed four-step biology pilot used ordinary Adam at constant `5e-5`; the unexecuted ten-step plan uses ordinary Adam with cosine and no warmup. [Marin’s AdamH implementation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ca9511b8db88f120549f1c3c67eece49f5c52045/lib/levanter/src/levanter/optim/adamh.py) preserves matrix norms and uses separate parameter groups, so equal nominal learning rates do not imply equivalent updates. This is a material difference to review, not an established explanation for the earlier incoherent model or the preflight NaNs. The latter occurred before any optimizer update.

  [Luke’s pinned launch record](https://gist.github.com/lukedhlee/d152f86a58e8619a988361e1502f9e55) is a separate reproducible precedent: `lukedhlee/vista-snowball-sft@23d8fda7`, Grug trainer/AdamH, 16 × 4 GH200s, EP8, batch 64, sequence 32,768, and a different Stage-3 starting model. It cannot be substituted for Harshit’s unspecified setup without checking those differences. Further GPU submissions are on hold with the user’s agreement; preserve the 31 traces, baseline, and failed-run evidence. The resume condition is an exact successful training/export configuration, not a merge flag alone.

- **Working precedents and revised recommendation (September 23, 21:15 UTC):** [PR #9331](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9331) reports completed one-update Snowball SFT followed by FinanceBench evaluation: baseline 26/50, task-only 27/50, curriculum 23/50. Those results use an earlier unpacked, assistant-masked path; the PR explicitly distinguishes the later packed/full-text recipe, which has not been rerun on H100s. [Issue #9380](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9380) separately documents a 64-H100 run at step 135 with a usable HF export despite a final checkpoint rewrite error. Our two failed preflights establish a problem in the tested configuration, not a general Snowball SFT blocker. The next investigation should recover and compare a successful run’s exact revision, model, mesh, attention backend, and data path before proposing another allocation. #9328 [merged into the #9331 feature branch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9328#issuecomment-5802057836), so its merged flag does not establish a new validated main-branch recipe. The Discord message was subsequently supplied as a screenshot; its report is summarized above. No additional GPU run was submitted.

- **Corrected GPU preflight failed (September 23, 19:28 UTC):** `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-layoutfix-20260923-192616` passed the previous incompatible-sharding operation, then failed the strict native/previous gradient comparison with `AssertionError: (nan, nan)`. The recorded reference-gradient magnitude is NaN; the current logging does not identify the first affected parameter or establish whether the native gradient is also non-finite. CPU testing used reference attention; this GPU preflight uses `gpu_fa4_cute`, context parallelism, and a different tiny shape. The cause is unresolved, and this does not establish a failure of the 10-step schedule or the full student. **Zero student updates, no new trained checkpoint, all four GPU tasks terminal.** No tolerances were relaxed and no further GPU retry was submitted. Recommendation: resume after a maintainer-tested H100 forward/backward and usable HF-export path is available, then repeat preflight before training. Merge status alone does not establish those checks. Keep the 31 accepted traces, matched baseline, and agreed hyperparameters for that retry.

- **Corrected retry submitted (September 23, 19:26 UTC):** `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-layoutfix-20260923-192616` uses pinned `ca9511b` plus the CPU-tested one-line layout correction described below. Output is `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-logistic-sft-sep21-cosine10-native-loss-layoutfix-20260923/`. The launcher verifies the original and patched source SHA256 before importing the model. Training remains ten cosine steps from `5e-5`, batch eight, length 4,096, fresh optimizer, and final BF16 export only, with zero automatic retries and a 75-minute cap. The matched original-task evaluation is prepared; 21 protocol fields and the task archive hash match the baseline. Evaluation waits for verified training/export completion.

- **CPU reproduction and candidate correction passed (September 23):** `/exedev/bio-native-loss-cpu-repro-20260923-191828` reproduced the exact native-loss `ShardingTypeError` using a tiny random Snowball model and 32 virtual CPU devices. Wrapping the per-token loss with `hax.auto_sharded(...)` before the existing weighted reduction resolved it. Against the preceding pilot loss, FP32 losses were **3.874972582 vs 3.874972820**, with maximum absolute gradient difference **2.24e-8**; BF16 loss and gradients matched exactly. Tolerances remain `atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-5`. This checks a targeted layout correction, not full-model GPU or generation correctness. The original GPU preflight remains required. A retry is prepared with the same 10 cosine steps, batch eight, sequence 4,096, original checkpoint, 32 H100s, and final export only. This adds one documented native-code correction to pinned `ca9511b`; The approved GPU retry is recorded above.

- **Native-loss preflight failed (September 23, 19:12 UTC):** `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-20260923-191030` reached `loading_preflight → native_value_grad → Snowball.compute_next_token_loss → maybe_reduce_loss`, then raised `ShardingTypeError` at `arr * effective_weight`. The loss uses `((replica_dcn, data, expert), context)`; the mask uses `((replica_dcn, replica, data), None)`. Source: [Snowball loss at the tested revision](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ca9511b8db88f120549f1c3c67eece49f5c52045/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py#L838). This occurred on the tiny random model before student loading: **zero student updates and no new trained checkpoint**. All four GPU tasks are terminal. The 10-step cosine hypothesis remains untested. CPU-only job `/exedev/bio-native-loss-cpu-repro-20260923-191828` completed the failure reproduction and correction checks described above. It uses no pretrained weights and has a ten-minute cap. The approved GPU retry is recorded above.

- **Agreed experiment submitted (September 23, 19:10 UTC):** job `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-20260923-191030` restarts from the original September 21 checkpoint with **10 updates, cosine decay from 5e-5, global batch eight, sequence 4,096, no packing**, and the native recipe's Adam settings. Eighty presentations are about 2.58 passes over 31 traces. The full conversations average 2,822 tokens and have a maximum of 3,477, so 4,096 preserves all examples. Use [PR #9328 at `ca9511b`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ca9511b8db88f120549f1c3c67eece49f5c52045) for Snowball's native loss; the PR remains unmerged. The documented exceptions are the existing BF16 CPU import/native GPU placement helper and a thin Trainer driver with default checkpoint hooks disabled. This preserves the agreed final-BF16-export-only policy; the stock launcher would force a model-and-optimizer checkpoint. Distributed initialization precedes model config parsing; W&B and reference-code copying remain disabled. A tiny native/previous loss-and-gradient comparison, exact checkpoint round trip, and an 80-presentation corpus audit precede student loading. The same first training batch will be scored before and after each update; it remains training data and creates no validation split. Use 32 H100s with zero retries and the existing 75-minute cap. A newer maintainer-tested path can be tried when available.

- **Full regression audit completed (September 23):** CPU-only job `/exedev/bio-sft-weight-audit-20260923-183344` compared **67,078,882,816 values across 502 tensors and 39 shards**. Both checkpoints have zero non-finite values; no delta exceeds the conservative four-update Adam bound plus BF16 rounding. Global relative L2 change is **0.414%**. This reduces evidence for gross corruption but does not rule out harmful optimization or training semantics. Source/final tokenizer JSON, inference/training templates, and generation configuration match exactly. Full per-tensor report: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-sft-weight-audit-20260923-183344/report.json`.

- **Post-SFT evaluation stopped and preserved (September 23, 18:20 UTC):** `/exedev/snowball-sep21-bix51-post-sft-20260923-180511` produced incoherent, invalid JSON from its first response; later inspected responses remained incoherent. Harbor received SIGINT after approval and saved the trial as `CancelledError`: one attempted, zero graded, no answer, null reward, **496.04 seconds** of agent execution. This is not a scored benchmark failure. The parent is terminal and its eight-H100 inference child was released. A subsequent Daytona inventory found no owned sandbox. Canonical record: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/snowball-sep21-bix51-post-sft-20260923-180511/record.json`; sibling `results/protocol-stop.json` records the stop. Trajectory SHA256: `93b4bb468d4b09ad466903809711b01b0a6e1507009f51d5b42b770f99321c0f`.

- **Regression investigation:** sixteen evaluation settings and all task-file hashes match the coherent baseline. The tiny HF round-trip check and finite training losses do not establish full-model generation correctness after updates. The [native recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2163b2b4e50bdeb697f17433e296ad9fe842008f/experiments/sft/configs/snowball_h100.py) uses a base checkpoint, ten updates, and cosine decay from `5e-5`; this pilot continued an SFT checkpoint for four updates at constant `5e-5`. Those settings are not validated for this continuation. Too few updates may limit learning; an excessive learning rate, training error, or export/serving mismatch could explain the degradation. The completed weight audit and the subsequent cosine run are recorded above.

- **SFT and final export succeeded (September 23):** `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-native32h-20260923-174000` completed successfully on all four tasks. Its loader audit confirms **31 unique traces presented once**, four updates, one zero-loss padding slot, **26,963 supervised tokens**, and exclusion of the original task. Full-weight training used FP32 parameters/Adam, BF16 compute, batch eight, sequence 4,096, and learning rate 5e-5. Final export contains **39 shards and 502 tensors**, with **134,157,765,632 bytes of BF16 tensor data**; the complete index matches the source tensor names, total tensor bytes, and shard mapping. No optimizer or intermediate checkpoint was saved. Rank-zero timings: **154.36 seconds** to import/place/cast the student, **33.39 seconds** for the four updates, and **984.66 seconds (16.4 minutes)** for export. All updates had finite loss. This successful attempt used **11.45 recorded GPU-hours**; the eight native 32-GPU attempts total **43.30 GPU-hours**, excluding earlier eight-GPU experiments and the new evaluation. These are task-runtime figures, not a provider bill.

- **Trained artifact and evaluation:** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-logistic-sft-sep21-1epoch-32h100-fixedio-20260923/hf/`; sibling `training-complete.json` records the audit, losses, timings, tensor count, and index SHA256. The matched evaluation `/exedev/snowball-sep21-bix51-post-sft-20260923-180511` was submitted at 18:05 UTC for **one attempt on unchanged `bix-51-q2`**, using eight H100s and the baseline's `/nothink` protocol. It checks the saved training-completion record, index, shard presence, and inference template before serving. Sixteen protocol fields and all task-file hashes match the baseline. The result is pending; this one-task test will not establish a benchmark-wide score or pass-rate estimate.

- **Preceding attempt stopped before student loading (September 23):** `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-native32g-20260923-171659` passed the tiny GPU-cast/import/export check: one finite optimizer update and all 103 BF16 HF tensors exactly preserved. The new I/O probe then failed because `get_fs_token_paths(..., mode="wb")` expands a scalar destination into `io-probe.safetensors/0.part`, while verification and cleanup targeted the parent as a file. issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
Validate Marin's BioProBench integration against the released prompts and graders, including the LLM judge used for reasoning consistency. The integration is scoped to non-commercial research under the upstream code and data terms.

Reference: [YuyangSunshine/bioprobench at cf00fecd62583b98350cc48e26a29c92d3f21e5d](https://github.com/YuyangSunshine/bioprobench/tree/cf00fecd62583b98350cc48e26a29c92d3f21e5d).

The release contains 1,200 PQA, 1,161 ORD, 1,200 ERR, and 772 GEN rows. REA-ERR and REA-GEN reuse ERR and GEN inputs. Reference prompt rendering matched all 6,305 mode-specific requests in direct conversion checks; curation-driver publication and live scoring still need validation.

The audit will distinguish task requirements from reference behavior: single-choice QA with a numeric confidence, a permutation of all step indices, a single True/False error judgment, protocol-generation similarity metrics, and agreement between a reasoning response and the supplied error description. Known reference behaviors to measure include accepting ambiguous True/False answers, excluding malformed answers from accuracy denominators, pair-weighting ordering scores, and judging 601 error rows even though three lack an error description.

Done when:

- All six modes publish through the curation driver and reproduce the source prompts.
- The 50-item Qwen3-0.6B smoke and full-population comparison have durable per-item records and complete graded coverage.
- Deterministic graders are compared with upstream on the same saved responses, with every disagreement explained.
- At least 20 real responses per generation mode are inspected, including unparseable outputs; the consistency judge has a frozen sample and independent blinded reviews.
- Grader errors and protocol differences are quantified, and the reviewed implementation links its validation records.

No live model scores or completed judge audit are available yet.

comments.body:
🤖
# Research

At Marin main commit [a9ebf7c](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/a9ebf7ceb09380b963615ddc3104012faa992285/experiments/evaluation), there is no BioProBench integration; the open PR search found no overlapping work. Marin's evaluation pipeline already has durable run records, but the pinned upstream release separates deterministic scoring from the REA-ERR LLM judge, and its portable evaluator has no REA-GEN alias. Prompt conversion alone therefore does not establish graded coverage or judge validity.

**Relevant code**
- [Marin evaluation pipeline](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a9ebf7ceb09380b963615ddc3104012faa992285/experiments/evaluation/pipeline.py) — launch and artifact entry point.
- [Marin run records](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a9ebf7ceb09380b963615ddc3104012faa992285/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/records.py) — durable run provenance.
- [Upstream evaluator](https://github.com/YuyangSunshine/bioprobench/blob/cf00fecd62583b98350cc48e26a29c92d3f21e5d/skills/evaluate-protocol-outputs/scripts/evaluate.py) — five graded aliases and error export.
- [Upstream REA-ERR judge](https://github.com/YuyangSunshine/bioprobench/blob/cf00fecd62583b98350cc48e26a29c92d3f21e5d/Scripts/LLM-as-a-judge_for_REA-ERR.py) — separate model judgment path.
- [Upstream terms](https://github.com/YuyangSunshine/bioprobench/blob/cf00fecd62583b98350cc48e26a29c92d3f21e5d/LICENSE.MD) — non-commercial code and data use.

# Proposed Fix

1. Pin the source revision, input IDs, prompts, grader versions, and non-commercial attribution. Publish all six modes through the curation driver, then compare its 6,305 rendered requests against the pinned source by ID and prompt bytes.
2. Run a 50-item Qwen3-0.6B smoke before the full population. Save each prompt, raw response, parse outcome, grader output or error, model configuration, and source ID in durable artifacts. Check expected counts and graded coverage by mode before reporting aggregate scores.
3. Replay the same saved responses through Marin and upstream deterministic graders. Publish every disagreement with its input, both decisions, and explanation; report malformed-answer counts and denominators separately, including the known True/False, ordering-weight, and missing-description cases.
4. Inspect at least 20 real responses in each generation mode, including unparseable ones. Freeze a REA-ERR judge sample that includes the three missing-description rows, obtain independent blinded reviews, and report agreement with the judge plus its model, prompt, and version. Document how REA-GEN is graded, since the portable upstream evaluator does not expose it.
5. Link the per-item records, comparison table, review rubric and labels, and measured protocol differences from the validation PR. Merge only after the curation, scoring, and judge evidence satisfies the issue's completion criteria.
