issues.title: [eval] Validate BioProBench scoring and reasoning consistency

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
## What

We propose the 50 public BiomniBench-DA tasks as a Marin in-distribution (ID) development evaluation. A model analyzes biomedical data and submits a methods report and a final answer. A judge scores them against a task-specific rubric. We used Marin’s evaluation launcher, the selected BixBench Pi harness and MiniMax judge configuration, and Biomni’s one-hour agent limit. This proposal uses external checkpoints only. [Pinned dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/phylobio/BiomniBench-DA/tree/e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235) · [Launch code, task recipes and receipts](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/tree/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full)

**How the inputs differ from the release.** We used the original inputs for 45 tasks. For five tasks, the released data files exceeded our Daytona account’s 10 GiB disk limit. The merged [Marin Harbor adapter PR #184](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/184) introduced two optional changes. We enabled both for all three models:

- **Two colorectal cancer tasks** (`da-1-3`, `da-1-4`). We omitted the 19.18 GB expression matrix and retained the clinical and cell metadata. The supplied cell annotations remain available, but they can no longer be rederived from expression in these sandboxes.
- **Three lupus tasks** (`da-17-1`, `da-17-3`, `da-17-5`). We replaced the 12.22 GB single-cell file with a 2.64 GB version that preserves every cell, raw counts and metadata. It omits the normalized expression matrix and embeddings. [Pinned data and conversion recipe](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/biomnibench-da-lupus-raw-counts/tree/60044fab4ca09e55041729670deb55b4e6205c83)

All five tasks remain in the 50-task score. The open question is whether the retained inputs support every criterion in their original rubrics.

## Why

- **Broader scientific coverage.** One task asks which expanded T-cell receptor clonotypes are shared across patients in a lung cancer cohort, using supplied clonotype annotations. Another explicitly asks for weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) to identify groups of genes whose expression varies together in ALS spinal cord. Our review found no close counterpart for either workflow among BixBench’s 205 public questions. [T-cell repertoire task](https://huggingface.co/datasets/phylobio/BiomniBench-DA/blob/e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235/da-4-7/instruction.md) · [Co-expression network task](https://huggingface.co/datasets/phylobio/BiomniBench-DA/blob/e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235/da-15-2/instruction.md) · [Task-by-task comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6781595235)
- **An independent source of tasks.** Phylo developed BiomniBench-DA and FutureHouse developed BixBench. Including both gives Marin two independent teams’ choices about which datasets to use, which scientific questions to ask, and what counts as a good answer. [BiomniBench-DA](https://huggingface.co/datasets/phylobio/BiomniBench-DA) · [BixBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench)
- **Visibility into methodological choices.** Both benchmarks require multi-step analysis. BixBench grades whether the submitted answer matches the reference. BiomniBench-DA also grades the model’s written account of how it reached its conclusion, so reviewers can inspect which reported methods met the rubric. Verifying that the model executed those steps requires a separate audit of its tool use. [BixBench verifier](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/e96b6dcca1513e97e43523eaa971a85c68fcedae/adapters/bixbench/src/bixbench/task-template/tests/llm_judge.py#L14-L27) · [BiomniBench-DA verifier](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/pilot/llm_judge.py#L185-L213)

## Validation

**All 150 external-model outcomes are scored.** Both benchmarks rank the three matched checkpoints Qwen, Gemma, then GPT-OSS. Whether the additional workflows help select between nearby training checkpoints remains open. The paper reports results over 100 tasks and three repetitions. Our public-50 evidence covers one pass per model, including operational recoveries. [Paper](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.05.12.724604v2.full)

### External-model evidence (November 20)

| Checkpoint and task-level scores | Biomni signed mean / 100 | Scored | BixBench solved / scored |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [Qwen3.6-35B-A3B](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full/qwen-reconciled-50.csv) | 49.72 | 50/50 | 73/202 (36.14%) |
| [Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/d411dfa070/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full/gemma-reconciled-50.csv) | 21.70 | 50/50 | 62/204 (30.39%) |
| [GPT-OSS-20B](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full/gpt-oss-reconciled-50.csv) | 14.74 | 50/50 | 35/205 (17.07%) |

Gemma’s replacement on `da-13-1` earned 12 signed and 17 unsigned points, giving a final unsigned mean of 25.30/100. [Final Gemma reconciliation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/d411dfa070/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/notebook.md#november-20--completed-gemma-scorecard). All five derived-input tasks have scores for every model. Qwen and GPT-OSS had unsigned means of 52.72 and 17.40. Qwen used four frozen-submission grades. GPT-OSS had 23 judged submissions and 27 verified missing submissions scored zero. For GPT-OSS and Gemma, malformed judge output permits up to four total calls on the same submission, stopping at the first valid grade. Exhausted submissions remain unscored. [Interim comparison, subgroup results and recovery history](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/notebook.md#november-20--interim-evidence-for-the-marin-id-decision).

BixBench attempted 205 questions at each matching model revision. The table uses the higher-coverage Gemma run. The other scored 60/190 (31.58%) and gives the same order. BixBench measures questions solved and Biomni measures rubric points. One pass over three external checkpoints leaves the value for choosing between nearby training checkpoints open. [Comparison records and coverage](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full/bixbench-comparison-records.json).

### Inspect runs in EvalDash

The only verified BiomniBench-DA dashboard link for these baselines is the [Qwen control on da-4-6](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261113-170958-Qwen-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-74446197bd5c4ddd8e5c7c5e0e596e5b-control-2d398d772a4753f281a924f06e1a3df9) (one graded task, 28/100 signed). Marina login is required.

The EvalDash API returned 404 for the Qwen, Gemma and GPT-OSS first-pass run IDs and their checked continuation or replacement IDs on November 20. For the public-50 results, use the task-level scorecards in the table above: all three now cover 50/50 scored tasks.

<details>
<summary>Protocol, input modifications and scoring rules</summary>

### Proposed protocol

| Component | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| Population | All 50 public tasks; no exclusions based on model performance. Report the aggregate and separate 45 unchanged-input / five derived-input summaries. |
| Sandbox | Daytona; preserve each task's native CPU/GPU allocation (2 CPUs, no GPU); RAM = min(native, 8 GiB), disk = min(native, 10 GiB). The release requests 16/20 GiB for 48 tasks and 4/10 GiB for two. |
| Time limits | 3,600 seconds for the agent; 900 seconds for the verifier. Setup and serving startup are separate. |
| Harness | Pi through Marin's standard launcher and vendored Harbor. Pilot pin: Pi 0.87.0. The selected BixBench YAML does not pin Pi; the final baseline version still needs agreement. |
| Context/output | BixBench policy's 65,536 context / 16,384 per-response output settings, with its compaction behavior and model-specific reasoning settings. Verify effective requests. |
| Judge | MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, revision `c5454eb03678d8710e54a4e0fc681b9f3b4a3dba`, using the selected BixBench campaign's dedicated-server configuration. Preserve Biomni's rubric and grading prompt. |
| Judge request | Pilot candidate: temperature 0, 8,192 output tokens, 120-second request timeout, no SDK retries; outer verifier limit 900 seconds. These are explicit Biomni pilot settings, not a claim of identical BixBench request settings. |
| Baselines | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B first, then Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it and GPT-OSS-20B. Use pinned campaign configurations and record effective reasoning settings. No Marin/Snowball models. |
| Attempts | Pilot: one attempt, no automatic trial retries. Proposed full baseline: three independent solver repetitions per task, subject to protocol and compute-budget agreement. Agree on uncertainty estimation and invalid-output/timeout/recovery rules before launch. Operational retries and judge-only recovery are not independent repetitions; do not take a best-of score. |
| Concurrency | One trial for the initial control; two proposed for the four-case pilot. Concurrency is an operational setting. |
| Evidence | Preserve per-task submissions, trajectories, judge responses, rubric decisions, failures and provenance; validate continuous-score reporting through EvalDash. |

The pilot uses Marin commit `246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7`, with local adapter/preparation files and a bundle-inclusion change. It is not an unchanged main-only execution. Freeze the complete source, image and input manifests for baseline runs. The copied Qwen configuration pins model revision `995ad96eacd98c81ed38be0c5b274b04031597b0`; the [external-model pins](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full/external-model-pins.json) record all three baseline revisions.

### Changes from the release

Live create requests against the Daytona eval account rejected 16 GiB RAM and 20 GiB disk with explicit per-sandbox maxima of 8 GiB and 10 GiB. These are verified account constraints, not universal Daytona limits. The current choice is the closest supported allocation on this account without requesting a limit increase.

| IDs | Change | Reason and validation required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M01–M02 | For `da-1-3` and `da-1-4`, omit the approximately 19.18 GB expression matrix `GSE236581_counts.mtx`; retain clinical and cell metadata. | The matrix exceeds the disk limit. Verify that retained data supports every rubric requirement; expression-based annotations can no longer be rederived. |
| M03–M05 | For `da-17-1`, `da-17-3` and `da-17-5`, replace the approximately 12.22 GB lupus H5AD with the pinned 2.64 GB raw-count derivative. | Preserve all cells and required metadata within the disk limit. Validate gene/cell/donor alignment and task-specific feasibility; normalized expression and embeddings are absent. |
| M06–M07 | Disclose the five input changes in task instructions and remove copies of deliberately omitted files from image recipes. | Prevent assumptions about unavailable data; retain exact prompt/recipe diffs and file hashes. |
| M08 | Existing adapter normalizes `da-20-3`'s 72 JSON-form Docker `COPY` entries to a directory copy. | Historical workaround for Daytona Dockerfile parsing. Apply only if needed by the prepared-image path; verify identical paths and bytes with no extra files. |
| M09 | Cap RAM/disk at 8/10 GiB; preserve smaller native requests and native CPU/GPU. | The confirmed account ceilings reduce the computational budget. Record requested/enforced resources and OOM/disk failures; input fit alone does not prove analysis feasibility. |
| M10 | Replace the release's judge provider implementation with the selected MiniMax judge through Marin's verifier connection. | Align judge model/serving with the selected BixBench campaign. This can change grading decisions and requires auditing. |
| M11 | Apply signed rubric penalties; retain an unsigned comparison score from the same decisions. | The written rubric includes negative points that the released parser drops. This is an intentional scoring change. |
| M12 | Require complete, unique criterion judgments with valid levels/reasons; reject malformed or truncated judge responses. | Treat grader failures as unscored, rather than silently accepting incomplete grades. Error and recovery rates can differ from the release. |
| M13 | Prepare digest-pinned images with Pi/verifier dependencies; adapt verifier connection variables and export continuous `reward`. | Required by the current Marin path. The control image needed a separate data layer to restore its original input at its original path; runtime checksum validation passed. Preserve build recipes, package versions and hashes. |

If any modified task cannot support a required rubric criterion, that blocks the full-50 protocol. Restore sufficient inputs/resources or seek review of a revised protocol before running full baselines; do not count input-induced impossibility as model failure or silently exclude the task.

<details>
<summary>Lupus derivative construction and provenance</summary>

The lupus derivative retains `obs`, `raw` and `uns`, rebuilds `var` from `raw.var`, and links root `X` to `raw.X`. It retains all cells; it is not cell subsampling. Both `X` and `raw.X` contain raw counts. Other root groups, including the original normalized matrix and embeddings, are omitted. The original container filename is retained.

- [Pinned derivative](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/biomnibench-da-lupus-raw-counts/tree/60044fab4ca09e55041729670deb55b4e6205c83): revision `60044fab4ca09e55041729670deb55b4e6205c83`, file `lupus-raw-counts.h5ad`, 2,642,705,030 bytes.
- Derived SHA-256: `33179d1cf993091dc0bd41372629534f6b7da1ce1114d74c36110ffbee375d53`.
- Original SHA-256: `7ba85edbdc033a9aeeecabe7a1cfcb0660282cc24b04f49fb52dd3825052c620`.
- These values come from the existing adapter. Rehash downloaded bytes before use; preserve the conversion recipe, source attribution and license. Record the CRC matrix's source hash and all prepared-file hashes in the final manifest.

</details>

### Scoring and failure handling

Preserve `/app/trace.md`, `/app/answer.txt` and the source rubrics. The judge reads agent-authored reports; it does not independently verify every reported action. Audit sampled judgments against the captured tool trajectory.

For each task, sum signed rubric points, retain the raw total, and clamp to `[0, 100]`. Average the clamped per-task scores. Thus a raw −5 is reported as zero, and a reliability penalty of −10 reduces otherwise perfect work from 100 to 90. The released parser's unsigned calculation would yield 100 in the latter case. Neither calculation is established as the one used for the paper's results.

Export `reward = score / 100` for Marin's continuous metric path, preserving the 0–100 score, raw signed total and unsigned comparison in the evidence. Verify EvalDash's displayed scale; report mean rubric score, not accuracy.

The selected runner does not yet guarantee this failure contract: with no exception and a present `verifier_result`, `_read_trial` marks the trial scored even when `rewards.reward` is missing, defaulting its value to zero ([source](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py#L207-L233)). This is confirmed by code inspection, not an end-to-end control. Add missing, nonnumeric and nonfinite reward controls alongside a valid zero; verify scored coverage as well as the aggregate. Resolve any demonstrated adapter/shared-runner defect in a scoped PR before full baselines.

Proposed failure handling:

- Confirmed empty submissions receive zero; grade partial submissions and flag them. Confirm emptiness only after successful inspection of the stopped agent's output location and successful collection. Missing files in an incomplete archive do not establish emptiness. Distinguish confirmed empty output from collection failure in result metadata before full baselines.
- Setup, collection and judge failures remain unscored. Failure to collect a report is not evidence that the report was empty.
- On agent timeout, establish that the agent stopped before capturing and grading its submission. This behavior still needs live validation for the selected runtime.
- Judge-only recovery reuses the same saved submission, rubric and judge settings; retain both original and recovery records. Record any solver rerun separately.
- Report graded coverage and all failures. An incomplete scored-task mean is not a complete 50-task score. Resolve retry/invalid-output rules before full baselines: the paper specifies a retry for invalid/missing output and then zero, which differs from the current pilot's zero retries and proposed unscored infrastructure failures.

Preserve the source instructions' paper-lookup restrictions. Record network access and installed packages; the current environment permits runtime installation and does not fully pin transitive dependencies. The unchanged-input group still shares resource, harness, judge and scorer changes; its score is not native-protocol parity.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Control checks, adoption checklist and supporting links</summary>

Initial control checks (November 13):

| Check | Result and limit |
| --- | --- |
| Resource limits | Live requests confirmed the eval account's 8 GiB RAM / 10 GiB disk ceilings. |
| Scorer replay | Local controls reproduce signed 100/95/90 versus unsigned 100/100/100 for reliability levels A/B/C. These are synthetic judgments, not model scores. |
| Empty submission | An intentionally empty local submission directory emits zero and makes no judge call. The current `missing_submission` label does not itself distinguish confirmed emptiness from failed collection; this control does not validate remote collection-failure handling. |
| Control environment (`da-4-6`) | Remote validation passed for Pi, Python/R, verifier dependencies, the original input checksum and sandbox closure. This does not validate the other 49 tasks or live judging. |
| Standard launcher | Qwen control completed: 28/100 signed, 38/100 unsigned, both reports preserved, verifier status `graded`, 1/1 scored and no recorded trial errors. EvalDash API readback agrees (reward 0.28, continuous metric); this is one control task, not a benchmark-wide score. |

<details>
<summary>Preparation failures and repairs</summary>

Early image preparation failed on an interactive package-install prompt and then on a missing input file; both were repaired before the control evaluation was submitted. A local transport check timed out; the remote worker check subsequently passed. Preserve these negative records in the evidence package. They are not solver failures or zero scores. Historical Luna/GLM diagnostic scores use different settings and will not be pooled into the proposed baselines.

</details>

Before requesting ID adoption:

- [ ] Freeze the final protocol and a 50-row task manifest recording original/derived input hashes, image digests, rubric feasibility, requested/enforced resources and model/Pi/judge revisions. Agree on the proposed three independent solver repetitions and compute budget separately from infrastructure retries and judge recovery. Proposed reporting: mean each task across repetitions, then average tasks equally; report per-repetition means and a task-cluster bootstrap interval, preserving repetitions within each resampled task. Label this as task-sampling uncertainty, not a complete estimate of solver or judge variability.
- [ ] Verify transformed inputs and rubric feasibility for all five affected tasks; validate packaging, enforced resources and task-specific disk/memory use.
- [ ] Exercise good, wrong, partial, confirmed-empty, malformed-judge, missing/invalid-reward and collection-failure controls, plus timeout capture and judge-only recovery; verify coverage and continuous-score display, and audit live judgments against tool traces.
- [ ] Complete external-model public-50 baselines with per-task scores, coverage, 45/five subgroup summaries, failure rates and the agreed uncertainty analysis.
- [ ] Attach the exact pilot patch, preparation recipes and compact validation records; the linked base commit alone does not reproduce the locally modified pilot.
- [ ] Verify archived results and EvalDash ingestion/display; attach reviewable evidence links. The published task-level files above cover all 150 outcomes. Full-pass dashboard visibility remains open.
- [ ] Report wall time, startup/queue time, tokens, sandbox/GPU use, retries, cleanup and measured cost where available. Separate estimates from measurements.
- [ ] Assess incremental coverage beyond BixBench using matched external-model results and documented protocol differences. Reuse suitable existing BixBench evidence where available; additional runs require a separate agreed plan. Three model rankings alone are limited evidence and do not establish checkpoint-selection value. Resolve implementation placement and ownership with evaluation maintainers before the policy decision.

### Links

- [Evaluation launchers, task recipes, grading code and submission receipts](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/tree/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full) on the research branch. The receipts identify the source revision used for each submission. [Reproduction instructions](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full/README.md).

- [Biology evaluation tracking #9258](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258).
- [Existing adapter PR #184](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/184) and [adapter source at inspected revision](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/95a4b88b54cae602ade6e79d9536a2c766657301/adapters/biomnibench-da/src/biomnibench_da).
- [Selected BixBench policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/harbor-configs/bixbench-pi.yaml) and [MiniMax judge configuration](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/judge-model-configs/MiniMaxAI-MiniMax-M3-MXFP8.yaml).
- [External-baseline evidence precedent #11063](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11063).
- [Graded Qwen control in EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261113-170958-Qwen-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-74446197bd5c4ddd8e5c7c5e0e596e5b-control-2d398d772a4753f281a924f06e1a3df9). Scorer investigation and complete pilot provenance package: pending attachment before an adoption request.

</details>

## Cost

In the first Qwen pass, 33 trials reported 26,451,485 input tokens and 886,903 output tokens. Median solver time across those trials was 8 minutes 19 seconds. Median verifier time was 7.41 seconds across the 32 trials with verifier timestamps. These measurements exclude queueing and serving startup. The pinned MiniMax judge requests eight H100s. Total GPU-hours, judge token usage and dollar cost for the three-model comparison remain unmeasured. [Resource accounting](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full/first-pass-resource-accounting.json)

## Decision requested

**Does this coverage justify maintaining BiomniBench-DA as a Marin ID eval? If another check would change your decision, which one?** In particular, we’d like feedback on the five modified inputs, the signed rubric penalties and whether further independent repetitions are needed. If maintainers support adoption, the next step is to agree on TaskCompendium placement and ownership, then open a focused implementation and policy-registration PR. Marin checkpoints remain held out until the policy decision.

🤖 We can run the remaining BiomniBench-DA tasks directly from their pinned images in Daytona. I propose trying Harbor’s `environment.kwargs.image_build: declarative` for the 17 pending solver tasks. The snapshot-based launcher needs 16 missing named snapshots, and all 45 slots in the shared eval account were occupied. Each task image already contains its inputs. Starting a fresh sandbox from that same image preserves the packaged files and resource request, avoids deleting anyone’s snapshots, and lets us keep setup outside the solver’s 60-minute budget. Its sandbox started in 43 seconds with the original resource request, Pi reported 0.87.0, and all three input files matched their recorded SHA-256 hashes. All 45 slots were still occupied afterward, no snapshot was added, and we verified that the probe sandbox was removed. issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
### What

Add SciRecipe-Eval to Marin’s curated catalog. Given a goal and a list of allowed actions, a model writes an ordered protocol and a readable summary. Draft PR #12111 implements all 600 questions and all 23 reference metrics, with scores overall and by question type and level. [Pinned dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/manglu3935/SciRecipe/tree/2aad80a53a2288963b24c504ddcccd58d6b8bfec) · [Released runner](https://github.com/InternScience/Thoth/blob/a155710079da47bb26a021646fa84d5544aa180e/eval/eval_batch.py)

### Why

A model can name the right actions and still put them in the wrong order or apply them to the wrong objects. SciRecipe-Eval scores action order, step count, object and parameter overlap, and summary text separately. Those measures help explain what changes between checkpoints. They also expose format failures that a single zero would hide.

### Validation

- All 600 prompts match the released runner. The eight structured metrics agree on 3,600 constructed examples. On a 50-answer smoke run, all 1,150 metric values and 225 additional text-control values matched the reference exactly.
- Qwen3-0.6B graded **600/600**, with zero infrastructure errors. Mean raw content score and standard error were both **0.0**. None of the 600 saved final answers contained a line matching the reference step syntax.
- On six computational questions, Qwen3-4B produced zero parseable answers with the released prompt in both Transformers and Marin vLLM. Showing the exact step syntax in a separate vLLM diagnostic raised parseability to **6/6** and mean raw content score to **0.0714**. The two graders agreed on all eight structured metrics for all 12 vLLM answers. The paper’s full Qwen3-4B result remains unreproduced. [Paper](https://openreview.net/pdf/916854768ac5a1f1edfb008d3033a82a7783d362.pdf) · [Run settings, paired results and archived evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12111#issuecomment-7135316991)

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Match all 600 prompts and support offline grading with the pinned text models.
- [x] Score the full population and report coverage, mean and standard error.
- [x] Document protocol differences, including how the adapter handles serving APIs that return reasoning separately. [Implementation and validation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12111)
- [ ] Independently compare all 23 metrics on each of the 600 saved answers (13,800 values) and document any discrepancies. This can use the archived answers without generating another model run.

The full 600-item comparison remains pending, and the draft PR currently has merge conflicts.

1. Regrade the 600 saved responses with the pinned Thoth runner and offline text models; compare all 23 metrics per item (13,800 values), including raw `content_score`.

Add NVIDIA's [Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env) to the RL Data Atlas with a reproducible assessment that helps people decide whether to use the tasks. This issue tracks registration, conversion, validation, and publication. Training integration and upstream grader repair remain separate work.

**Status · November 19, 2026.** Catalog registration (#10120) and Harbor Hub acquisition (#10198) are merged. #10154 is open for review at `7281375039`. The earlier full-release QUICK run converted 7,452 of 7,496 tasks and explicitly excluded 44. The current SAMPLE campaign prepared two tasks for quality review and recorded 0 of 2 verdicts. A separate one-task diagnostic timed out waiting for GLM-5.3. Task admission, difficulty and live Atlas publication remain unverified.

**Remaining work**

- [ ] Review and merge #10154.
- [ ] Check whether the bulk relay received and forwarded the November 19 diagnostic request between 18:53:53 and 18:58:53 UTC. Once review responses are available, complete a bounded SAMPLE campaign and verify its grader controls, admission decisions and difficulty assessment.
- [ ] Resolve actor and verifier images for tasks that retain native build contexts, validate resource limits, and assess snapshot requirements before broader execution.
- [ ] Verify the live Atlas inventory entry. Qualify, publish and verify the assessment and its pinned artifacts under the current curation workflow.

<details>
<summary>November 19 validation at recipe revision 14</summary>

- In a 100-task selection, two digest-pinned tasks (email writing and interview synthesis) reused the upstream Python image for actor and grader, 97 retained native build contexts and one was excluded. For those two tasks, local Docker grading reproduced the native rewards for both reference solutions and both output-deletion controls.
- The first SAMPLE conversion attempt exposed archive bytes that could not be hashed as JSON. The reader now encodes file contents as base64 and the converter decodes them before checking the upstream digest. [PR commit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/7281375039eab9248dd36c22473a4507e1e6e2a1).
- The two-task SAMPLE pilot (`skill2env-atlas-sample2-f9cfb22-1119c`) normalized both tasks and prepared both review inputs. Its worker picked up the batch at 18:26 UTC and still reported it in progress at 18:44 UTC. At the execution limit there were zero saved quality verdicts, grader controls, admission decisions or assessments. A successful model-list request established endpoint reachability only.
- The single-request diagnostic (`skill2env-review-one-1119d`) used the same bulk GLM-5.3 route, Atlas review request builder and response parser for `task_email-writing_51ejbzzh`. The client sent one request at 18:53:53 UTC and raised `TimeoutError` 300.1 seconds later while reading the HTTP response. No response reached the parser. The worker exited after that attempt. Queue time, backend execution and the cause of the earlier two-task stall remain unknown.
- An earlier integration check passed 104 affected tests. Sixteen local-sandbox grading cases remain unverified because of unavailable Bubblewrap namespaces or missing Python `os.pidfd_open` support.

</details>

<details>
<summary>October 22 release, validation and remaining work at that checkpoint</summary>

Current status (2026-10-22): catalog registration (#10120) and Harbor Hub acquisition (#10198) are merged. QUICK conversion in #10154 is ready for human review at `4b45b34ebf`. The full-release run confirmed 7,452 converted tasks and 44 exclusions. Runnable SAMPLE/FULL campaigns remain unfinished; live Atlas publication has not been verified. The earlier #9632 implementation is superseded.

The inventory entry is `Harbor Hub:skill2env`, pinned to release version 1.0.1 / revision 2 with 7,496 tasks, digest `sha256:bef4f739bde8d865af04c04a2cb1c84ecad83b52dd558f4d582dd46c7933666c`.

Completed validation:

- The full-release QUICK driver at `4b45b34ebf`, recipe revision 10, processed cached packages in 75 batches: 7,452 converted, 42 `native_outputs` exclusions, and 2 `native_workspace` exclusions. - Native and converted grading matched across 146 controls for all 29 digest-pinned capture exceptions. Controls cover initial state, reference solutions, corrupted state, deleted state, and empty submissions, plus one symlink control. Both reward components and scalar means matched. One native reference solution scored 0.98; conversion reproduced that value. Matching rewards do not establish grader correctness.
- All 22 focused tests and mechanical lint pass. CI at `4b45b34ebf` has 18 successful checks and 20 skipped, with none failed or pending. The latest independent review of that exact commit found no actionable code defects. Its PR-description cleanup is applied.

The 44 exclusions remain explicit because the current runtime cannot preserve their execution contracts or validation found a mismatch. They include filesystem metadata, live-process and startup requirements, inaccessible state, and incomplete Git metadata in a cached export. Seven candidates failed symlink/executable-state comparisons. The Go-based `yeet` task scored 1.0 natively and 0.0 after conversion and stays excluded. The cached `lsp-edit-symbol` failure has not been established as an upstream dataset defect. The adapter introduces no new service fixture or privileged capture mechanism.

Remaining work:

</details>

<summary>Current validation setup and evidence locations</summary>

The full-release rerun completed in 35 minutes 15 seconds on one CPU, with peak child RSS about 2.72 GiB. Iris job `/exedev/skill2env-quick-batches-20261022-4b45b34ebf` succeeded. Actor and grader ran sequentially with networking disabled and bounded resources. These limits are diagnostic settings, not a validated training configuration. Native solutions and tests were unchanged. One task uses its released entrypoint through the existing setup interface; another installs Python only in the grader image. Native controls were run at `fbe65530bb`; production code is identical at `4b45b34ebf`, which only removes an implementation-specific test assertion.

The production reader/converter also checked 46 cached candidates: 29 accepted and 17 explicitly rejected. This bounded check preceded the complete release rerun. No model calls or quality/difficulty measurements were made during this conversion validation.

Original full-release output and input caches remain under `gs://marin-us-central2/tmp/ttl=7d/skill2env-quick-batches-20261021` and `gs://marin-us-central2/tmp/ttl=7d/skill2env-hub-cache-20261021`, also with seven-day retention.

<details>
<summary>Historical status and evidence before the native-image validation</summary>

Add NVIDIA's [Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env) to the RL Data Atlas with a reproducible assessment that helps people decide whether to use the tasks. This issue tracks registration, conversion, validation, and publication. Training integration and upstream grader repair remain separate work.

Current status (2026-10-21): catalog registration merged in #10120 and Harbor Hub acquisition merged in #10198. The inventory entry is `Harbor Hub:skill2env`, pinned to the 7,496-task release, version 1.0.1 / revision 2, at `sha256:bef4f739bde8d865af04c04a2cb1c84ecad83b52dd558f4d582dd46c7933666c`. Live Atlas publication has not been verified.

#10154 is open for review at `8c9be40510` and adds conversion for QUICK inspection through the existing task-curation interfaces. It retains native task files, private tests and reference solutions, and defines grading through the unchanged native test script with the arithmetic mean of its reward components. Actor and verifier images remain unresolved Docker build contexts: QUICK can produce TaskSpecs for inspection, but SAMPLE/FULL execution is not ready. The earlier implementation in #9632 is superseded.

Validation so far:

- The full-release QUICK driver at `5078b1e56a` processed all 7,496 tasks in 75 batches of at most 100: 7,423 TaskSpecs, 67 `native_outputs` exclusions, and 6 `native_workspace` exclusions. All batches completed and their output archives were uploaded and hash-checked. This establishes conversion coverage, not executable-task quality.
- Static inspection of all 73 exclusions found 41 candidates for directory capture, 22 filesystem-metadata limitations, 5 live-process limitations, and 5 cases requiring startup validation. Candidate status does not establish grading equivalence.
- At `8c9be40510`, two digest-pinned candidates now convert: `task_c-memory_qi67nu17` captures `/workspace` and `/root/.claude/memory`; `task_gws-sheets-append_njhq0ebv` captures `/work` and `/var/lib/gws-local`. The unchanged native verifier and converted grading path returned identical components in all ten controls: initial state, reference solution, modified state, deleted state, and empty submission for each task. Both reference solutions scored 1.0; negative controls reduced rewards as expected.
- These ten controls used isolated, network-disabled host-Python sandboxes and the real runtime file-capture/grading interfaces. The original Docker images were not built. Other exclusions remain: 39 file-capture candidates still need validation, plus the 22 metadata, 5 live-process, and 5 startup cases. The full-release QUICK driver has not been rerun after these two exceptions.
- All 14 focused conversion and fixture-grading tests and mechanical lint pass at `8c9be40510`. The broader affected suite is left to CI; no new independent review has run on this checkpoint. The independent review of `5078b1e56a` found no actionable issues.
- Image resolution, native-container grading, quality reviews, and difficulty runs remain unfinished. No model calls were made for this conversion validation.

Remote evidence: Iris job `/exedev/skill2env-quick-batches-20261021`, recipe revision 8. Batch manifests, output archives, logs, and `result.json` are under `gs://marin-us-central2/tmp/ttl=7d/skill2env-quick-batches-20261021`. The original 7,496 archives remain cached under `gs://marin-us-central2/tmp/ttl=7d/skill2env-hub-cache-20261021`; subsequent checks can reuse them. These paths have a seven-day retention policy. The case-by-case exclusion assessment and ten-control result JSON are retained locally in `/tmp/10154-all-evidence/`.

Remaining work:

- [x] Merge the pinned catalog declaration (#10120).
- [x] Merge Harbor Hub acquisition (#10198).
- [ ] Review and merge QUICK conversion (#10154).
- [ ] Build and pin actor/verifier images, configure native resource limits, and validate preservation of native grading behavior on a varied bounded sample. Keep unsupported execution contracts explicit.
- [ ] Run a bounded SAMPLE campaign under the current workflow and inspect execution, grading controls, task quality, and model difficulty results. Document defects, exclusions, and assessment limits.
- [ ] Publish the inventory through a curation campaign and verify the live Atlas source entry. Inventory publication does not require executing Skill2Env.
- [ ] Publish and verify the resulting assessment and evidence in Atlas, then close this intake issue.

The earlier sampled investigation and verifier-defect reproduction below remain evidence for follow-up validation, not a completed assessment under the current curation workflow. Historical ratings, eligibility rules, runtime choices, and deployment procedures are not current completion requirements. The official release and grader remain unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Earlier 100-task conversion validation</summary>

Validation so far:

- The complete QUICK driver on a deliberately varied sample of 100 real tasks across 80 skill-name groups produced 99 TaskSpecs, one expected rejection, and no unexpected failures at `5078b1e56a`. The run used one CPU worker on reserved TRC capacity through Iris; captured manifests and Parquet outputs were retrieved and checked, including TaskSpec readback. This is not an estimate of release-wide coverage.
- The rejected `task_winui-app_exphg7he` requires a running process and a live socket outside `/workspace`. It remains explicitly unsupported by this adapter; copying files alone would not preserve its grading contract.
- All 14 focused conversion and fixture-grading tests and mechanical lint pass at `5078b1e56a`. GitHub review findings were addressed, including filtering stale cached archives against the current acquisition manifest. An independent review of that commit found no actionable issues.
- These checks do not establish native container grading equivalence. No full-release conversion, image build, native container grading, quality review, difficulty run, or model call was performed for the current conversion PR.

Remote validation evidence: Iris job `/exedev/skill2env-quick100-20261021-r2`, recipe revision 8, completed successfully on 2026-10-21. The driver took about 17 seconds with peak RSS about 794 MiB. Captured output archive SHA-256: `c9b7727869de36bde4091efc7612ad2075c9ef914986fa984991faa9097a7a7d`. Iris retains the remote archive for seven days; a downloaded copy, driver log, selection, manifest, and Parquet outputs are retained locally. This validates QUICK conversion only, not task execution or grading.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Historical investigation and superseded implementation plan (before #10120)</summary>

The record below is preserved for its evaluation evidence and implementation history. Status statements, integration questions, and checklists in this section refer to the former #9632 approach and are superseded by the current status above.

Add NVIDIA's [Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env) to the [RL Data Atlas](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/fb11c931-5861-4878-8bb5-a964d652b45f/) with an assessment that helps people decide whether to use the tasks. This issue tracks dataset intake, validation and publication. Training integration and repairing the dataset's grader are separate work.

The target is the official [Harbor Hub release](https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets/skill2env/skill2env), revision 2, containing 7,496 tasks. Harbor shows the tags `latest` and `v1.0`; the same release's version field is `1.0.1`. These labels refer to the same content. The paper's private S2EBench evaluation set is separate.

Current status: implementation and sampled validation are prepared in PR #9632, now ready for review. The proposed Atlas rating is "Some issues" because one task's grader was shown to reject valid tests. This rating is not yet published. The official release and its grader remain unchanged; the investigation used two temporary copies with modified reference answers.

The intake can finish with a documented "Some issues" rating. Existing Atlas policy permits the standard Small/Large/Hosted model difficulty comparison only for sources rated "Good", so no difficulty comparison was launched. That is an eligibility decision, not an estimate that these tasks are easy or hard. The three-task quality sample does not establish quality across the full dataset.

Evaluation scope: reported rewards come from the released executable graders. The release also includes written rubrics; the paper's additional LLM rubric-scoring layer was not run or validated here ([§§3.2.2 and 4.2](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2609.reinforcing-agents-collective-skills.pdf)). Atlas's GLM-5.3 quality audit separately reviews tasks and graders and does not contribute to those rewards.

The PR contains the implementation and concise design rationale. The evidence and integration review questions below support the assessment. The author has marked the PR ready; Ben's Atlas integration review is still pending. The proposed sequence is review, merge, publish, then verify the live entry; this issue stays open through that verification.

### Integration questions for review

- Catalog design: add checked-in Harbor release registrations as an extension to merged #9518. To assess a newer release, a contributor would update the registration through a Marin PR. Atlas refresh would read that registration; it would not automatically switch releases. Evaluation jobs download tasks separately.
- Runtime dependency: retain the review runner's existing MarinSkyRL result adapter and checkout metadata. The catalog entry needs no training registration, but the runner still has this dependency. Review whether to keep it or separate the Harbor runner from MarinSkyRL before landing.
- Agent setup: use Atlas's Terminus-2 with checksum-pinned tools installed offline, preserving the tasks' network restrictions and resource limits. The paper used Pi; these measurements evaluate the Atlas setup.
- Evaluation budget: the sample used a 50-turn limit inherited from Atlas's example configuration. Two of three attempts reached that limit before signaling completion. Review whether this budget is sufficient for initial intake or whether a larger-budget follow-up is needed.
- Scores: preserve all native reward components from the released executable graders, report their arithmetic mean, and count a full pass only when every component reaches one within numerical tolerance. The paper's additional LLM rubric reward was not run. Atlas's separate LLM quality audit does not contribute to these scores.
- Shared tooling: keep the review-output validation, provenance, evidence-retention and provider-call fixes here, or split them into prerequisite PRs.
- Assessment scope: accept the seeded three-task sample as initial intake evidence. It does not establish quality or difficulty across all 7,496 tasks.

Done when:

- [x] Identify the official release and record its task count, source links and license scope in the proposed registration.
- [x] Run the sampled quality review and preserve the original solver, grader and review evidence.
- [x] Assess eligibility for the standard difficulty comparison; currently ineligible under the "Good"-only rule.
- [ ] Review and merge #9632.
- [ ] Reconcile the currently deployed Atlas source with Ben and agree on who will publish the update.
- [ ] Publish and verify the source entry, dated assessment and grading-problem record in Atlas, then close this intake issue.

<details>
<summary>Evaluation results, diagnostic reproduction and evidence identifiers</summary>

The official dataset accompanies [Reinforcing Agents with Collective Skills](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2609.reinforcing-agents-collective-skills). The registered release digest is `sha256:bef4f739bde8d865af04c04a2cb1c84ecad83b52dd558f4d582dd46c7933666c`. Project-owned code is Apache-2.0; third-party task assets retain their own terms.

Sampled evaluation:

Three tasks were selected with seed 42 from all 7,496 pinned release tasks. Every reference-solution reward component was 1 and every no-op component was 0. Task checksums match across those controls and the original GLM-5.3 attempts. All three model attempts reached the native grader without an execution exception; none achieved a full pass.

| Sampled task | Mean component reward | Agent outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ai-seo | 0.93 | Declared completion |
| api-design-reviewer | 0.00 | Used all 50 turns; did not declare completion |
| property-based-testing | 0.25 | Used all 50 turns; did not declare completion |

Scores describe performance within a 50-turn budget. We have not tested whether additional turns improve the two unfinished attempts.

The solver used Terminus-2, GLM-5.3 on Together, Low reasoning effort, and 65,536-total/16,384-output token limits. The Atlas quality-review panel uses GLM-5.3 for three judgments per task and task/source syntheses. All 555 trace-section reviews and 16 original records pass content, schema, reference and evidence-hash checks. The 246 original native artifact files remain byte-identical.

Grader diagnostic:

The task `task_property-based-testing_2kbxlnww` asks the agent to write property tests for a software-version comparison API. A separate diagnostic checked whether its grader wrongly penalizes valid self-comparison tests. Harbor's "oracle agent" runs the supplied reference solution; it is not another model.

The task was pinned at digest `c193f032e03538d875efd6a54026a39621329c2bd88614dab0160b256ed8b4a7`, using official Harbor runner commit `bf991e490394ef9c3250a6db2bc5cbda903cb4c3`. These identifiers make the diagnostic reproducible.

| Reference answer used | Mean native reward | Reference tests | Native mutation result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Authors' original answer | 1.00 | 11 pass | 12/12 killed |
| Same answer with direct self-comparison tests | 0.25 | 12 pass | Skipped by static gate |
| Same tests expressed through a variable alias | 1.00 | 12 pass | 12/12 killed |

To reproduce in a temporary copy, append this property to the reference `solution/test_properties.py`, then run the unchanged native grader through Harbor's oracle agent:

```python
@CI_SETTINGS
@example(Version(1, 2, 3))
@given(valid_versions)
def test_version_reflexivity(version):
    assert version == version
    assert version <= version
    assert version >= version
```

For the equivalent passing control, assign `same_version = version` inside the function and use `same_version` as each comparison's left operand. The grader's `is_self_comparison` compares operand syntax trees; its `no_self_comparison` gate blocks mutation testing for the direct form. The documented task contract does not prohibit valid reflexivity properties on overloaded comparisons.

Only `solution/test_properties.py` in the two temporary diagnostic copies changed. The official release, the grader and the original evaluation artifacts are preserved. All three diagnostic trials completed without an execution exception. They do not replace the original GLM score or establish whether its answer would pass the mutation threshold.

This grading defect supports the prepared "Some issues" assessment. A separate review-panel allegation of leaked SEO helpers was false: the saved trajectory shows the solver creating those helpers. The supplemental review retains the original opinions and replaces their source-level conclusion with the confirmed grading finding. Editable API verifier imports remain a separate concern without a demonstrated exploit.

Evidence and corrections:

- [`publish_review.py#L118`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cb91eb230b46ad188cb14b23f8c6fecdca4927ae/experiments/rl_data_reviews/publish_review.py#L118) — publisher rejects missing MarinSkyRL commit.

# Skill2Env Atlas contribution

## Design

Create `agent/YYYYMMDD-fix-9630` from the latest #9518 head and open a separate PR against that branch. Register one `Skill2Env:skill2env` source row from a pinned Harbor package release, with the package version or digest, exact task count and count method, source and verifier provenance, links to the official Hub and repository, and license information supported by the released package and its source inventory. Resolve the immutable package identifier and enumerate task IDs before coding the row; do not use `latest` or infer a corpus-wide Apache-2.0 license from the code license. Catalog refresh should retain the pinned row without downloading task archives or silently advancing it.

Extend the Atlas origin list, public table and details, and refresh status for Skill2Env. Use the existing source/review tables so changed data or verifier revisions make prior ratings historical. Adapt the Harbor review route and schema to record its actual Harbor checkout, task bytes, and verifier implementation without requiring unrelated MarinSkyRL source provenance. Keep the native `tests/test.sh` result distinct from the qualitative rubric and the three independent reviewer judgments; preserve solver trajectory, verifier output, judge responses, sample IDs, seed, and dated source synthesis through publication.

Run the standard seeded quality sample against the pinned Harbor tasks and publish its rating and evidence. If it is Good, run the same task IDs through the Atlas Small (Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct), Large (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B), and Hosted (GLM-5.3) arms under the current protocol enforced by `app.py`; use its judge-verifier variant only if the native verifier calls a model. Record checkpoint identities, generation settings, per-arm solved/verified/attempted counts, and infrastructure failures separately. Publish difficulty only when the protocol matches and the source review remains current. Link the dated Atlas review and dependent implementation PR here.

## Validation and risk

Test the pinned count and links, refresh idempotence, revision-based staleness, Harbor-only provenance and publication, and public filtering. Validate the applet and inspect the public page after publication. Native Harbor execution needs a Docker-capable environment; the first sampled run must establish that the released package and its verifier work before any model comparison. Keep failed executions as evidence and out of solve-rate denominators until their status is resolved.

## Open question

Does the Hub expose an immutable package digest and task-level license metadata for this release? If it exposes only a version tag, archive a task-ID and file-hash manifest with the review so the counted and executed populations can be checked later.

issues.body:
Marin’s catalog includes **118 of the 119 upstream tasks** in [SWE-bench Science](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19799) under one Pi protocol. Task 019 (pycisTopic) is excluded pending permission to modify the package. Each task asks the agent to repair a scientific software repository. A fresh verifier applies the candidate patch, rebuilds the software and awards one point when all applicable private tests pass. [Implementation PR](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12109) · [Pinned release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenMOSS-Team/SWE-bench-Science/tree/997408298e8e4d09978b1120b95c4540d1a71bcb/tasks)

## Why

SWE-bench Science is a candidate for Marin’s in-distribution (ID) suite because it gives us a repeatable way to track scientific coding agents across 98 repositories and 20 scientific domains. An agent has to reproduce a failure, use domain knowledge to diagnose it, and verify that the repair preserves the scientific result. For example, one task repairs atmospheric interpolation in MetPy and another checks that a SciPy reaction simulation conserves mass. These tasks let us see which kinds of scientific errors a model still makes as it improves. [Benchmark paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19799) · [MetPy task](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenMOSS-Team/SWE-bench-Science/tree/997408298e8e4d09978b1120b95c4540d1a71bcb/tasks/task_026) · [SciPy task](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenMOSS-Team/SWE-bench-Science/tree/997408298e8e4d09978b1120b95c4540d1a71bcb/tasks/task_035)

As an ID benchmark, SWE-bench Science would cover some of the skills exercised by Terminal-Bench Science (OOD), including running scientific tools, diagnosing a calculation that gives the wrong result, and checking the output against domain constraints. [Terminal-Bench Science task coverage](https://www.terminal-bench-science.ai/announcement#tasks)

## Validation evidence

### Reference comparison

Both Marin harnesses ran the same Qwen3.8-27B checkpoint and received native grades on **all 118 Marin tasks**. The authors’ row below uses the same 118 task IDs. [Published per-task grades](https://github.com/swescience/swescience.github.io/blob/f16153e5c47c46b2f6f2ebf0aaefae34bdf8c8bd/data/task-matrix.json)

| Qwen3.8-27B run | Solved | Pass@1 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Marin Pi 0.87.0, xhigh (catalog protocol) | 23/118 | 19.5% |
| Marin Claude Code 2.1.330, xhigh (research branch) | 32/118 | 27.1% |
| Authors’ Claude Code, xhigh | 35/118 | 29.7% |

Marin Claude Code finished three solves below the authors. They agreed on 95 of 118 outcomes. Marin alone solved 10 tasks and the authors alone solved 13. Compared with Marin Pi, Marin Claude Code gained 14 solves and lost five. Each run contributed one grade per task. The Pi result includes the verifier-only regrade of task 002’s reconstructed patch. [Regrade provenance](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12108#issuecomment-7144059476)

Pi used a 65,536-token context and a 16,384-token reply cap. Marin Claude Code used a 262,144-token context and honored the CLI’s requested reply limit. On 112 tasks at least one Claude Code prompt exceeded Pi’s window, and on 36 at least one reply exceeded Pi’s cap. The comparison changes both harness and token budget. The authors’ exact CLI version and token limits are unknown. [Pinned Claude Code research branch, per-task differences and token audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/fe984647e285f3dbff097a8bd2934adbff35ceed/logbooks/12108-swebench-science-claude-code/README.md#all-eligible-tasks) · [Pinned Marin Pi model preset](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a6b2b398cf019fdfa0cc129e7cefc97ffe37fa5e/experiments/evaluation/serve/models/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-Pi-xhigh.yaml)

### Catalog and verifier checks

**Catalog.** We converted the pinned release and verified the exact 118 catalog task IDs. Every included task matched the release on instruction bytes, solver and verifier image digests, and both timeouts. [Catalog revision](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/243f52de4c3cbd91b1b20b1a34bafcc12de66e1d) Marin requests **10 GiB of disk per solver** because the Daytona workspace used for validation rejected the upstream 20 GiB request before the solver could start. Its per-sandbox limit was 10 GiB. At that allocation, the task 002 empty-patch control completed native grading, and the Pi reference run produced grades on all 118 eligible tasks. We did not measure peak disk usage across the benchmark. The catalog CLI smoke also completed patch collection and grading on its evaluator worker. The 118-task research runs used Daytona verification. [Validated implementation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/d1e8497b47274a7c69dd0fe483983a6d07fc6468)

**Verifier agreement.** We froze one patch from each of 17 tasks with archived patches and replayed them without model calls. Marin and the standalone upstream Pier verifier collected identical patch bytes and returned identical public test reports, private test reports and binary grades on all 17. Seven patches passed and ten failed. This checks whether both verifiers grade the same submission consistently.

**Verifier load.** We submitted 32 previously graded patches at once to Marin’s local verifier on one Iris worker requesting 8 CPUs, 12 GiB RAM and 64 GiB disk. All 32 reproduced their archived grades (12 passes, 20 failures) in 4 min 40 s, including image preparation. The worker took 5 min 34 s including startup. This verifier-only replay used no GPUs or model calls. It exercises the catalog worker under simultaneous grading on these 32 tasks. The worker shared its filesystem with the host, so the replay does not establish a hard 64 GiB disk ceiling or per-verifier resource isolation.

## Pi runtime and compute cost

| Qwen3.8-27B with Pi 0.87.0 at xhigh | Hardware per batch | GPU worker runtime | H100-hours | Estimated GPU cost |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 118 graded tasks | 4 × H100 | 8 h 28 min | 33.86 | $208 |

The 108-task batch allowed up to **16 concurrent Pi tasks** sharing one four-H100 inference server. The three smaller batches contained 2, 4 and 4 tasks and capped concurrency at their respective batch sizes.

Runtime is the sum of the four Iris inference workers’ start-to-finish intervals. It includes model startup on allocated GPUs and excludes scheduler queues and gaps between batches. The separate verifier-only recovery for task 002 took 214 seconds on CPU and used zero GPU-hours. [Grade provenance](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12108#issuecomment-7144059476)

The dollar estimate uses the same $6.155 per H100-hour list-price assumption as Marin’s SuperGPQA report. It covers GPU time only and excludes Daytona sandboxes, CPU verification and storage. [SuperGPQA cost methodology](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11688)

<details>
<summary>License decisions for the pinned release</summary>

Upstream flags 23 task packages for explicit license opt-in. Marin includes 22 of those packages in the catalog and reference runs. Task 019 is the sole exclusion. [Upstream license flags](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenMOSS-Team/SWE-bench-Science/blob/997408298e8e4d09978b1120b95c4540d1a71bcb/README.md#restricted-licenses)

| Task IDs | Disposition and reason |
| --- | --- |
| 003, 020, 021, 032, 057, 066, 074, 075, 082, 083, 084, 085, 096, 097, 098, 118 | **Included for private research scoring.** The pinned source and task notices identify GPL/LGPL components. Preserve the notices in the images and any applicable attribution. Task 032 includes LGPL-covered OpenMM platform code. Task 074 excludes the cited NC-ND paper. Private execution and a numeric score present no identified copyleft-specific obstacle. The opt-in covers the benchmark run and numerical results. |
| 023 | **Same execution recommendation.** The release flags AGPL; the [pinned MDAnalysis license](https://github.com/MDAnalysis/mdanalysis/blob/2acd594449c02c2a354b07291031d89b50b52186/LICENSE) describes a GPLv3-or-later combination with component exceptions. Preserve that discrepancy in the record. The solver runs the program in an isolated workspace. Offering a modified program as a network service would warrant separate review. |
| 100 | **Same execution recommendation for the pinned snapshot.** Upstream records conflicting MIT/LGPL declarations. The [pinned license file](https://github.com/DCoupry/autografs/blob/c2f22341f2b1eb2f619b76534cf4abe2e5e6b3a3/LICENSE.txt) specifies LGPL. Preserve the mixed notices and avoid describing the whole snapshot as MIT. |
| 019 | **Hold pending permission for the benchmark edit or a legal review of this use.** The reproduction uses standalone pycisTopic. The authors explicitly list pycisTopic among the packages covered by the SCENIC+ license, and the pinned pycisTopic metadata points to that license. Task 019 requires editing pycisTopic before grading. Clause 10(i) restricts modification, including private edits, unless expressly permitted. Clauses 7–8 also matter for hosted copies. [Authors’ scope statement](https://github.com/aertslab/scenicplus#license) · [Pinned metadata](https://github.com/aertslab/pycisTopic/blob/cb5f54111d2affd89ad732c20c14dab6138026f0/pyproject.toml#L17-L22) · [Packaged license](https://github.com/aertslab/pycisTopic/blob/cb5f54111d2affd89ad732c20c14dab6138026f0/LICENSE.txt#L19-L26) |
| 026 | **Include for noncommercial research scoring.** MetPy is BSD-3-Clause. The flagged March 2019 WRF technical note in the solver image is byte-identical to the UCAR download. UCAR permits noncommercial, nonprofit research use under its site terms. Preserve the notice and citation. Its separate CC BY-NC catalog entry describes the April 4.1 edition. [March PDF](https://www2.mmm.ucar.edu/wrf/users/docs/technote/v4_technote.pdf) · [UCAR terms](https://www.ucar.edu/terms-of-use/website) · [April catalog record](https://data.ucar.edu/dataset/a-description-of-the-advanced-research-wrf-model-version-4-1) |
| 035 | **Include.** The bundled report matches NASA-RP-1327 / UCRL-ID-113855 by title, authors and identifiers. NASA lists public distribution and expressly permits public use. The release inventory points to the wrong NASA record, and the bundled scan differs in checksum from the current NASA PDF. Retain the attribution. [Correct NASA record](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19940030753) · [Release inventory](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenMOSS-Team/SWE-bench-Science/blob/997408298e8e4d09978b1120b95c4540d1a71bcb/tasks/task_035/environment/public/MATERIALS.json) |
| 101 | **Include for noncommercial research scoring.** The flagged files are modified Chen2020 CSVs. CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 §2(a)(1)(B) permits making and reproducing adaptations privately for noncommercial purposes. It reserves public sharing of adaptations. Keep the CSVs private and retain attribution. [Task inventory](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenMOSS-Team/SWE-bench-Science/blob/997408298e8e4d09978b1120b95c4540d1a71bcb/tasks/task_101/environment/public/MATERIALS.json) · [Chen et al.](https://doi.org/10.1149/1945-7111/ab9050) · [CC terms](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/legalcode.en#s2a) |
| 102 | **Include for noncommercial research scoring.** The seven 2016H66 parameter files and bibliography in the image match the pinned Polyply files byte-for-byte. Polyply explicitly ships this directory as package data. Its paper describes the library and credits Horta for checking it. ACS publishes the underlying authors’ supplementary material under CC BY-NC 4.0. These facts support using the existing library privately with attribution. A separate redistribution grant for every downstream parameter file remains unverified. [Pinned files](https://github.com/marrink-lab/polyply_1.0/tree/160e9707d844ad1b108e1d8184152050d16088a0/polyply/data/2016H66) · [Packaging](https://github.com/marrink-lab/polyply_1.0/blob/160e9707d844ad1b108e1d8184152050d16088a0/setup.py#L40-L43) · [Polyply paper](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-27627-4) · [ACS supplementary material and license](https://acs.figshare.com/articles/journal_contribution/A_GROMOS-Compatible_Force_Field_for_Small_Organic_Molecules_in_the_Condensed_Phase_The_2016H66_Parameter_Set/3475124) |

**Scope.** The license decisions cover private, noncommercial research scoring with Marin-served inference, retained notices and aggregate reporting. The runner makes working copies: Daytona stores image layers for the sandbox, and Marin passes a source-bearing candidate patch to the verifier. Public reporting of scores publishes none of those files. This decision does not cover publication of images, raw trajectories, patches, or data. Marin already registers FinanceBench and CMMLU for evaluation. Both publishers specify CC BY-NC 4.0. These are precedents for this evaluation purpose, not blanket clearance for other uses. [Runner implementation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d066a47b1a/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/swebench_science.py) · [Marin FinanceBench](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d066a47b1a/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/financebench.py#L28-L52) · [FinanceBench terms](https://huggingface.co/datasets/PatronusAI/financebench/blob/e04404e3a97f69f79c14d42f24981a1c9c3bcd18/README.md) · [Marin CMMLU](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d066a47b1a/experiments/evals/task_configs.py#L524) · [CMMLU terms](https://huggingface.co/datasets/haonan-li/cmmlu/blob/efcc940752ea4a1ea94d2727f11f83858d64fc8e/README.md)

</details>

🤖 On the 100 graded Qwen3.8-27B tasks, Pi 0.87.0 solved 3 and the authors’ Claude Code run solved 31 on the same IDs. All three Pi solves were also solved upstream. These 100 are the graded portion of an interrupted run.

I classified the last recorded model request by its system prompt and finish reason. In **75/100** trajectories, the last request was a compaction summary that reached its output limit. Of those, 74 ended at exactly 6,553 completion tokens and one at 4,096. This includes **21 of the 28** tasks solved only by the authors. It establishes a recurring failure mode. The number of solves recoverable by changing the limits is still open. [Authors’ per-task grades](https://github.com/swescience/swescience.github.io/blob/f16153e5c47c46b2f6f2ebf0aaefae34bdf8c8bd/data/task-matrix.json)

Pi budgets a main summary at 80% of the reserved output tokens, rounded down, and a split-turn prefix at 50%. With an 8,192-token reserve those limits are 6,553 and 4,096. Pi rejects a summary whose provider stop reason is length, including summaries containing partial text. The older Harbor investigation found a separate Terminus-2 fallback that could omit the latest tool observation. Its larger-budget follow-up also showed why completed handoffs, resumed solver steps and grades should be measured separately. [Pi 0.87.0 compaction implementation](https://unpkg.com/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.87.0/dist/core/compaction/compaction.js) · [Harbor #165](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/165)

The authors report 40,670 output tokens across 21 calls on 012 and 420,892 across 60 calls on 015. Their published aggregates do not give a per-call maximum. issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
### Summary
The SWE-bench-style shared graders (the taskcompendium log parsers behind the SWE_REBENCH profile) record reward 0.0 for rows whose full test suites PASS in an identical environment. The F2P/P2P parse fails to match the config's test ids against the suite output, so fully-passing suites score 0.0.

### Evidence (SWE-rebench V2.1 repaired wave, the sealed canonical)
The wave's oracle verdicts for three rows, compared against diagnostic runs of the SAME setup + gold patch + test command in the same environment family (the full captures linked below):

| instance | wave oracle reward | diagnostic run |
|---|---|---|
| blitz-js__superjson-78 | 0.0 | Test Suites: 8 passed, 8 total; Tests: 48 passed, 48 total |
| goplus__gop-1659 | 0.0 | 26 `ok` package markers, 0 `FAIL` |
| segmentio__encoding-45 | 0.0 | `--- PASS`, `PASS`, `ok` — 0 `FAIL` |

The suites are fully green; the recorded oracle rewards are 0.0.

### Suspected mechanism
The family config's test ids (FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS) are matched against the suite output by the taskcompendium log parser (parse_log_node for jest, the go-test parser for go). The parsed test names do not match the ids' form (the describe-block-qualified jest names vs the ids' form; the go package-level output), so the parse reports 0 matches and the reward collapses to 0.0.

### Reproduction
- The wave's ledger: s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/atlas/swe-repair/2026.11.20.1/wave-v11/fidelity-wave1-outcomes.json (the keys `<instance>|condensed|oracle`, reward 0.0).
- The diagnostic captures (the same setup + patch + test command, the full output): s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/atlas/swe-repair/2026.11.20.1/wave-v11/diagnose-blitz-js__superjson-78.txt (and the gop/encoding-45 siblings).

### Impact
The repair wave's oracle-failed tail (13,471 rows) includes a material share of such false negatives; the rows are graded 0.0 despite passing suites.

### Labels
agent-generated

🤖 Two results that may help while the wave's own trial files are pulled.

Full reruns agree with the replays above. With each row's gold patch and the dataset's test command, run through main's rendered `solve.sh`, `test.sh` and generated `grade.py` with the images' toolchain versions (Go 1.18.1; Node 16.20.2 with jest 24.9.0), all three rows score 1.0: `superjson-78` 31/31 F2P and 17/17 P2P, `gop-1659` 4/4 and 746/746, `encoding-45` 1/1 and 340/340. The parsers find no ids only in other output forms: jest without `--verbose` (0 names), `go test` without `-v` (one package `ok` line, 0 names) and `go test -json` (341 names, each prefixed with the package path, so no id matches). A runtime path zeroes `gop-1659` with no parse problem, if the wave graded through the shared-source controller of #11844 without network. That controller runs `test.sh` as UID 10002 with `HOME=/home/taskcompendium-grade` ([`runtime/shared_source.py` L494](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c35cd238310452c070a059e9d1fd81a1575362a9/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/shared_source.py#L494)). With module downloads off, the gold patch fails to build (`module lookup disabled by GOPROXY=off` on every import), the log has no `--- PASS` or `--- FAIL` line, and the reward is 0.0; with a copy of the image's cache, still offline, it is 1.0. Of the 2,269 V2.1 Go rows, 2,030 leave the module cache under the build user's `HOME` (209 set a path outside it, 30 vendor their modules). The other two rows score 1.0 as UID 10002 with a fresh `HOME`, so this can explain gop only. A module download error in the wave's gop `test_output.log` would confirm it.

When reading those logs: the controller opens `test_output.log` as `test.sh`'s stdout without `O_APPEND` ([L496](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c35cd238310452c070a059e9d1fd81a1575362a9/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/shared_source.py#L496)), and `test.sh` writes the test output into the same file with `cat >`, so its `test_cmd exit code: N` line overwrites the first bytes of the test output before `grade.py` reads it. On these three rows those bytes are an `=== RUN` or header line, so no id is lost.

issues.title: SWE-bench-style graders record reward 0.0 for fully passing test suites (the F2P/P2P parse fails to match the suite output)

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
Curated evaluations can run the solver and verifier in separate environments. The verifier gets its resources from the run-level `verifier_machine` setting. Catalog presets currently leave that unset, so a benchmark’s CPU, memory, and disk requests for the verifier aren’t enforced. [Discussion on #12109](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12109#issuecomment-7171954223)

This came up with SWE-bench Science. We ran 32 verifiers concurrently on one worker and all 32 reproduced their previous grades. The open question is how to honor those requests for each verifier. [Load check](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12108#user-content-validation-evidence)

This is done when a curated evaluation can specify verifier resources independently of the solver and a test verifies that the backend applies them. If the backend can’t enforce a request, the runner should report that explicitly.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

`EpisodeInputs` records one CPU, memory, and disk allocation. The Harbor importer fills it from the solver environment, and SWE-bench Science also reads only the solver allocation; both discard a separate verifier environment's resource request. Curated settings expose only `task_machine`, so the evaluation worker defaults the verifier to a local machine without resource limits. The local backend rejects disk quotas and may run without CPU or memory limits when cgroups are unavailable. [#12283](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12283) changes default verifier placement and overlaps the worker path, but does not carry verifier resources.

**Relevant code**
- [`package.py#L420-L429`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2f4074f5e170db2072512b02130d889005966e23/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/harbor/package.py#L420-L429) — Harbor records solver allocation only.
- [`swebench_science.py#L112-L119`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2f4074f5e170db2072512b02130d889005966e23/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/swebench_science.py#L112-L119) — science item drops verifier allocation.
- [`records.py#L425-L500`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2f4074f5e170db2072512b02130d889005966e23/lib/evalrecords/src/evalrecords/records.py#L425-L500) — curated settings have no verifier selection.
- [`dataset_evaluator.py#L120-L138`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2f4074f5e170db2072512b02130d889005966e23/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/dataset_evaluator.py#L120-L138) — only task machine reaches the run config.
- [`machine.py#L1127-L1155`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2f4074f5e170db2072512b02130d889005966e23/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/local/machine.py#L1127-L1155) — local quota limits.

# Proposed Fix

1. Add a typed verifier CPU, memory, and disk allocation to each agent episode item. Populate it from Harbor's `verifier_environment` and SWE-bench Science's `[verifier.environment]`; keep solver values separate. Bump affected corpus recipes so published items contain the new fields.
2. Add an independent `run.verifier_machine` selection to `EvaluationOverrides` and `CuratedSettings`. Record it in run identity, pass it through `DatasetEvaluator` to `EvaluationRunConfig`, and bind Daytona credentials when either machine uses Daytona. The task-machine backend override must leave verifier placement alone.
3. Apply item verifier values over run verifier defaults when building `TaskRolloutSpec`, only for graders with a separate machine. Fail with the task ID, backend, and requested limits when enforcement is unavailable: local disk quotas are unsupported; local CPU and memory requests need delegated cgroups; Docker disk limits need a supported storage driver; Daytona must reject an over-quota request. Do not silently reduce a source request.
4. Test source conversion with different solver and verifier allocations. Run a curated fixture through the existing fake Daytona client and assert its verifier creation request has the exact CPU, memory, and disk values while the solver keeps its own. Assert that a local verifier with requested disk fails explicitly, and cover CPU and memory enforcement in the delegated-cgroup test lane.

The SWE-bench Science fixture requests **2 CPUs, 8 GiB RAM, and 20 GiB disk per verifier**. The validation Daytona workspace capped sandboxes at 10 GiB, and 32 simultaneous verifiers would request up to 64 CPUs, 256 GiB RAM, and 640 GiB disk. Choose its preset backend and concurrency after verifying an enforceable allocation; until then, reject that preset's unsupported request explicitly. Rebase the worker change on #12283 if it lands first.
