Marin’s data is reproducible in principle, but reproducing it still requires expensive scans and pipeline runs. We want a cheap path that reuses existing selection decisions, scores and embeddings.

David’s handoff completed text reconstruction for cluster 22. Our follow-up work checked output counts and stored Harrier coverage, and is adding foreign keys to original source rows or records, alongside document IDs, cluster and quality metadata, and stored vectors.

Validated metadata now covers **85 of 150 sources in cluster 22, totaling 11,527,805 selected occurrences**. This includes all selected Nemotron Code v2 **synthetic Code Review (4,932,132)**, **synthetic Rewriting (3,447,382)**, **synthetic Student-Teacher (1,150,817)** and **synthetic Transpilation (878,851)** documents, with keys to their original sources and physical rows, selection metadata and stored Harrier vectors. Full output audits checked every exported file and source coordinate for all four sources.

All **953,132 SFT Code selected occurrences** now include original source-row keys, selection metadata and stored Harrier vectors. The full output audit checked all **220 files** and **1,024,319 physical source locations**, preserving **71,187 additional row witnesses**.

All **98,589 SFT General selected occurrences** now include original source-row keys, selection metadata and stored Harrier vectors. The full output audit checked all **355 exported files** and **131,650 physical source locations**, preserving **33,061 additional row witnesses**.

QA’s original-row mappings are complete. Its final source index and vector join remain unfinished. The full cluster 22 metadata export remains in progress. Where identical text matches several upstream rows, we retain alternatives without claiming to know which historical occurrence supplied the document.

We plan to publish metadata, stored embeddings, manifests and reconstruction instructions on Hugging Face. Users should be able to retrieve upstream inputs and reconstruct the selected corpus without repeating deduplication, contamination checks, classifiers, embedding inference or clustering. Cluster 22 is the first validation target; the goal covers all 40 topic clusters.

We do not plan to republish upstream text or tokens. Retrieval stays upstream to preserve attribution and creators’ control over removals and opt-outs. Pinned revisions cannot guarantee access to removed data.

Done when the metadata is accessible, source/vector joins and selected counts are validated, and a worked reconstruction example reports time, bytes read and compute.

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
The DS-1000 mini-200 corpus (`DS_1000_MINI_200` in `experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/agentic.py`, packages from `penfever/harbor-datasets@791c0607`) grades two ways that do not measure the candidate:

- A `solution.py` that calls `sys.exit(0)` scores 1 without running any assertion. `tests/test.sh` derives the reward from `run_test.py`'s exit code ([test.sh L17-L33](https://github.com/penfever/harbor-datasets/blob/791c0607c15a6d7946aa52e9c1a427d104fc0916/datasets/ds1000/3/tests/test.sh#L17-L33)), and `run_test.py` runs the test program under `except Exception` ([run_test.py L159-L179](https://github.com/penfever/harbor-datasets/blob/791c0607c15a6d7946aa52e9c1a427d104fc0916/datasets/ds1000/3/tests/run_test.py#L159-L179)), which does not catch `SystemExit`. Every task in the corpus shares this verifier.
- Task 701 scores 0 for every candidate, its own reference included. Its `exec_context` inserts the solution in front of `.numpy()`, and the reference ends with a newline, so the assembled program is a `SyntaxError`.

Reproduce:
1. In task 3's environment, write `import sys; sys.exit(0)` to `/workspace/solution/solution.py` and run `tests/test.sh`; `/logs/verifier/reward.txt` is `1`.
2. In task 701's environment, run `solution/solve.sh`, then `tests/test.sh`; the reward is `0` and the traceback is a `SyntaxError`.

Expected: reward 1 only when the test program's assertions pass, and every task passes with its reference solution.

`run_test.py` already writes `reward.txt` only after the assertions pass. Having `test.sh` keep that file instead of deriving the reward from the exit code, and counting a missing file as 0, closes the first problem; catching `SystemExit` alone would still let `os._exit(0)` through. Found by XiaoyuanWang111 in a review of #12147.

Their [`test.sh`](https://github.com/penfever/harbor-datasets/blob/791c0607c15a6d7946aa52e9c1a427d104fc0916/datasets/ds1000/3/tests/test.sh#L17-L33) overwrites the reward from the Python exit code, although [`run_test.py`](https://github.com/penfever/harbor-datasets/blob/791c0607c15a6d7946aa52e9c1a427d104fc0916/datasets/ds1000/3/tests/run_test.py#L159-L179) writes reward 1 only after assertions pass. `SystemExit` and `os._exit(0)` can therefore skip the assertions and still score 1. issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
A Daytona command request that returns HTTP 400 "failed to resolve container IP after 3 attempts: no IP address found. Is the Sandbox started?" escapes shellbox as a bare `DaytonaValidationError` and stops the whole evaluation run. The 400 means the sandbox could not be reached at that moment, but the evaluation worker doesn't recognize the error, so it treats it as permanent rather than retrying the attempt as an infrastructure failure.

A 500-task SWE-bench Verified run of Muse Glimmer 30B (mini-swe-agent on Daytona) stopped this way after about 3 hours, with more than 430 attempts finished. In the job log, a command's exec request failed with a transient `DaytonaError` ("Reattaching to a Daytona command after DaytonaError"). [`_exit_after_lost_request`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8b2261a308/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py#L385) then repeated the request, and the repeat returned the 400. [`_provider_failures`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8b2261a308/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py#L455-L476) re-raises a 4xx unchanged when a refresh still reports the sandbox as `STARTED`, so the error reached `run_evaluation`'s task group.

Reproduce:
1. Run an agentic evaluation on Daytona long enough that a sandbox briefly loses its container IP while still reporting `STARTED` (it happened in one of roughly 2,000 SWE-bench attempts across five models).
2. The run ends with `daytona.common.errors.DaytonaValidationError: Failed to execute command: bad request: failed to resolve container IP after 3 attempts: no IP address found. Is the Sandbox started?`

Expected: shellbox reports the unreachable sandbox as `MachineUnavailable` (or `ConnectionError`), and the evaluation worker retries the attempt as an infrastructure failure, as it does for a sandbox removed before it starts (#12268).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Research**

`DaytonaMachine.run()` retries a lost command request; the repeated request can return a 400 while the sandbox still reports `STARTED`. `_provider_failures()` probes the state but re-raises every started-sandbox 4xx, so this unreachable-sandbox response escapes as `DaytonaValidationError`.

**Relevant code**
- [`machine.py#L552-L568`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8b2261a3084e962281d72864210b6519a99a895c/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py#L552-L568) — command reattachment
- [`machine.py#L455-L476`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8b2261a3084e962281d72864210b6519a99a895c/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py#L455-L476) — provider error classification
- [`test_daytona_machine.py#L1197-L1240`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8b2261a3084e962281d72864210b6519a99a895c/lib/shellbox/tests/test_daytona_machine.py#L1197-L1240) — existing classification regression

**Proposed Fix**

After the state probe confirms `STARTED`, translate the 400 response containing `no IP address found` to `ConnectionError`. Keep other 4xx responses as validation errors, and add the reported response to the existing regression.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body: 🤖 The fix is in [PR #12322](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12322). The reported 400 now becomes `ConnectionError` when the sandbox remains `STARTED`; other 400 responses retain their validation error. The Daytona test file passes (110 tests), and the advisory lint review found no issues.

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body:
The Marin codebase needs to maintain a high level of quality to preserve development velocity. As agents have increased the rate of code production, the burden of doing code reviews has increased as well. While we don't demand code review for every PR, we still rely on it for important new code additions and to ensure code fits our guidelines.

One area we're particularly concerned about is slop. Agents produce "slop" in a way and scope well beyond a normal human coder: documentation or comments written in a bizarre style, oddly baroque abstractions, or repetitive coding practices. As a reviewer, it's frustrating and tiring to have to comment on slop code.

We have an initial set of agentic linting rules tied into our commit process that were mostly created from scratch. This proposes a weekly process to automatically refine and improve these rules based on observed reviewer feedback: rules which have never triggered are removed, and new rules introduced to capture common patterns, measured automatically and rolled out against a benchmarking set to ensure we don't regress.

## Current status

Our review process tracks findings by rule and user. Currently 3,672 findings across 61 distinct rules; the top 12 rules account for ~62% of findings, with the remaining 49 rules accounting for 37.4% (1,373).

Top rules by finding count:

| Rule | Findings | Share |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| ml-tuple-return-shape | 285 | 7.8% |
| ml-duplicate-logic-block | 277 | 7.5% |
| ml-magic-constant | 245 | 6.7% |
| ml-overloaded-function | 245 | 6.7% |
| ml-impl-narration-docstring | 244 | 6.6% |
| ml-slop-test | 243 | 6.6% |
| ml-unused-param | 216 | 5.9% |
| ml-echo-across-files | 154 | 4.2% |
| ml-module-globals | 108 | 2.9% |
| ml-env-var-vs-param | 97 | 2.6% |
| ml-duplicate-constant | 93 | 2.5% |
| ml-misleading-name | 92 | 2.5% |
| Remaining 49 rules | 1,373 | 37.4% |

A spot review shows these reviews are almost always acted on by the development agent, implying even the ad-hoc reviews have saved thousands of user interactions. Despite this, we still regularly post PRs full of agentic slop, with plenty of room for improvement.

## Proposal

Two levers:

- **Better enforcement:** auto-reject PRs that don't have the `agentic-review` tag assigned to them. This should force agents that forgot the agentic review process to trigger review.
- **Better quality:** every human comment on a PR is something that *could* have been caught during agentic PR review. Analyze these weekly and identify the comment types that recur most frequently and are easiest to resolve.

## Approach

- Move statistics out of WandB and into Finelog via a bulk import & CLI adjustments
- Add a Grafana dashboard for monitoring & alerting rules as appropriate
- Set up a weekly GitHub action which:
  - **Fetch:** all PRs with comments in the last week
  - **Triage:** which comments are actionable for linting
  - **Review:** which rules haven't fired for > 1 month
  - **Adopt:** new rules which would have captured the failure patterns

## Success criteria

- A live dashboard on Grafana showing agentic code review feedback statistics, including triggers, feedback quality metrics, timing (too slow a feedback loop and users get impatient), and any issues we run into
- Weekly report sent to Slack with our PR statistics
- A codified, tentatively weekly, auto-improvement process for our agentic linting patterns

Long-term success metric: *does the number of PR comments that could have been caught by agentic linting go down over time?* This is not a hard metric — it will fluctuate as coding standards change and as agents get more powerful — but in general we want to see it go down.

## Rollout

Bulk upload of all agentic lint data into Finelog with the initial rollout, then set up GitHub actions for the maintenance loop.

## Expected timeframe

~1 day of work, which can be overlapped with other ongoing projects.

## Alternatives considered

**Do nothing.** Rejected: this is a low-effort way to reduce human reviewer load.

**Adopt some external service.** Rejected: lack of a self-reinforcement cycle, and an initial survey found no external service provided significantly higher value.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 Research

The Finelog migration is live, but [`review.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1ce93369edc85d24e9b38bbac3f7e560e8548815/infra/codehealth/review.py) has no scheduled caller and the latest classified human-review rows are from June 24. The current [PR review workflow](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1ce93369edc85d24e9b38bbac3f7e560e8548815/.github/workflows/ops-claude-review.yaml) launches two Claude jobs, while the [commit workflow](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1ce93369edc85d24e9b38bbac3f7e560e8548815/.agents/skills/commit/SKILL.md) leaves no durable proof that its local agentic lint pass ran. I found no open PR overlapping #8738.

Proposed Fix

The first PR will replace the Claude jobs with a secretless, workload-federated Weaver review; require the `agentic-lint` label that the commit workflow adds after its local review; schedule aggregation and reporting; and preserve inline diff context when classifying review comments. It will include behavior tests and update the [code-health operator documentation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1ce93369edc85d24e9b38bbac3f7e560e8548815/infra/codehealth/README.md). The benchmark corpus, rule refinement engine, and the one-month no-exposure removal policy will follow in a second PR.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 Research

The current PR proves complete GitHub review collection, but it rebuilds an archive for each run and hard-codes matching, analysis, and report rendering. The survey needed repeated thread inspection and rule probing, so those judgments belong to an exploratory agent. The shared `marin-metadata` PostgreSQL service can persist the 30-day review window and incremental cursors directly; no GCS corpus archive is required.

Proposed Fix

Rewrite #8747 around PostgreSQL-backed review and lint activity, structured YAML lint rules, and bounded agent tools for listing PRs/comments, fetching comment context, and probing a selected rule with a caller-selected model and effort. The scheduled agent will edit catalog YAML, open a normal templated PR, author its own Loom report and charts, and send the report link to `marin-eng`; fixed feedback matching and report-rendering code will be removed.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
Serve Snowball (67B-A2B) on TPU with vLLM, using data-parallel replicas and long context. This issue groups the TPU serving work from 2026-11-19 to 2026-11-20. Session routing (vllm-router) is tracked in the sub-issue https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11856.

## Changes

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| [PR 11780](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11780): single-host data parallelism and the session router on TPU ([sub-issue](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11856)) | Draft, CI green |
| [tpu-inference PR 36](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/pull/36): give each data-parallel rank the right chips on v4/v5p | Draft, needs review |
| [vllm-project/tpu-inference PR 4010](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/pull/4010): the same fix upstream | Draft |
| [PR 11781](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11781): pin tpu-inference to the fix | Draft; re-pin after fork PR 36 merges |

## Results

- **v4/v5p chip fix:** `get_num_cores_per_chip()` returns 2 on v4/v5p, but JAX exposes one device per chip (Megacore). Each DP rank therefore got half its chips, and TP>1 with DP>1 failed with "Insufficient devices for 2D mesh". With the fix, Snowball v0.1 on v5p-8 with TP=2/DP=2 served 16/16 requests over 8 sessions. Each rank had a 1.9M-token KV cache.
- **Launch settings that work for Snowball:** `--memory 400g --wait-timeout 3600`, and load the tokenizer from the HF repo. With a `gs://` model and DP>1, the API servers rewrite one shared tokenizer folder at the same time.

## Offloading and context

- tpu-inference supports one kind of offload: a host-RAM **KV prefix cache** (`TPUOffloadConnector`). It reloads KV blocks on a prefix hit, but one request's live KV must still fit in HBM, so it does not raise maximum context. Marin has not tried it with Snowball.
- The TPU platform rejects LMCache and the other generic vLLM KV connectors. There is no weight offload (`cpu_offload_gb`, sleep mode).
- Snowball was served on TPU at up to `max_model_len` 73,728 (v6e-8, v5p-8, v4-32). That was an eval-policy choice matching H100, not an HBM limit: v5p-8 had a 6.8M-token KV cache. 131K or 262K has not been tried.

## Related

- [Issue 11216](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11216): completions corrupt when the KV cache fills.
- [Issue 9751](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9751): tpu-inference fork refresh blocked.
- [PR 10854](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10854): sliding-window fix for TPU serving.

## Next

1. Review and merge tpu-inference PR 36, re-pin PR 11781 to the merged SHA, and land PR 11781 after PR 11780.
2. Serve Snowball at 131K and 262K context on v5p-8 on the final pin, and compare a long-context eval against H100.
3. Try `TPUOffloadConnector` on a multi-turn workload, and measure prefix-hit rate and latency.

The reported v5p-8 TP=2/DP=2 Snowball run served 16/16 requests, but 131K/262K context and `TPUOffloadConnector` remain untested.

Plan:
1. Review and land [tpu-inference #36](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/pull/36). Re-pin #11781 to the merged fork `main` SHA and rerun its TPU qualification. Land #11780, then #11781.

Record whether each run boots, the longest successful prompt plus generation, per-rank KV capacity, and any failure. spillover_issues.author: gonzalobenegas
spillover_issues.body:
**Training passed SAMPLE qualification on the feature branch. Code review and publication to the shared RL Data Atlas are pending.** Atlas admitted all 47,118 retained training tasks from NVIDIA Litmus-Bench v0.2 and included the source in the branch’s default training selection. All 2,056 validation tasks remain held out for evaluation. [Tested commit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/72f06904b813d4fb7f73737da3ea5b4b3a7b7875) · [Split declarations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/72f06904b813d4fb7f73737da3ea5b4b3a7b7875/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/litmus/tasks.py)

- **Quality review.** GLM‑5.3 returned 97 conclusive reviews and 3 invalid responses on the fixed panel of 100 training tasks. The verdict was **GOOD**. An independent check confirmed the upstream answer on the one flagged task. [SAMPLE receipt reference](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/72f06904b813d4fb7f73737da3ea5b4b3a7b7875/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/sample_qc_receipts/part-005.json) · [Review and adjudication](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12304#issuecomment-7176523699)
- **Training loader.** All 32 selected tasks matched the pinned training split by both task ID and rendered prompt. Across all 2,056 validation rows, there were **zero matching IDs and zero matching prompts**. The earlier lexical scan flagged zero rows in either split. [Loader verification](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12304#issuecomment-7178543242) · [Decontamination and retained counts](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12304#issuecomment-7174907853)
- **Code checks.** Pre-commit passed. The scoped suite had 36 passes and three failures. The same three tests failed on the integration base. [Test comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12304#issuecomment-7178543242) · [Integration base](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/72a5a494ca931b1dd4b400318a7b08a1e0c3fe2a)

## Checklist

- [ ] Open a pull request for code review.
- [ ] Publish separate TRAIN and EVAL entries in the shared Atlas and verify the published entries.
- [x] Report retained counts and verify that training selection excludes validation.
- [x] Preserve the prompts, per-question licenses, and answer-matching rules. Compare the converted grader with NVIDIA’s verifier on accepted and rejected answers covering each question family. [NeMo Gym benchmark and verifier](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Gym/tree/e87f88065db6105548194e1f12feea720c129cca/benchmarks/litmus-bench) [Packaged grader controls](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12304#issuecomment-7172696340)
- [x] Measure v0.2 training-question overlap with the v0.1 training set. Report the matching rule, overlap count, and distinct v0.2 questions before claiming additional training coverage. [v0.1 comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12304#issuecomment-7172060933)

## Dataset background

NVIDIA’s Litmus-Bench v0.2 expands molecular-property questions with experimental drug-property data from Biogen and ExpansionRx. The existing Atlas entry, `laion/nemotron-gym-litmus-bench-v2`, packages 5,232 training questions from NVIDIA v0.1. Its `-v2` suffix refers to a Task Trove packaging revision. [Pinned NVIDIA release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-RL-litmus-bench-v0.2/tree/c180425444ebcc6db8dafdb897e51a94927df62a) · [LAION conversion code](https://github.com/open-thoughts/OpenThoughts-Agent/blob/6896d0037a6c03fa39df675260e80b6d2e807a73/data/nemotron_gym/converters/litmus_bench.py)

The training target is **SAMPLE** quality. Validation remains **EVAL**. Atlas qualification, retained counts and publication are pending.

spillover_issues.author: asartran
spillover_issues.body:
The RL unit tests in `experiments/post_training/rl_tests/` spend most of their time starting SkyRL subprocesses. They took 21.9 min of the 120 min of test time in a full run of every unit suite on Nov 25 (18%, in 124 tests), and they run on most post-training PRs.

Each `rl_gate.compose_configs` call runs `_native_json("python", "-c", program, ...)` in a fresh process in SkyRL's CPU environment. Measured on a development machine with the two heaviest tests, `test_rl.py::test_submission_exit_codes_and_publication_retries` (13 cases) and `test_rl_gate.py::test_gate_compares_recorded_configuration_and_defaults` (18 cases):

| Measurement | Value |
|---|---|
| Composition subprocesses in those 31 cases | 96 |
| Unique after normalizing temporary paths and attempt IDs | 94 |
| Time in those subprocesses | 743 s of about 1,000 s, 7.7 s per call |
| SkyRL Python start-up plus imports of `cloud.iris.launch_config`, `skyrl_train` and `marinskyrl` alone | 3.3-4.0 s warm, 6.4 s cold |

Because 94 of 96 compositions are unique, caching results across cases would save about 9 s. Roughly half of each call is process start-up and imports, which every call repeats.

Done when:
- the RL tests stop paying SkyRL start-up for every composition, for example through one long-lived SkyRL process per test session or lighter imports in the composed program, and
- the full `rl_tests` folder's test time in CI drops accordingly, measured with `--durations` on a full unit run.

A test-only prototype of the long-lived process is in #12343 for discussion.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`rl_gate.compose_configs()` calls `_native_json()`, which starts a fresh SkyRL CPU Python process for every composition. The issue measures 743 seconds in 96 calls across two parameterized tests; 94 compositions are unique. Draft [#12343](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12343) already prototypes a session-scoped worker at this boundary, so another implementation PR would duplicate active work.

**Relevant code**
- [`rl_gate.py#L661-L702`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/post_training/rl_gate.py#L661-L702) — subprocess boundary and composition program.
- [`rl_tests/conftest.py#L4-L12`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/post_training/rl_tests/conftest.py#L4-L12) — shared test fixtures.
- [`unified-unit.yaml#L39-L54`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.github/workflows/unified-unit.yaml#L39-L54) — PR tests are selected from the diff.

# Proposed Fix

1. Continue #12343. Compare fresh-process and persistent-worker results for consecutive distinct launch files, including configuration defaults and failure mapping. Exercise worker exit, timeout, and the existing `subprocess.run` replacement cases; repeated composition must not retain Hydra or other process-global state.
2. Run the complete `experiments/post_training/rl_tests/` unit folder on matched baseline and PR environments with `--durations=20`. Report total folder time and both named slow tests; diff-selected PR CI alone does not measure the requested full-folder improvement.

spillover_issues.author: hammer
spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

Six changes to make Marin's anti-slop tooling enforce what it finds and report whether it works. They come from comparing Marin's practice with the [No AI Slop manifesto](https://www.slopmanifesto.com). The full comparison, with citations, is [here](https://gistpreview.github.io/?b91c964142d07072e5b0183d38412bb3).

## Background

The review-to-lint loop from #8738 and #8747 runs every week and opens rule PRs such as #9503 and #9754. It has some gaps:

- **Advisory only.** The `ml-*` rules are judged by an LLM and never block a merge. #9463 made lint review best-effort.
- **Low recall.** On real review context the rules scored 1/17 positive recall (#8747).
- **No retirement.** No rule has been retired.
- **No reporting.** Nobody reports whether the number of catchable human comments is going down.
- **Lapsing epic.** #8738 got a stale warning on 2026-11-23.

Branch protection requires one approval from anyone. The Pulumi config sets `require_code_owner_reviews=False`, and the repo has no CODEOWNERS file. The review policy issue #2304 closed as stale. #8422 removed the rule that a PR over 500 LOC needs a spec.

## Proposed work

1. **Deterministic checks first.** For each `ml-*` rule, the weekly refinement agent should ask whether a ruff rule, AST check or grep could express it. Where one can, it should open a PR that adds a blocking check to `infra/pre-commit.py`.
   - Start with a data-size guard and with raw `gs://` paths in training data.
   - #11548 replaced the large-data guard with the advisory `ml-committed-data` rule, because a fixed byte limit can't tell a dataset shard from a fixture. A shrink-only allowlist may cover that case. If it can't, record why.
2. **Review policy and CODEOWNERS.**
   - Write a short review policy, for example `docs/dev-guide/review-policy.md`. It should name the high-stakes areas: training and data pipelines, Iris and Zephyr, and evals.
   - Add a CODEOWNERS file so those paths need their owner's approval, and turn on `require_code_owner_reviews` in the Pulumi branch-protection config.
   - State that bot accounts never count as the required approval.
3. **PR size warning.** Warn in CI when an `agent-generated` PR changes more than about 500 non-generated lines without a linked design issue.
4. **`ml-multi-topic-pr` rule.** Add a meta-lane rule that flags unrelated changes bundled into one PR.
5. **Prune agent docs.** Extend the weekly lint loop to AGENTS.md and `.agents/skills/`. It should propose deleting instructions that no review comment or rule data still supports.
6. **Finish #8738.**
   - Publish live-context recall for each rule.
   - Retire rules that never fire.
   - Post the weekly report somewhere people read it, such as Slack `marin-eng`. Today it goes only to a Loom channel.

## Done when

- [ ] `infra/pre-commit.py` has blocking checks for committed data size and raw `gs://` training paths, and the refinement agent's template asks the deterministic-check question for each rule.
- [ ] The review policy doc and CODEOWNERS file have landed, and branch protection requires code-owner review on the listed paths.
- [ ] CI warns on large `agent-generated` PRs that have no linked design issue.
- [ ] `ml-multi-topic-pr` is in the lint catalog.
- [ ] The weekly loop has opened at least one PR that deletes or trims AGENTS.md or skill text, backed by evidence.
- [ ] The weekly report shows recall for each rule and the trend in catchable comments, has retired at least one never-firing rule, and is delivered to a channel the team reads.

Related: #8738, #8747, #9463, #11548, #11657, #2304, #8422, #6424.

comments.body:
🤖 # Research

This is a coordinated code-health rollout, not one small fix. For committed data, main still has only a 500 KiB per-file check; `ml-committed-data` is advisory, both main-branch protection declarations disable code-owner review, and the weekly agent publishes a Loom report without a Slack route or a labeled recall measure. [PR #11657](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11657) already adds an advisory raw-training-path rule, and [PR #12155](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12155) corrects refinement exposure counts; the proposed work should build on those PRs.

**Relevant code**
- [`pre-commit.py#L325`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bf4b85caa09586d287b503bfa3e9f9d19393424b/infra/pre-commit.py#L325) — existing file-size gate.
- [`ml-committed-data.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bf4b85caa09586d287b503bfa3e9f9d19393424b/infra/lint/rules/cruft/ml-committed-data.yaml) — advisory data rule.
- [`dependency_updater.py#L193`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bf4b85caa09586d287b503bfa3e9f9d19393424b/infra/pulumi/src/iac/github/dependency_updater.py#L193) — classic protection and ruleset.
- [`ops-codehealth-refinement.yaml#L32`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bf4b85caa09586d287b503bfa3e9f9d19393424b/.github/workflows/ops-codehealth-refinement.yaml#L32) — weekly agent instructions.
- [`refinement_tools.py#L210`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bf4b85caa09586d287b503bfa3e9f9d19393424b/infra/codehealth/refinement_tools.py#L210) — current rule-exposure output.

# Plan

Land this in separate PRs, each with behavior tests and the repository's commit, lint-review, and CI workflow:

1. **Blocking checks and rule selection.** Add focused checks to `infra/pre-commit.py`: a shrink-only baseline for existing committed data, with new dataset shards and renamed dumps rejected while test fixtures remain allowed; and an AST check for literal `gs://` training *components* at the SFT configuration boundary, with outputs and versioned `adopt()`/`pretokenized()` inputs allowed. Use #11657's rule and examples as the boundary definition. Add positive and allowed-case tests before enabling either check in `marin-lint.yaml`. Update the weekly agent instructions and refinement PR template to ask, for every proposed `ml-*` rule, whether Ruff, AST, or a precise text check can enforce it; record why an advisory rule remains advisory when none can.

2. **Review ownership and protection.** Add `docs/dev-guide/review-policy.md` and `.github/CODEOWNERS` for training/data, Iris, Zephyr, and eval paths. Confirm actual maintainers or teams, valid CODEOWNERS resolution, and existing bypass actors before turning on code-owner review in both the classic protection and `protect main` ruleset. State that bot approvals do not satisfy the required human review. Run a Pulumi preview and verify on a test PR that a changed owned path requests its owner, an unrelated approval does not satisfy the owner requirement, and bot approval does not satisfy the human requirement. If GitHub's native rules do not provide the last guarantee, specify and test the additional required check before rollout.

3. **PR warning and meta rule.** Add a non-blocking CI job for `agent-generated` PRs with more than 500 added/deleted non-generated lines and no linked design issue; run it on PR changes and label changes. Count from the PR diff against its base, use an explicit generated-path list, and report the count and missing design link in the job summary. Add `ml-multi-topic-pr` to the meta lane with examples that distinguish unrelated work from necessary multi-file changes. Test the threshold, generated-file exclusion, design-link recognition, and label-triggered rerun.

4. **Measured weekly loop.** After #12155 lands, add an independently labeled live-context benchmark so each rule's report shows positive recall as `caught / eligible positives`, negative specificity, and the sample size; do not treat probe output or zero findings as recall. Report the weekly count and per-reviewed-PR rate of catchable human comments with stable window definitions. Use current-catalog eligible-run counts when nominating never-firing rules for retirement, then remove at least one with enough exposure and documented counterexamples. Extend the same evidence review to `AGENTS.md` and skill instructions, and open a separate deletion or trimming PR only where the instruction lacks supporting review or rule evidence. Route the existing versioned Loom report to `marin-eng` and verify delivery from a manual weekly run.

Open decision before PR 2: which human maintainers or GitHub teams own each CODEOWNERS path? That assignment determines whether code-owner review can be enabled without blocking routine PRs.

spillover_issues.author: chrismc91
spillover_issues.body:
Marin has few coding evals outside Python. [SWE-bench Multilingual](https://www.swebench.com/multilingual.html) has 300 GitHub issues from real repositories in nine languages: C, C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, Ruby and Rust. The agent edits the repository to resolve the issue, and the task's hidden tests decide pass or fail.

The tasks are the Harbor registry dataset `swebench_multilingual@1.0`, pinned to laude-institute/harbor-datasets at `19fb29e2` and lowered into curated TaskSpec corpora (#11664). The agent is Terminus 2 with 16,384-token replies, each task's 50-minute agent limit, and a 4-CPU, 8 GB Daytona sandbox built from the task's image, pinned by digest. The default `swebench-multilingual` evaluation runs a fixed 100-task subset, drawn at random within each language in proportion to its share of the 300. `swebench-multilingual-full` runs all 300 and `swebench-multilingual-lite` runs two. None is in a suite.

Qwen reports 67.2% for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and 60.3% for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on the full set, from its own scaffold at 200K context. Full 300-task runs with Terminus 2 at 131K context, through Harbor, scored [61.3%](https://evaldash.oa.dev/runs/swebml-v2-resume-qwen36-20261118-swebench-multilingual-2288a5fcb8c250fdbb665205ce566dae) and [53.3%](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fevals%2Fswebml-v2-qwen35-20261117-swebench-multilingual-58a70d9ee3f95aeaabb1af1772a9eeb5%2Fresults): 6 to 7 points below the reported scores, in the same order. The gold patches of 299 of the 300 tasks pass in declarative-build sandboxes.

The curated port reproduces those Harbor runs. On the 100-task subset, with 131K context and thinking on:

| Model | Curated | Harbor | Paired difference | Same outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Muse Glimmer 30B](https://evaldash.oa.dev/runs/swebml-cur-glimmer-20261124-swebench-multilingual-9094c551ee1b52da89b3b6fa9de6608d) | 66% | 66% | +0.0 ± 3.8 | 86 of 100 |
| [Qwen3.6-35B-A3B](https://evaldash.oa.dev/runs/swebml-cur-qwen36-20261124-swebench-multilingual-1bd2b3c4468f59f7a58d14fa78ddb36b) | 57% | 59% | −2.0 ± 4.7 | 78 of 100 |
| [Nemotron 3.5 Super](https://evaldash.oa.dev/runs/swebml-cur-nemotron-super-20261124-swebench-multilingual-150746fb7b115b4999f812a538e4a01d) | 64% | 59% | +5.0 ± 3.9 | 85 of 100 |
| Snowball v0.1 | not run | 10% | | |

Differences are per task, in points, with standard errors; disagreeing tasks flip in both directions. Every curated attempt was graded. Agents hit the 50-minute limit on 3, 8 and 2 tasks; those are graded on the changes made. The Qwen3.6 inference worker was preempted seven times during its run. Snowball's Harbor score reflects its replies: 83% of its turns were malformed, against 10% for Glimmer and 2% for Nemotron.

The subset trades precision for a third of the cost. In 5,000 simulated stratified draws over two full Qwen runs, the subset score was within 7 points of the full score 90% of the time, and the two models swapped order in 3.8% of draws.

| Run | GPUs | H100-hours |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Glimmer, 100 tasks | 2 H100 | 2.8 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Super, 100 tasks | 4 H100 | 5.5 |
| Qwen3.6, 300 tasks (Harbor) | 4 H100 | 21.0 |

Each run uses 32 concurrent attempts.

The dataset is MIT-licensed; each task's repository keeps its upstream license.

spillover_issues.author: chrismc91
spillover_issues.body:
Curated evaluation grading uses memory in proportion to request concurrency times each task's verifier files, and a grader that runs out of memory loses the whole run. LiveCodeBench Pro (in development: 678 Codeforces problems, each graded against its test archive, mean about 20 MiB) was OOM-killed (exit 137) in the 12 GiB `curated-eval` job at the default concurrency of 64 after all generation had finished. The run is unrecoverable, and the only workaround is lowering `evaluation_num_concurrent` per model, which also throttles inference. At concurrency 16 the same job peaked at 7.2 GiB (Finelog `iris.task` `memory_peak_mb`) over its first 3.5 hours of grading.

Three properties of the current design combine here, and each affects every benchmark with large verifier files, not only LiveCodeBench Pro.

Grading is admitted by the inference bound. Each of `concurrency` consumers generates and then grades in one coroutine, behind a queue of `2 * concurrency` whole cases (`lib/marin/src/marin/rollouts/evaluation.py:916`). Each case carries its `TaskSpec` with resources as base64 strings, so about `3 * concurrency` task payloads (around 5 GiB at 64 × 20 MiB, estimated from code, not measured) are resident before staging. Staging then copies each payload again: decoded bytes held for the whole grade (`taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py:673`, `runtime/staging.py:24`), a `grading.tar`, and a second tar built in a `BytesIO` for upload (`shellbox/backends/local/machine.py:388`). The default local verifier has no memory cap (`marin/evaluation/task_worker.py:134-141`), so graded programs share the same 12 GiB. Raising the job's memory is not a fix: #11662 lowered it from 32g to 12g because a 32g worker waited over an hour to schedule.

Large files can only live inline in the task. `TaskResource.source` accepts only `InlineFile`, and the TaskCompendium README defers the alternative: "Shared external files are deferred until a `TaskSet` contract defines their location and loading" (`lib/taskcompendium/README.md:244`). Benchmarks raise the 1 MB `resource_budget_bytes` default instead (LongBench 128 MiB, long-context 64 MiB; LiveCodeBench Pro needs 400 MiB), which admits the task without reserving anything to grade it. The same representation is why attempts needed `--task-evidence reference` (#11661) and benchmark-declared evidence defaults (#11885): embedded copies of LiveCodeBench tasks pushed a TPU run past the 10 GB cross-region budget.

A failed grader job is lost work. `curated-eval` runs with `max_retries_failure=0` (`marin/evaluation/dataset_evaluator.py:200`). A saved generation is reused only for an attempt that finished with an infrastructure error (`rollouts/evaluation.py:323`), so a kill between generation and the grade commit discards the model turn, and `--resume-results-path` accepts only Harbor evaluations (`experiments/evaluation/cli.py:265`).

A possible score effect, not measured: 64 compile-and-run graders on 8 CPUs with wall limits of twice each problem's time limit may fail correct solutions, while `concurrency` is excluded from run identity.

Proposed direction, for discussion:

1. Bound grading separately from inference in `run_evaluation`. Queue row locators rather than whole cases, load a task when its attempt starts, and admit grades against verifier needs the benchmark declares (CPU, peak memory, scratch), with the worker's `ResourceSpec` derived from the same declaration.
2. Add an external file kind to `TaskResource`: large files published once beside the corpus by sha256, with size and path, and streamed to disk at staging. Small files stay inline. This defines the deferred `TaskSet` file contract, removes the large budget overrides, and makes task-evidence modes unnecessary.
3. Persist the model turn before grading, add same-output resume for curated runs, then allow bounded retries of the grader job.

Done when: a benchmark with multi-hundred-MiB verifier files runs at the default model concurrency on the default grader job without per-model overrides, and a grader job killed after generation resumes without regenerating.

cc @rjpower

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

The 12 GiB OOM has three reinforcing causes: `run_evaluation` queues full cases at twice model concurrency, generation and grading occupy the same consumers, and staging holds decoded verifier bytes while Shellbox builds another tar in memory. The default verifier has no memory cap; a killed Iris job cannot resume a generated turn unless its attempt already finished with an infrastructure error. This crosses the corpus format, TaskCompendium staging, RolloutEngine, and the curated launch path, so it needs staged implementation rather than one configuration change.

**Relevant code**
- [`evaluation.py#L932-L1004`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4ae83a5f6c4e665b4fb3d1cd0209b40dda046760/lib/marin/src/marin/rollouts/evaluation.py#L932-L1004) — full-case queue and shared consumers
- [`engine.py#L106-L171`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4ae83a5f6c4e665b4fb3d1cd0209b40dda046760/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/engine.py#L106-L171) — generation and grade in one attempt
- [`staging.py#L24-L55`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4ae83a5f6c4e665b4fb3d1cd0209b40dda046760/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/staging.py#L24-L55) — decoded bytes and tar staging
- [`models.py#L269-L303`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4ae83a5f6c4e665b4fb3d1cd0209b40dda046760/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/models.py#L269-L303) — inline-only resource contract
- [`dataset_evaluator.py#L188-L200`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4ae83a5f6c4e665b4fb3d1cd0209b40dda046760/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/dataset_evaluator.py#L188-L200) — 12 GiB job, zero failure retries

# Proposed Fix

1. **Resource contract and staging.** Add a content-addressed file reference under the immutable corpus root, with digest and byte length, alongside `InlineFile`. The publisher writes large files once; the corpus reader resolves references against that root and verifies length and digest. Stage from a stream into the grader archive and stream local-machine upload, keeping whole verifier files out of Python byte buffers. Update resource inventory, build-context consumers, and role isolation together; [#11958](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11958) changes the same inventory code.
2. **Separate admission and durable generation.** Queue selected row locators, prompt-variant choices, and trial metadata, then load the case only while it is used. Expose a generation/grade boundary in RolloutEngine and commit a generation-complete record to FineStore before grading; resume from that record without another model request. Add typed CPU, memory, and scratch requirements to `EvaluationProtocol`; use them for both weighted grader admission and verifier-machine limits. Keep model concurrency at 64. For graders that must reuse the agent machine, reserve grader capacity before starting that machine until a machine handoff can preserve its state across the boundary.
3. **Restart the curated worker.** Expose same-output resume for curated runs, retain the existing run-identity check, and enable bounded Iris job retries only after generation checkpoints and grade commits are idempotent. A restart skips terminal attempts and grades saved generations. The separate [Taskforge checkpoint PR #12139](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12139) is a useful precedent, but it does not cover this evaluator.

Test the resource resolver with a corrupted or missing blob, enforce the declared grade budget with concurrent synthetic large files, and inject a worker kill after a generation checkpoint to assert zero repeated model calls and one terminal grade. Then run LiveCodeBench Pro at model concurrency 64 on the 8 CPU/12 GiB worker: record `iris.task.memory_peak_mb`, complete all 678 grades, regrade the same saved responses at lower grading concurrency to check score equivalence, and restart a killed grader from the same results path. The memory estimate and any score effect from grader contention remain unmeasured until that run.

spillover_issues.author: chrismc91
spillover_issues.body:
Launching several jobs that depend on the same uncached steps can fail one or more of them while checking a step's cache. On 2026-11-25, four Muse Glimmer eval jobs submitted within a minute of each other to cw-rno2a all built the same corpus and environment-image steps. Three failed, each on a different shared step:

```
s3fs.utils.FileExpired: [Errno 16] The remote file corresponding to filename
marin-us-east-08a/marin/data/eval/evalchemy-humanevalplus-1b269fdacec9ae28/2026.11.08.1/.executor_info
and Etag "b577a9cbcda68fc5563f773317429074" no longer exists.
```

The read is `StepRunner._launch_step` → `check_drift` → `read_record` → `_read_text` ([artifact.py:231](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/263527428c/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/artifact.py#L231)). s3fs records the object's ETag when it opens the file and fails if the object is replaced before the ranged read. Another job is evidently rewriting `.executor_info` between those two calls. The failed steps were `data/eval/evalchemy-humanevalplus-…`, `data/eval/harbor-bfcl-parity-1.0-pi-…` and `images/env-f25fb7e6001aef22`. The fourth job and the relaunched ones succeeded once the steps were cached.

Reproduce:
1. Choose eval selections whose corpus steps are not yet cached.
2. Submit several eval jobs that depend on them at the same moment, for example `experiments.evaluation.policy.cli launch --all-candidates`.

Expected: a job that finds a shared step being built by another job waits for it or reads it again, rather than failing.

`--all-candidates` submits one job per candidate at once, so a cold cache makes this likely for policy launches.

**Relevant code**
- [`artifact.py#L286-L302`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/artifact.py#L286-L302) — legacy sidecar fallback.

Check status before reading drift metadata in the launcher, worker, and pruned-cache path. Read the record only for a successful cache entry, while still rebuilding mutable versions; cover the cold-cache case with an incomplete sidecar regression test.

spillover_issues.author: chrismc91
spillover_issues.body:
An agent attempt that reaches its time limit can lose its Daytona task machine before grading. The attempt is then recorded as a grading infrastructure error instead of being graded on what the agent left. In SWE-bench-Science runs on Daytona with a 1-second agent limit, this happened to 2 of 119 attempts (tasks 081 and 094) and, in a rerun, 4 of 96 (tasks 030, 050, 064 and 073), all different tasks. Each stopped with `total_turn_timeout`, and grading failed within a millisecond with `MachineTerminated: The Daytona machine was closed after CancelledError()`. The other attempts were graded normally.

The likely path is in `DaytonaMachine.run` (`lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py`). A cancellation that arrives while a command is running goes through `_cleanup_cancelled_command`, which deliberately keeps the machine open so the verifier can still grade ("Keeping the machine available lets the verifier grade work from commands that already finished"). A cancellation that arrives a moment later, while the `finally` block removes the finished command's files, takes the `except asyncio.CancelledError` branch around `_remove_command_files` and calls `_close_preserving_failure(cancellation)`. That closes the whole machine. The engine then grades on the closed machine; the first command (Pier's `pre_artifacts.sh` collect step here) raises `MachineTerminated`, and the attempt is recorded with operation `grade`. The same race applies to any agent stopped by a turn, attempt or wall limit, so full runs can lose gradable attempts at random.

A related gap: cleanup after a cancellation has no overall time bound. `_cleanup_cancelled_command` and `close` each wait on several Daytona calls (`_stop_command`, `_remove_command_files`, session and keepalive teardown, `AsyncDaytona.close`), and `finish_owned` absorbs further cancellations until they finish. The engine bounds machine closes it owns with `cleanup_timeout`, but the cleanup inside `run` is not covered, so a Daytona call that stalls there can hold an attempt past its deadline. This was not observed; an overnight "hang" that first looked like it was turned out to be the laptop sleeping, which pauses the monotonic clock every deadline uses on macOS.

Suggested direction: treat a cancellation during command-file removal like one during the command, leaving the machine open, and pass one remaining-time budget through cancellation cleanup and `close` so that each attempt ends within its deadline plus `cleanup_timeout`.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

`DaytonaMachine.run()` preserves the sandbox when cancellation interrupts command execution, but cancellation during its `finally` file removal calls `_close_preserving_failure()`. Grading then sees `MachineTerminated` even though the command has finished. The draft Daytona v2 migration in #12039 retains the same cancellation branch; it does not resolve this race.

**Relevant code**
- [`machine.py#L426-L445`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py#L426-L445) — cancellation cleanup keeps the sandbox
- [`machine.py#L598-L616`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py#L598-L616) — file-removal cancellation closes it
- [`process_session.py#L53-L62`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/process_session.py#L53-L62) — owned cleanup survives repeated cancellation

# Proposed Fix

On cancellation during file removal, run the existing cancellation cleanup and propagate the original cancellation while keeping the sandbox available for grading. Add a local Daytona regression that cancels the first removal and successfully grades on the same machine. Keep this PR scoped to the observed grading race and carry the correction into #12039 before it merges.

The separate unobserved deadline risk needs one cleanup budget shared by command stop, file removal, session teardown, and Daytona client close. First add a fake provider call that stalls at each phase; then thread the remaining `cleanup_timeout` through those phases and prove each attempt finishes within the budget while preserving the original cancellation and recording incomplete cleanup. This should be reviewed as a follow-up because it changes machine-close semantics beyond this race.

comments.body: 🤖 PR #12279 fixes the observed grading race: cancellation during command file removal now finishes cleanup and leaves a completed task machine available to the verifier. The Daytona regression passed locally (109 tests in `test_daytona_machine.py`); #12277 remains open for the shared cleanup deadline described above. PR #12039 still needs this correction in its v2 backend before merging.

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
Concurrent SkyRL jobs can start on the same Iris host. Some Ray services require a concrete TCP port before the service binds it. Two launchers can choose the same free port during that interval, even when their pods have separate filesystems. PR #12313 holds a host-network lease for those listeners in `vendor/skyrl/cloud/iris/ray_ports.py`.

Move the lease primitive into Iris and make SkyRL call it. Keep the mapping of Ray services to their supported port modes in SkyRL. Explicit Iris allocations must still take precedence, and Ray services that accept a kernel-assigned port should still receive zero.

Cover two independent launchers sharing a network namespace. They should receive distinct ports while their leases overlap, skip occupied ports, and release their claims when the launcher exits, including after a crash.

[PR review requesting the follow-up](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12313#issuecomment-7180835193)

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

PR #12313 implements host-network leases in SkyRL's [`ray_ports.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7a1ae6ed8b3120862f3ac1f941d72284a65033e0/vendor/skyrl/cloud/iris/ray_ports.py#L36-L101). The generic candidate scan and abstract Unix socket claim sit beside Ray-specific port policy, so another Iris caller cannot reuse the claim. Iris's [`find_free_port`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2de6fcd77775426aecfc8c9c7c78cbc7db8a5d99/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/types.py#L70-L97) returns a port after closing its TCP probe; it does not hold a cross-process lease.

**Relevant code**
- [`ray_ports.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7a1ae6ed8b3120862f3ac1f941d72284a65033e0/vendor/skyrl/cloud/iris/ray_ports.py) — allocation and Ray policy
- [`task_runtime.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7a1ae6ed8b3120862f3ac1f941d72284a65033e0/vendor/skyrl/cloud/iris/task_runtime.py#L2387) — lease lifetime
- [`test_ray_ports.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7a1ae6ed8b3120862f3ac1f941d72284a65033e0/vendor/skyrl/cloud/iris/tests/test_ray_ports.py) — concurrent launcher coverage

# Proposed Fix

Move candidate selection and the socket lease into a public Iris runtime module. Have SkyRL request leases only for services requiring concrete ports, keep explicit Iris allocations and native zero modes unchanged, and hold the leases around Ray's lifetime. Add Iris tests using independent processes to check overlapping claims, occupied ports, release on normal exit, and release after a killed launcher. Stack the follow-up on #12313 until it merges.

comments.body: 🤖 PR #12361 moves host-network port leases into Iris and leaves Ray's zero-port and explicit-allocation policy in SkyRL. The regression tests cover two overlapping launchers, an occupied TCP port, normal release, and release after a killed launcher. The PR is stacked on #12313 until that branch merges.

Last observed decode spans reach 1,743.155 s (median 1,291.646 s), mostly from progress events rather than completed requests. These aggregates include three sessions outside a coarse timing check. Session reuse, Ray log suppression and unobserved pre-engine waits prevent a strict causal fraction for all 58 rows. comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

On [#11120](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11120), the total-turn timer starts when the first model request is sent, and the model-turn timer also covers engine queue time. vLLM already records QUEUED and SCHEDULED events with per-request queue wait, but that signal stays in engine logs; the model client returns only after generation. The outer attempt timer starts before harness execution, while the zero-token unavailable row appears to have both loss and baseline eligibility disabled; the latter still needs an end-to-end assertion.

**Relevant code**
- [`recorder.py#L222-L236`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6f431fe52c3f14b03f616d6f38330eb2403447e3/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/recorder.py#L222-L236) — total-turn deadline starts on send
- [`recorder.py#L358-L369`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6f431fe52c3f14b03f616d6f38330eb2403447e3/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/recorder.py#L358-L369) — model-turn deadline includes queue time
- [`engine.py#L162-L168`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6f431fe52c3f14b03f616d6f38330eb2403447e3/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/engine.py#L162-L168) — attempt deadline starts before harness
- [`request_timing.py#L35-L85`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6f431fe52c3f14b03f616d6f38330eb2403447e3/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inference_engines/request_timing.py#L35-L85) — scheduler events and queue-wait evidence
- [`task_projections.py#L199-L223`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6f431fe52c3f14b03f616d6f38330eb2403447e3/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_projections.py#L199-L223) — unavailable-row training disposition

# Proposed Fix

This spans the rollout engine, SkyRL inference transport, Harbor trial limits, and trainer evidence, so it belongs on #11120 or a coordinated follow-up after that branch lands. #11120 is open and currently conflicts with `main`; a separate implementation PR would duplicate its branch-only rollout engine.

1. Carry a request-ID-correlated SCHEDULED notification from the vLLM engine to the pending model call. Start total-turn and model-turn budgets on first engine scheduling, including long prefill and decode. Bound pre-scheduling wait with a separate queue-admission deadline, and preserve a separate setup watchdog. Align the outer attempt and Harbor trial clocks with that lifecycle so neither can cancel a queued first request.
2. Reuse the existing per-request QUEUED/SCHEDULED/first-token timing to emit queue wait and generation durations as separate rollout metrics. Propagate them into SkyRL's train/eval telemetry; include cancelled and never-scheduled requests in queue diagnostics.
3. Add a saturated-engine regression: hold all slots beyond the turn timeout, queue a short request, confirm it remains pending, then release a slot and confirm its deadline begins. Cover a request that never gets scheduled under the queue deadline. Add a trainer test for a zero-token unavailable row that checks zero loss mask, baseline exclusion, and zero advantage with the configured estimator; document the observed disposition.

Validate with the affected CPU tests and a bounded mixed-source replay, comparing its zero-token timeout count and score coverage against the issue's 58/500 train and 69/434 Micro210 baselines.

Across all 80 engine snapshots, the most requests running at once were 19 (`.129`) and 18 (`.131`), against a limit of 64. "Turn deadline expired before the first response" means no *completed* non-streaming response. The outer 1800 s deadline discarded unfinished generations.
- **Rates in the uniform 10% retained archives:** `.129` 212/1,786 = 11.87%; `.131` 194/2,083 = 9.31%. All of them are masked.
- **Fix, future runs only:** `0602a5bbdc` on `benfeuer/long-loop-prototype`. At 1770 s, inside the unchanged 1800 s turn deadline, active requests are returned through vLLM's partial-output abort. Real tokens, logprobs and routes are preserved, the actual verifier runs, and no further turn is allowed. Requests with no tokens stay unavailable. `.131` is unchanged.
- **Evidence:** the investigation report in #12267 (comment 7182161172), Echo incident wiki/1087, and `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/mochi-zero-token-timeouts/2026.11.26.1/investigation-record.json`.

The slot-ownership clock requirement remains as a guard. The measured queue share is small (seconds), but a trial's clock should still start only when it owns an engine slot.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 **Diagnostic correction:** the original blanket queue-starvation explanation is unsupported. An archived `generated_tokens=0` means no complete non-streaming `ModelTurn` reached the recorder; it does not mean vLLM generated no tokens. Cancelling a long active decode at the turn deadline can discard its exact partial response. The [recorder contract](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77f3e5f57ad298b72b0647bbce309e8af9ac85f1/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/recorder.py#L173) makes this distinction explicit.

- **Masking:** .129's 25 consumed batches contain **363/12,800 verifier-unavailable rows (2.84%)**. They were masked from token loss and excluded from the RLOO baseline, **not trained as reward 0**. The balanced 500-rollout sample's 58 timeout rows (11.6%) use a different denominator.
- **Engine join:** 29 of the 58 sampled session IDs have 44 retained timing events covering 32 request IDs, with **115–19,735 generated tokens**. Internal queue wait was at most **18.529 s**; first-token delay was at most **19.773 s**.
- **Decode time:** last observed first-token-to-last-token spans were **9.073–1,743.155 s**, median **1,291.646 s**. Thirty of the 32 final observations are progress events, so these are mostly **right-censored lower bounds**, not completed decode durations. The two retained ended events span 9.073 s and 1,602.944 s. Examples that pass the coarse timing check: session `19830_3` had 14,615 tokens after 1,743.155 s, and `11198_5` had 17,397 after 1,741.821 s.
- **Join limits:** those aggregates include all 29 session-ID matches; only 26 pass a coarse previous-optimizer-through-step+4 timing check. Session reuse and Ray log suppression prevent a strict per-invocation join. In particular, the short 9.073 s ended request belongs to a session outside that check.
- **Real queue-wait share:** no retained event shows a 1,800 s engine admission wait. This is **not a measured 0% for all 58 failures**: 29 sampled session IDs have no joined evidence, and internal vLLM timing excludes pre-engine waits. The total causal share is **unknown**. The user's slot-ownership-clock guard remains a separate Done-when requirement; the saturated-slot regression demonstrates the code gap, not that it caused this cohort.

[Partial-retention fix 0602a5bbdc](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/0602a5bbdc91d2f548d96b9f9ecb7404395b9261) uses vLLM's abort/output path to return exact sampled tokens, logprobs, routes and policy stamps, then invokes the real verifier under #10197; it synthesizes no EOS. Its 1,770 s cutoff, leaving 30 s inside the 1,800 s turn budget, is enabled in future authored Mochi RL recipes. [77f3e5f57a](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/77f3e5f57ad298b72b0647bbce309e8af9ac85f1) separately preserves execution budgets during admission. Neither changes an already submitted .129/.131 process.

**Shared adoption is now fixed for future jobs** by [36098e90e2](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/36098e90e2ea69f2beebfd3d76ba0c218cbb828e). The clock-aware task client requests the native partial abort before its nearest remaining trial/turn/agent deadline, including time spent in earlier turns, then awaits the original response collector. It needs no recipe-specific cutoff or frozen-protocol override. Caller cancellation remains cancellation; requests that generated no tokens remain unavailable. Both raw and chat paths retain exact token metadata. Clean-base regressions fail before the fix and pass afterward; CPU checks passed (58 related SkyRL and 260 rolloutengine tests). Broader checks have 12 independently reproduced baseline Harbor failures, not a broad-suite pass. No GPU certification is claimed.

The active exact-59 recovery remains pinned to 77f3 and has no 1,770 s engine cutoff; **the new shared partial-return fix is not active in that submitted job**. It continues unchanged, protecting all 375 prior grades.

There are also 12 retained same-request decode intervals; all show positive token progress, with interval-average rates **8.726–12.724 tokens/s**, median **10.271**. Long outputs at these rates explain how a short prompt can consume most of a 1,800 s turn budget. These sparse intervals do not exclude shorter stalls or identify whether kernel/expert-collective contention, weight synchronization or another load effect limits the rate. **Slow-decode attribution remains open.** [Interval evidence](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fmochi-zero-token-timeouts%2F2026.11.26.1%2Fdecode-intervals-evidence.json): `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/mochi-zero-token-timeouts/2026.11.26.1/decode-intervals-evidence.json`.

The title already matches “Turn-deadline expiry discards partial generations as zero-token rollouts”; the issue body has been corrected. [Retained evidence](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fmochi-zero-token-timeouts%2F2026.11.26.1%2Fdeadline-correction-evidence.json): `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/mochi-zero-token-timeouts/2026.11.26.1/deadline-correction-evidence.json`.

## Overview

This document is an attempt to formalize Marin’s policy towards what constitutes reportable, public-facing, canonical eval results for Marin models as well as the baselines we compare against.

Why do we need this document? With the first “snowball” release of a 67B A2B MoE, Marin is entering a regime where we regularly compare Marin models to existing open and closed-source models. Because Marin’s unique claim is that we are open development, we will need to hold ourselves to a high standard of transparency on how we report eval scores of Marin models and what claims we make about Marin model capabilities based on those scores.

What is in scope? This document is intended to act as a living snapshot, trustworthy for any given period in time, as to the what and the how of Marin’s canonical set of evals, a set of standards to which we will aspire to hold ourselves. By "the what", we mean “which evals did we run, with what consistent set of hyperparameters and experimental constraints”. By "the how", we mean “where is the self-contained codebase that is both necessary and sufficient to reproduce our eval results independently”.

## Previous version notes

* Released Sept 24, 2026: 18 non-agentic benchmarks, 8 Harbor agentic benchmarks, and 4 reserved out-of-distribution benchmarks.
